Which of the following best describes the purpose of the Trading Account in final accounts? Answer: To calculate gross profit or loss. The Trading Account is primarily used to determine the gross profit or loss before deducting administrative and selling expenses.

concepts.u: System of Government Accounting in Nepal
concepts.t: What is the term used to describe the system where financial transactions of the government are recorded, classified, and summarized? Answer: Government Accounting. Government Accounting refers to the systematic recording of all financial transactions conducted by the government.

concepts.u: System of Government Accounting in Nepal
concepts.t: In the context of Nepalese Government Accounting, what does the term 'Fund' refer to? Answer: A separate accounting entity with its own assets, liabilities, and budget. In Nepalese Government Accounting, a fund represents a separate accounting entity with its own set of financial resources and obligations.

In the context of government accounting, what does the term 'virement' refer to? Answer: Transfer of funds between different heads of accounts within the same department.. Virement refers to the internal reallocation of funds within a department's budget without changing the total amount appropriated.

According to the rules of government accounting, how is the payment of salaries categorized? Answer: Revenue expenditure. Salaries paid by the government fall under revenue expenditure as they are regular payments for services rendered.

In store accounting, what does the term 'stock-in-hand' refer to? Answer: The quantity of stock available at the end of an accounting period. Stock-in-hand represents the physical inventory count of items available at the end of an accounting period.

Which of the following best describes the purpose of a bin card in store accounting? Answer: To track the movement of specific stock items. A bin card is a document used to keep track of the movement of specific stock items in a warehouse.

What is the role of a perpetual inventory system in store accounting? Answer: It updates inventory records after every transaction. A perpetual inventory system automatically updates inventory records after every transaction involving the purchase or sale of inventory.

In fund accounting, which type of fund is typically used by a government to manage its general operating expenses? Answer: General Fund. The General Fund is used for managing general operating expenses and is not restricted for any specific purpose.

What does the retention account represent in financial statements? Answer: The cumulative earnings reinvested in the business. Retention account represents the earnings kept within the company that have not been distributed as dividends.

In the context of fund accounting, which statement best describes the purpose of a special revenue fund? Answer: To account for taxes and other revenues that are legally restricted to specific purposes. Special revenue funds are used to account for revenues that are legally restricted to specific purposes, ensuring these resources are used appropriately.

Which agency is primarily responsible for managing the budgetary allocations and expenditures of the government? Answer: Ministry of Finance. The Ministry of Finance is responsible for managing the budgetary allocations and expenditures of the government.

What role does the Comptroller General's Office play in government accounting? Answer: Overseeing the financial transactions and accounts of the government ministries and departments. The Comptroller General's Office oversees the financial transactions and accounts of the government ministries and departments.

In the context of government accounting, which body has the authority to approve the annual budget? Answer: Parliament. Parliament has the authority to approve the annual budget in the context of government accounting.

concepts.u: Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting
concepts.t: Which of the following software is primarily used for maintaining financial records in an accounting system? Answer: QuickBooks. QuickBooks is specifically designed for accounting tasks including financial record-keeping.

concepts.u: Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting
concepts.t: In computerized accounting systems, which function allows for the automatic adjustment of ledger accounts at the end of an accounting period? Answer: Automated Year-End Adjustments. Automated Year-End Adjustments help in adjusting ledger accounts without manual intervention.

concepts.u: Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting
concepts.t: What is the primary purpose of using barcode scanning technology in office and accounting operations? Answer: For quick inventory tracking and management. Barcode scanning technology enhances efficiency in inventory management by providing quick access to item information.

concepts.u: Use of Information Technology in Office and Accounting
concepts.t: Which of the following best describes the role of an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system in accounting? Answer: It integrates various business processes into a unified system.. ERP systems integrate different aspects of business operations, including accounting, to provide a comprehensive solution.
Which device forwards data between different networks using IP addresses? Answer: router. routers read IP addresses and choose a path.
Which device sends every signal it receives to all its ports? Answer: hub. a hub repeats to all ports; a switch sends to one.
Which of these is a private IPv4 address? Answer: 172.20.4.1. 172.16 to 172.31 is private; 172.40 is outside it.
Which command shows the IP address and default gateway of a Windows computer? Answer: ipconfig. ipconfig; ping only tests whether a host replies.
A company's portal that only its own staff can open is an Answer: intranet. staff-only means intranet; outsiders with access make it an extranet.
A student's plan is 50 Mbps but a speed test reads 38 Mbps. The 38 Mbps is the Answer: throughput. the measured rate is throughput; 50 Mbps is the bandwidth.
A walkie-talkie works in Answer: half-duplex mode. both sides talk, but only one at a time.
Which medium carries data as pulses of light? Answer: optical fibre. fibre carries light; the others carry electrical signals.
Which device sends a frame only to the port of the destination computer? Answer: switch. a switch reads the MAC address; a hub copies to every port.
A foreign key Answer: refers to the primary key of another table. it links to another table's primary key and may repeat.
Which of these is a DDL command? Answer: ALTER. ALTER changes structure; the others are DML.
Which command removes a table together with its structure? Answer: DROP. DROP removes structure and data; TRUNCATE keeps the structure.
A field that uniquely identifies each record and can never be NULL is a Answer: primary key. unique and not NULL is the primary-key rule.
In a table marks(roll, subject, marks), the key (roll, subject) is a Answer: composite key. two fields together form a composite key.
The pitch of a sound depends on its Answer: frequency. frequency sets pitch; amplitude sets loudness.
One second of mono, 8-bit sound sampled at 8,000 Hz needs Answer: 8,000 bytes. 8,000 × 8 × 1 × 1 = 64,000 bits = 8,000 bytes.
Which program is used to cut, arrange and export video clips on a timeline? Answer: CapCut. CapCut is a video editor; Audacity edits sound.
Which one is NOT an element of multimedia? Answer: compiler. a compiler translates programs; it is not a medium.
Which format is lossless and supports a transparent background? Answer: PNG. PNG is lossless with transparency; JPG has no transparency.
What does print(7 // 2 + 7 % 2) display? Answer: 4. 7 // 2 = 3 and 7 % 2 = 1, so 4 (tested).
random.randint(1, 3) can never return Answer: 4. randint stays between 1 and 3 inclusive.
int("abc") raises Answer: ValueError. the type is right (str) but the content is not a number.
A large language model writes an answer by Answer: predicting the next token again and again. next-token prediction, one token at a time.
An AI image generator usually begins with Answer: random noise. diffusion models remove noise step by step.
Training an AI on data from only one group of people mainly causes Answer: bias. the AI copies the imbalance in its data.
The part of a robot that moves its wheels or arms is the Answer: actuator. motors are actuators; sensors only measure.
An AI chatbot confidently gives a false date. This limitation is called Answer: hallucination. false but fluent output is hallucination.
Which is the best way to reduce bias in an AI system? Answer: train it on diverse, representative data. balanced data lets the AI treat all groups fairly.

Which law states that as more units of a variable input are added to fixed inputs, the marginal product will eventually decrease? Answer: Law of Diminishing Returns. The Law of Diminishing Returns explains the decrease in marginal product as more units of a variable input are added to fixed inputs.
What is the term for the additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of a good? Answer: Marginal Cost. Marginal cost refers to the cost of producing one additional unit of output.

In microeconomics, what does the term 'market equilibrium' refer to? Answer: A state where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded. Market equilibrium occurs when the quantity supplied matches the quantity demanded at a certain price.

Which of the following best defines 'elasticity of demand' in economics? Answer: The responsiveness of the quantity demanded to changes in price. Elasticity of demand measures how much the quantity demanded responds to a change in price.

What does GDP stand for in macroeconomics? Answer: Gross Domestic Product. GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, which is the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

Which of the following is considered an automatic stabilizer in macroeconomic policy? Answer: Unemployment insurance payments. Unemployment insurance payments are an example of an automatic stabilizer as they increase during economic downturns without requiring new legislation.

If the government decides to decrease taxes, how is this likely to affect the aggregate demand in the economy? Answer: It will increase. Decreasing taxes increases disposable income, leading to higher consumer spending and thus increasing aggregate demand.

What does the Human Development Index (HDI) primarily measure? Answer: The overall development of a country based on health, education, and income levels. HDI combines indicators of life expectancy, education, and income into a single statistic to measure a country's overall development.

Which of the following is an indicator of economic growth? Answer: Increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) over time. An increase in GDP over time indicates economic growth as it reflects an expansion in the economy's production capacity.

Sustainable development focuses on which of the following principles? Answer: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own needs. Sustainable development aims to balance economic growth with environmental protection to ensure long-term viability.

Poverty line is defined as the level of income that allows a person to afford basic necessities such as food, shelter, and clothing. If a family's total monthly expenditure on these items is $3000$, what is the approximate poverty line per capita if the family has 5 members? Answer: $600$. To find the poverty line per capita, divide the total monthly expenditure by the number of family members, resulting in $3000 / 5 = 600$.

What does the term 'GNP' stand for in the context of Nepal's economy? Answer: Gross National Product. GNP stands for Gross National Product, which measures the total value of goods and services produced by the nationals of a country.

Which law explains the relationship between price and quantity demanded, stating that as price increases, quantity demanded decreases? Answer: Law of Demand. The Law of Demand describes how demand for a good or service decreases as its price increases, assuming all other factors remain constant.

What is the term used to describe the situation where the production cost exceeds the revenue generated in Nepal's economy? Answer: Loss. In economics, when the production cost exceeds revenue, it is termed as a 'loss'.

Which of the following best defines 'capital formation' in the context of Nepal’s economic growth? Answer: Saving and investment in capital goods. Capital formation refers to the accumulation of new physical assets or capital goods within an economy, primarily through savings and investments.

Which law states that the marginal utility derived from a good decreases as its consumption increases? Answer: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility. The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility directly addresses the decreasing satisfaction from additional units of a good.

In time series analysis, what does the term 'seasonal variation' refer to? Answer: Regular patterns occurring at specific intervals within a year. Seasonal variation involves regular patterns recurring at predictable times within a fixed period.

What is the formula used to calculate the Price Elasticity of Demand? Answer: $\frac{\Delta Q / Q}{\Delta P / P}$. Price Elasticity of Demand measures the percentage change in quantity demanded due to a percentage change in price.

Which index number method gives equal importance to both base and current period quantities? Answer: Fisher's Ideal Index. Fisher's Ideal Index is the geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche indices, balancing both periods.
The charity that wrote the letter asked that children under 18 be included in Answer: the UN Youth Advisory Group on climate change. the letter asks for children's voices on climate policy.
At higher altitude, water boils at a Answer: lower temperature. pressure is lower, so less heat is needed.
The Nepali chef interviewed in the unit is Answer: Santosh Shah. Santosh Shah (MasterChef: The Professionals, 2020, BBC One).
In the myth, Pelops won Hippodamia by Answer: a chariot race. the king's chariot wheel pins were replaced by wax.
Driverless technology is being used most widely at present in Answer: the USA. the text says it is "slowly expanding across the US".
One effect of driverless cars on the environment is that they Answer: reduce carbon emissions. the article lists "lowering carbon emissions".
According to David Hynd, a driverless car must be able to cope with Answer: human drivers who break rules. Hynd: it "has got to be able to cope with human drivers speeding… or breaking the rules".
The article says the technology developed so far is Answer: partly trustworthy. much still has to be done before it becomes mainstream.
A factory price of Rs 1000 carries 10% excise duty and then 13% VAT. The final price is Answer: Rs 1,243. $1000\times1.10\times1.13=1243$; VAT applies to price plus excise.
A tax charged by the government on goods produced in the country, on the factory price, is called Answer: excise duty. excise duty is charged on factory price.
Rs 4000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year amounts to Answer: Rs 4,410. rate per half-year 5%, two periods: $4000(1.05)^2=4410$.
In half-yearly compounding the rate used per period is Answer: $\frac{R}{2}$. the annual rate is halved and the periods doubled.
For 1 year, the simple interest and the compound interest (yearly) on the same sum at the same rate are Answer: equal. for one period the interest is on the same principal.
A sum becomes four times itself in 2 years at compound interest. The rate is Answer: 100%. $(1+\frac{R}{100})^2=4$, so $1+\frac{R}{100}=2$, $R=100$.

The population of a city was 50,000 in 2020 and increases at an annual rate of 2%. What will be the population in 2025? Answer: $55127$. Using the formula $P = P_0(1 + r)^t$, where $P_0 = 50000$, $r = 0.02$, and $t = 5$, the population in 2025 is approximately 55127.
The area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is Answer: 84 cm². $s=21$; $\sqrt{21\times8\times7\times6}=\sqrt{7056}=84$.
A ring has outer radius 14 cm and inner radius 7 cm. Its area is Answer: 462 cm². $\frac{22}{7}(196-49)=\frac{22}{7}\times147=462$.
A path 1 m wide runs around the outside of a 20 m × 15 m garden. The area of the path is Answer: 74 m². outer $22\times17=374$; inner $20\times15=300$; $374-300=74$.
The number of 20 cm × 20 cm tiles needed for a 6 m × 4 m floor is Answer: 600. area 24 m² over 0.04 m² per tile gives 600.
The area of a quadrant (90° sector) of radius 14 cm is Answer: 154 cm². $\frac14\times\frac{22}{7}\times196=154$.

If the area of a rectangle is $56 \, ext{cm}^2$ and its length is $8 \, ext{cm}$, what is the width of the rectangle? Answer: $7 \, ext{cm}$. The width is calculated by dividing the area by the length, which equals $7 \, ext{cm}$.
Which of the following represents the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side length $a$? Answer: $3a$. The perimeter of an equilateral triangle is three times the side length.
The curved surface area of a cylinder with $r=7$ cm and $h=10$ cm is Answer: 440 cm². $2\times\frac{22}{7}\times7\times10=440$.
The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm is Answer: 462 cm². $3\pi r^2=3\times\frac{22}{7}\times49=462$.
The volume of a sphere of radius 10.5 cm is Answer: 4851 cm³. $\frac43\times\frac{22}{7}\times(10.5)^3=4851$.
A cylindrical tank has radius 0.7 m and height 2 m. Its capacity is Answer: 3080 litres. $\frac{22}{7}\times0.49\times2=3.08$ m³ $=3080$ litres.
If the radius of a sphere is doubled, its surface area becomes Answer: 4 times. surface area $\propto r^2$, so $2^2=4$ times.
The total surface area of the prism in item 2 is Answer: 132 cm². base area $\frac12\times3\times4=6$, so $120+2(6)=132$.

concepts.u: Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple
concepts.t: If one expression is $(x+2)(x-3)$, the HCF is $x+2$ and the LCM is $(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)$, the other expression is Answer: $(x+2)(x+1)$. other $=\frac{\text{HCF}\times\text{LCM}}{\text{given}}=\frac{(x+2)\cdot(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)}{(x+2)(x-3)}=(x+2)(x+1)$.
If $x=2+\sqrt{3}$, then $x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}$ equals Answer: 14. $x+\frac1x=4$, so $x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}=16-2=14$.
The length of a rectangle is 3 m more than its breadth and its area is 40 m². The breadth is Answer: 5 m. $b(b+3)=40\Rightarrow(b+8)(b-5)=0$; reject $b=-8$.
A median divides a triangle of area 36 cm² into two triangles each of area Answer: 18 cm². a median bisects the area: $36\div2=18$.
Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are Answer: equal in area. equal in area, though not necessarily congruent.

The theorem used to construct a triangle equal in area to a given quadrilateral is Answer: triangles on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area. shifting the vertex along a parallel keeps the area.

A rectangle equal in area to a triangle of base 8 cm and height 6 cm has the same base and a height of Answer: 3 cm. triangle area 24 cm²; with base 8 cm the rectangle height is $24\div8=3$ cm, half the triangle's height.
To draw a line through a point parallel to a given line, you use Answer: equal alternate angles. copy an angle so the alternate angles are equal.
In the steps of construction, the compass arcs Answer: should be left visible. examiners credit visible construction arcs.
An arc subtends 40° at the circumference. The angle at the centre is Answer: 80°. the centre angle is twice: $2\times40=80$.
If $\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}$ and $\theta$ is acute, then $\cos\theta$ is Answer: $\frac{12}{13}$. hypotenuse 13, opposite 5, adjacent $\sqrt{169-25}=12$.
$\sin25^\circ$ equals Answer: $\cos65^\circ$. complementary angles: $\sin\theta=\cos(90^\circ-\theta)$.
The standard deviation of 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 is Answer: 2. mean 5, squared deviations sum to 32, variance $\frac{32}{8}=4$, SD $=2$.

What is the formula for calculating the mean of grouped data? Answer: $\frac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i}$. The mean of grouped data is calculated by summing the product of frequency and class mark divided by the total frequency.
Which measure of central tendency is least affected by extreme values? Answer: Median. The median is less affected by extreme values as it represents the middle value in an ordered list.

In a frequency distribution, what does the term 'frequency density' refer to? Answer: Frequency per unit class width. Frequency density is defined as the frequency per unit class width in a histogram.
If a die is rolled once, what is the probability of getting an even number? Answer: $\frac{1}{2}$. There are three even numbers out of six possible outcomes.

Two coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability that both coins show heads? Answer: $\frac{1}{4}$. Each coin has two outcomes and there is only one favorable outcome among four total outcomes.

A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of drawing a queen or a king? Answer: $\frac{2}{13}$. There are 4 queens and 4 kings in a deck, making 8 favorable outcomes out of 52.
What is the value of $\left(2^3\right)^2$? Answer: $2^6$. Using the power rule $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$, we find $\left(2^3\right)^2 = 2^{3*2} = 2^6$.
Simplify $\frac{5^7}{5^3}$. Answer: $5^4$. Applying the quotient rule of indices $a^m/a^n = a^{m-n}$, we get $\frac{5^7}{5^3} = 5^{7-3} = 5^4$.
Evaluate $\left(4^{-2}\right)\left(4^5\right)$. Answer: $4^3$. By applying the product rule of indices $a^m * a^n = a^{m+n}$, we have $\left(4^{-2}\right)\left(4^5\right) = 4^{-2+5} = 4^3$.
If $x = 2$ and $y = 3$, what is the value of $x^2 + y^2$? Answer: 13. The value is calculated as $2^2 + 3^2 = 4 + 9 = 13$.
What is the area of a circle with radius $r = 7$ cm? (Use $\pi = rac{22}{7}$) Answer: 154 cm$^2$. Area is calculated as $\pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} \cdot 7^2 = 154$ cm$^2$.
What is the volume of a cube with side length $a = 4$ cm? Answer: 64 cm$^3$. Volume is calculated as $a^3 = 4^3 = 64$ cm$^3$.
The sum of the first 10 odd numbers is Answer: 100. the sum of the first $n$ odd numbers is $n^2=100$.
If the roots of $x^2+kx+9=0$ are equal, then $k$ is Answer: 6. equal roots need $k^2=4\times9=36$, so $k=\pm6$; of the options, 6.
If one root of $x^2-7x+c=0$ is 2, then $c$ is Answer: 10. $2$ is a root, so $4-14+c=0$ and $c=10$.
The graph of $y=-x^3$ passes through the Answer: 2nd and 4th quadrants. $a<0$, so the curve passes through quadrants 2 and 4.
The determinant of the identity matrix of order 3 is Answer: 1. every identity matrix has determinant 1.

Which of the following represents the identity matrix of size 3? Answer: \( \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \). An identity matrix has 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

concepts.u: Trigonometry: Multiple, Submultiple and Transformation Formu
concepts.t: If $\sin A=\frac{3}{5}$ and $A$ is acute, then $\sin2A$ is Answer: $\frac{24}{25}$. $\cos A=\frac{4}{5}$, so $\sin2A=2\times\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{4}{5}=\frac{24}{25}$.

concepts.u: Trigonometry: Multiple, Submultiple and Transformation Formu
concepts.t: $\sin40°+\sin20°$ equals Answer: $2\sin30°\cos10°$. $2\sin30°\cos10°$, which is about 0.98, the value of $\sin40°+\sin20°$.

concepts.u: Trigonometry: Multiple, Submultiple and Transformation Formu
concepts.t: The value of $\frac{\sin2A}{1+\cos2A}$ is Answer: $\tan A$. $\frac{2\sin A\cos A}{2\cos^2A}=\tan A$.

concepts.u: Trigonometry: Multiple, Submultiple and Transformation Formu
concepts.t: Which of these is not equal to $\cos2A$? Answer: $2\sin^2A-1$. $1-2\sin^2A$ is the correct form; $2\sin^2A-1=-\cos2A$.

concepts.u: Conditional Identities, Trigonometric Equations and Height a
concepts.t: A pole 10 m high casts a shadow 10 m long. The elevation of the sun is Answer: $45°$. $\tan\theta=\frac{10}{10}=1$, so the elevation is $45°$.

concepts.u: Conditional Identities, Trigonometric Equations and Height a
concepts.t: The angle of depression is measured Answer: downward from the horizontal. the depression is the angle below the horizontal.

concepts.u: Conditional Identities, Trigonometric Equations and Height a
concepts.t: If $\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\theta$ is acute, then $\theta$ is Answer: $60°$. $\cos60°=\frac{1}{2}$; $120°$ has the same cosine but is obtuse.

concepts.u: Conditional Identities, Trigonometric Equations and Height a
concepts.t: Given that $\tan(\alpha) = \sqrt{3}$, find $\alpha$ when it lies between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. Answer: $60^\circ$. Knowing the value of tangent for common angles, $\tan(60^\circ) = \sqrt{3}$.

concepts.u: Angle between Two Lines and Pair of Straight
concepts.t: The angle between the lines $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt{3}x$ is Answer: $15°$. slopes 1 and $\sqrt{3}$, so $\tan\theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{1+\sqrt{3}}=2-\sqrt{3}\approx0.268$, and $\tan15°=2-\sqrt{3}$, so $\theta=15°$.

concepts.u: Angle between Two Lines and Pair of Straight
concepts.t: The equation $x^2-y^2=0$ represents Answer: a pair of perpendicular lines. $x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)=0$ gives the lines $y=x$ and $y=-x$.

concepts.u: Angle between Two Lines and Pair of Straight
concepts.t: The equation $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$ represents two perpendicular lines if Answer: $a+b=0$. $a+b=0$ makes the denominator of the angle formula zero.

concepts.u: Angle between Two Lines and Pair of Straight
concepts.t: The lines given by $4x^2+12xy+9y^2=0$ are Answer: coincident. $4x^2+12xy+9y^2=(2x+3y)^2$; also $h=6$, $h^2=36=ab$.
The conic with eccentricity greater than 1 is Answer: hyperbola. an eccentricity greater than 1 gives a hyperbola.
The circle $x^2+y^2-8x-8y+16=0$ touches Answer: both axes. centre $(4,4)$ and $r=\sqrt{16+16-16}=4$, so the distance to each axis equals the radius.
What is the eccentricity of a circle? Answer: $0$. The eccentricity of a circle is always zero.
The midpoint of the line joining $(2,6)$ and $(8,2)$ is Answer: $(5,4)$. $\left(\frac{2+8}{2},\frac{6+2}{2}\right)=(5,4)$.
In linear programming the objective function is Answer: the quantity to be maximised or minimised. the objective is what the problem asks you to maximise or minimise.
The maximum of a linear objective over a feasible region is attained Answer: at a corner point. a linear function on a convex polygon peaks at a vertex.
In an inversion transformation with radius $k$, the product $OP\cdot OP'$ equals Answer: $k^2$. that product is the defining property, $OP\cdot OP'=k^2$.
The region satisfying $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$ and $x+y\leq4$ is Answer: a triangle. the three lines close a right triangle with corners $(0,0)$, $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$.
The maximum of $z=x+y$ subject to $x\geq0$, $y\geq0$, $x+y\leq4$ is Answer: 4. $z$ is largest at $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$, where $z=4$.
A point on the inversion circle is Answer: moved onto itself. a point at distance $k$ from the centre satisfies $OP\cdot OP'=k^2$ with $OP'=k$, so it is its own image.

In a linear programming problem, if the feasible region is unbounded, which of the following statements is true regarding the objective function $z = ax + by$? Answer: If the objective function line can be shifted indefinitely outward while staying within the feasible region, then there is an unbounded solution.. When the feasible region is unbounded and the objective function line can be shifted indefinitely outward, it indicates that the solution is unbounded.

Consider the system of inequalities that defines a feasible region in a linear programming problem. Which of the following is not a requirement for a point to be considered part of the feasible region? Answer: The point must maximize the objective function.. While maximizing the objective function is important, not every point in the feasible region needs to maximize the objective function; only the optimal solution does.
If $\lim_{x\to a^-}f(x)=3$ and $\lim_{x\to a^+}f(x)=5$, then at $a$ the function has Answer: a jump discontinuity. the one-sided limits differ, which is a jump.
The standard deviation of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is Answer: $\sqrt{8}$. deviations are $-4,-2,0,2,4$; $\frac{16+4+0+4+16}{5}=8$, so $\sigma=\sqrt{8}\approx2.83$.
If every observation is increased by 5, the standard deviation Answer: is unchanged. adding a constant moves every point but not the spread.
The coefficient of variation is a measure of Answer: relative dispersion. it expresses the spread as a percentage of the mean.
If the standard deviation of a dataset is 5, what would be the variance of the dataset? Answer: 25. The variance is the square of the standard deviation.
Which measure of dispersion is affected by extreme values? Answer: Range. Range is calculated as the difference between the maximum and minimum values, making it sensitive to outliers.

What does a smaller interquartile range (IQR) indicate about a dataset? Answer: Less variability within the middle 50% of data. A smaller IQR indicates that the middle 50% of the data points are closely clustered together.
A graph represents a function when no vertical line meets it Answer: more than once. one crossing at most is the definition the test checks.
The function $f(x)=x^2$ on all real numbers is Answer: not one-to-one. $f(2)=f(-2)=4$, so two inputs share an output.

The correct order of the scientific method after observing a problem is Answer: hypothesis, experiment, conclusion. a hypothesis is stated, then tested by an experiment, then judged in the conclusion.
A tentative, testable explanation of an observation is called a Answer: hypothesis. a hypothesis is a testable guess; a theory is already well tested.
The SI unit of mass is the Answer: kilogram. the kilogram is the SI base unit of mass; the gram is a sub-unit.
The variable that the experimenter deliberately changes is the Answer: independent variable. the independent variable is the one the experimenter changes.
Which instrument measures the volume of an irregular solid by displacement? Answer: measuring cylinder. a measuring cylinder shows the water level before and after immersion.
A project report should end with Answer: the conclusion and recommendations. a report closes with findings, conclusion and recommendations.
Which one is the correct order of the first three steps of the scientific method? Answer: problem, observation, hypothesis. we first state the problem, then observe, then form a hypothesis.
The SI unit of temperature is Answer: kelvin. the kelvin is the SI unit of temperature.
The variable that a scientist keeps the same in a fair test is called the Answer: controlled variable. controlled variables are kept constant so that the test is fair.
Technology is best described as Answer: application of scientific knowledge. technology uses knowledge to make useful things.
Which kingdom contains organisms without a true nucleus? Answer: Monera. Monera are prokaryotes: no nuclear membrane.
The cell wall of fungi is made of Answer: chitin. chitin is the fungal wall material; cellulose belongs to plants.
In the name Homo sapiens, sapiens is the Answer: species. the first word is the genus (Homo), the second the species.
Amoeba belongs to the kingdom Answer: Protista. Amoeba is a single-celled eukaryote, so it is a protist.
Which pair is correctly matched? Answer: yeast, Fungi. yeast is a unicellular fungus; a mushroom is a fungus, bacteria are Monera and ferns are plants.
An organism that makes its own food and has a cell wall of cellulose is placed in Answer: Plantae. plants are autotrophs with cellulose cell walls.
Who is called the father of taxonomy? Answer: Linnaeus. Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature and the ranks.
Which kingdom includes Paramecium? Answer: Protista. Paramecium is a ciliated unicellular eukaryote.
The only egg-laying female of a bee colony is the Answer: queen. workers are sterile females; the queen lays all eggs.
Which species is domesticated and native to Nepal? Answer: Apis cerana. Apis cerana is native and kept in hives; A. dorsata and A. florea are wild.
The main duty of the drone is to Answer: mate with the queen. a drone mates with a virgin queen and dies afterwards.
The sac in which the queen stores sperm is the Answer: spermatheca. the spermatheca keeps sperm alive for her whole life.
The correct order of the bee life cycle is Answer: egg, larva, pupa, adult. complete metamorphosis: egg, larva, pupa, adult.
Which honey bee species is domesticated in Nepal? Answer: Apis cerana. Apis cerana (and A. mellifera, introduced) are kept in hives.
Drones develop from Answer: unfertilised eggs. drones are haploid, from unfertilised eggs.
The device that stops the queen entering the honey chamber is the Answer: queen excluder. the queen is too large to pass the excluder.
The shape of the cells in a honey comb is Answer: hexagonal. hexagons need the least wax and leave no gaps.
Which part of the honeybee body is used to make wax for constructing honeycombs? Answer: Glands in the abdomen. Special glands in the abdomen of worker bees produce wax for constructing honeycombs.

Honeybees communicate the location of food sources through a dance. What is this dance called? Answer: Waggle dance. The waggle dance is used by honeybees to communicate the direction and distance of food sources.

Which type of bee in the hive has a barbed stinger that tears away when used? Answer: Worker bee. Worker bees have a barbed stinger that typically tears away from their body after stinging, leading to their death.
The father of genetics is Answer: Mendel. Gregor Mendel, from his pea experiments.
The sex of a child is decided by the chromosome contributed by the Answer: father. the mother gives only X; the father gives X or Y.
Colour blindness is more common in males because the gene is Answer: recessive and on the X chromosome. a male has one X, so a single recessive gene shows; a female needs two.

Which law states that during the formation of gametes, pairs of hereditary factors separate so that offspring inherit one factor from each parent? Answer: Law of Segregation. The Law of Segregation, proposed by Mendel, describes how alleles of a gene segregate randomly into reproductive cells.

What is the name given to an organism that possesses two different alleles of a gene, one dominant and one recessive? Answer: Heterozygous. Heterozygous organisms have two different alleles for a particular gene.
The functional unit of the nervous system is the Answer: neuron. a neuron carries nerve impulses; the nephron belongs to the kidney.
The hormone that lowers the blood sugar level is Answer: insulin. insulin from the pancreas; glucagon raises sugar.
The chamber of the heart that pumps oxygenated blood to the body is the Answer: left ventricle. the left ventricle drives blood through the aorta to the body.
A reflex action is controlled by the Answer: spinal cord. the reflex arc passes through the spinal cord, bypassing thinking.
The functional unit of the kidney is the Answer: nephron. each kidney has about a million nephrons.
The universal blood donor group is Answer: O. group O red cells carry no A or B antigens.
Fertilisation in humans normally takes place in the Answer: fallopian tube. the ovum meets the sperm in the fallopian tube, then travels to the uterus.
The part of the brain that controls balance of the body is the Answer: cerebellum. the cerebellum controls balance and posture.
The hormone that lowers blood sugar is Answer: insulin. insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
Fertilisation in human beings takes place in the Answer: fallopian tube. the egg is fertilised in the fallopian tube.
The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the Answer: pulmonary vein. the pulmonary vein is the one vein with oxygenated blood.
The gas mainly responsible for global warming is Answer: carbon dioxide. CO₂ is the most abundant added greenhouse gas.
The ozone layer is mainly damaged by Answer: CFCs. chlorine released from CFCs breaks down ozone.
Which is a biodegradable waste? Answer: vegetable peel. vegetable waste decays by microbes; the others do not.
The gas mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect is Answer: carbon dioxide. CO₂ is the main greenhouse gas from human activity.
According to the 10% law, if the producers store 5,000 kJ, the energy at the secondary consumer level is Answer: 50 kJ. 5,000 × 10% = 500 kJ (primary), then 10% = 50 kJ (secondary).
The value of $g$ at the centre of the Earth is Answer: zero. attractions from all sides cancel at the centre.
If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force becomes Answer: one quarter. $F \propto 1/d^2$, so $F$ becomes $\tfrac14$.
What is the term used to describe the rate of change of velocity with respect to time? Answer: Acceleration. Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity over time.

According to Newton's second law of motion, what is the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration expressed by the formula $F = ma$? Answer: Force is directly proportional to both mass and acceleration.. Newton's second law states that force equals mass times acceleration, indicating direct proportionality to both mass and acceleration.
Which statement correctly defines inertia? Answer: The ability of an object to resist changes to its state of motion.. Inertia is the property of matter that resists any change in its motion.

If two objects collide and there are no external forces acting on them, which law does this scenario best illustrate? Answer: Conservation of Momentum. In the absence of external forces, the total momentum before and after collision remains constant, illustrating the conservation of momentum.
The hydraulic press works on the principle of Answer: Pascal. Pascal's law transmits pressure through the confined oil.
An iron nail sinks but a huge iron ship floats because the ship Answer: displaces water weighing as much as the ship. the floating ship's weight equals the weight of water it displaces.
A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because the sharp edge has Answer: less area, so more pressure. for the same force, smaller area gives larger pressure.
The pressure in a liquid at a given depth depends on Answer: the density of the liquid. $P = h\rho g$; shape and area do not matter.
Hydraulic brakes work on Answer: Pascal's law. pressure on the brake fluid is transmitted equally to all wheels.
A body floats in a liquid when Answer: its density is less than the liquid. a body with lower density than the liquid floats.
Heat reaches us from the Sun mainly by Answer: radiation. radiation travels through the vacuum of space.
Water has its maximum density at Answer: 4 °C. anomalous expansion: water is densest at 4 °C.
Sea breeze blows from the sea to land during the day because Answer: land heats up faster than water. warm air rises over land and cooler sea air flows in; land has a lower specific heat.
During melting of ice at 0 °C, the temperature of the ice-water mixture Answer: remains constant. heat goes into latent heat, not into raising temperature.
Which of the following materials would have the highest thermal conductivity? Answer: Copper. Metals like copper are generally excellent conductors of heat compared to non-metals and insulators.

If the heat transfer coefficient (h) increases, what happens to the rate of heat transfer through convection? Answer: Increases. The rate of heat transfer through convection is directly proportional to the heat transfer coefficient.
Sound cannot travel through Answer: vacuum. sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium.
Short-sightedness (myopia) is corrected by a Answer: concave lens. a concave lens diverges rays so the image falls on the retina.
The bending of light as it passes from air to glass is called Answer: refraction. refraction is bending due to a change of speed.
White light splits into seven colours in a prism because Answer: every colour has a different speed in glass. dispersion: each colour has a different refractive index in glass.
Sound waves in air are Answer: longitudinal. air particles vibrate along the direction of the wave.
The speed of light in a medium of refractive index 2 is Answer: $1.5\times10^8$ m s⁻¹. $v = c/n = 3\times10^8/2 = 1.5\times10^8$ m s⁻¹.
A short-sighted person should use Answer: a concave lens. a concave lens moves the image back onto the retina.
A generator works on the principle of Answer: electromagnetic induction. a coil turning in a magnetic field has an induced emf.
The direction of force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is found by Answer: Fleming's left-hand rule. Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force.
Which rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field? Answer: Fleming's left-hand rule. thumb force, forefinger field, middle finger current.
A transformer works on Answer: AC only. only a changing current gives a changing flux.

In an AC generator, the output current reverses direction because of Answer: the rotation of the coil. as the coil rotates, each side alternately moves up and down through the field, reversing the induced current every half turn.

If the current flowing through a conductor is doubled, what happens to the magnetic field produced by the conductor? Answer: It doubles. The strength of the magnetic field is directly proportional to the current.
Which of the following materials is NOT a good conductor of electricity? Answer: Rubber. Rubber is an insulator, not a conductor.
What is the SI unit of electric charge? Answer: Coulomb. Electric charge is measured in Coulombs.

According to Ohm's law, if the resistance in a circuit is halved while the voltage remains constant, the current will: Answer: Increase by two times. Current is inversely proportional to resistance when voltage is constant.
A light year is a unit of Answer: distance. a light year is the distance light travels in a year.
Energy in the core of the Sun is released by Answer: nuclear fusion. hydrogen nuclei fuse to helium in the core.
A man-made body orbiting the Earth is called Answer: an artificial satellite. satellites are artificial; the Moon is natural.
A light year is a unit of Answer: distance. it is the distance light travels in a year.
The most accepted theory of the origin of the universe is the Answer: Big Bang theory. supported by red shift and the microwave background.
The star at the end of a Sun-like star's life is a Answer: white dwarf. a Sun-like star sheds its outer layers and leaves a white dwarf.
A geostationary satellite has a period of Answer: 24 hours. it matches the Earth's rotation, so it stays above one spot.
The full form of URL is Answer: Uniform Resource Locator. Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a web page.
Sending false messages to steal a person's bank details is Answer: phishing. phishing tricks users into giving private information.
Which is an output device? Answer: printer. a printer outputs information; the others are input devices.
The worldwide network of connected computers is the Answer: internet. the internet connects networks worldwide; a LAN is local.
Which of the following is an output device? Answer: monitor. a monitor displays results; the others are input devices.
A network that covers a school building is a Answer: LAN. a local area network covers a small area such as a building.
A fake e-mail used to steal bank details is called Answer: phishing. phishing tricks users into giving private information.

Which law states that the number of transistors on a microchip doubles about every two years, though the cost of computers is halved? Answer: Moore's Law. Moore's Law predicts the trend in the number of transistors on integrated circuits.
The modern periodic law states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their Answer: atomic number. Moseley's work led to atomic number as the basis.
An element with electronic configuration 2, 8, 7 is in Answer: group 17, period 3. three shells give period 3; seven valence electrons give group 17.
Which group contains the noble gases? Answer: group 18. helium, neon, argon and the rest are in group 18.
Which element is an alkali metal? Answer: sodium. sodium is in group 1; calcium is group 2.
Atoms of elements in the same group have the same Answer: number of valence electrons. the same valence electrons give similar properties.
The modern periodic law is based on Answer: atomic number. Moseley showed atomic number is the basis.
Which change speeds up a reaction? Answer: increasing surface area. more surface area gives more collisions.
In Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, zinc Answer: displaces copper. zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it.

Which law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure? Answer: Boyle's Law. Boyle's Law describes the inverse relationship between pressure and volume of a gas at constant temperature.

What is the term used to describe a reaction where two or more substances combine to form a single new substance? Answer: Synthesis reaction. A synthesis reaction involves the combination of two or more substances to form a new compound.

According to the law of conservation of mass, what happens during a chemical reaction? Answer: Mass is conserved.. The law of conservation of mass states that mass cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.

What type of reaction occurs when a substance reacts with oxygen to release heat energy? Answer: Combustion reaction. A combustion reaction involves the reaction of a substance with oxygen, often releasing heat and light.
In the laboratory, hydrogen is prepared from Answer: zinc and dilute H₂SO₄. zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute acid; copper does not.
MnO₂ in the preparation of oxygen from KClO₃ acts as a Answer: catalyst. MnO₂ speeds the decomposition and is unchanged.
The gas used in fire extinguishers is Answer: carbon dioxide. CO₂ does not support burning and is heavier than air.
In the preparation of oxygen from KClO₃, MnO₂ acts as Answer: a catalyst. it speeds up the reaction and is unchanged.
Brass is an alloy of Answer: copper and zinc. brass is copper and zinc; bronze is copper and tin.
Which metal does NOT displace hydrogen from dilute acids? Answer: copper. copper lies below hydrogen in the series.
Which non-metal is a good conductor of electricity? Answer: graphite. graphite has free electrons between its layers.
The molecular formula of propane is Answer: C₃H₈. $n=3$: $\text{C}_3\text{H}_{2(3)+2}=\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$.
The formula of ethyne is Answer: C₂H₂. a triple bond: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_{2(2)-2}=\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$.
Ethanol reacts with acetic acid to form Answer: an ester. esterification gives ethyl ethanoate and water.
Soap is made by heating oil or fat with Answer: sodium hydroxide. fat plus NaOH gives soap and glycerol (saponification).
The raw materials of glass include Answer: silica, soda ash and limestone. sand, soda ash and limestone are melted together.
Polythene is a polymer of Answer: ethene. polythene is made from many ethene molecules.
Soap forms scum in hard water, whereas detergent Answer: does not form scum. detergent calcium and magnesium salts remain soluble.
A plastic that softens on heating and can be remoulded is Answer: thermoplastic. thermoplastics can be reshaped; bakelite is thermosetting.
Detergents are better than soap in Answer: hard water. detergents do not form scum with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺.
What is the boiling point of water at sea level? Answer: 100°C. The standard boiling point of water at sea level is 100°C.
Which of the following is not a greenhouse gas? Answer: O₂. O₂ does not significantly contribute to the greenhouse effect.
The process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy is known as: Answer: Photosynthesis. Photosynthesis involves converting light energy into chemical energy using chlorophyll.
Which agency of socialization is the first and strongest? Answer: family. the family teaches language and values first.

Which of the following best describes the role of family in our society? Answer: To provide a nurturing environment for the growth and development of its members. The family primarily provides a nurturing environment for the holistic growth and development of its members.

In the context of community service, which activity demonstrates the principle of social cohesion? Answer: Organizing a community clean-up day. Community service activities like organizing a clean-up day bring people together, fostering a sense of unity and shared responsibility.

What is the primary purpose of implementing community-based initiatives in rural areas? Answer: To empower local communities by involving them in decision-making processes. Community-based initiatives aim to empower locals by integrating them into decision-making processes, enhancing their autonomy and development.

Which of the following practices promotes environmental sustainability in our society? Answer: Implementing recycling programs for waste management. Recycling programs contribute to environmental sustainability by reducing waste and conserving resources.

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: The three dimensions of HDI are health, education and Answer: standard of living. standard of living (measured by GNI per capita).

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: The number of local levels in Nepal is Answer: 753. 753 (6 metropolitan, 11 sub-metropolitan, 276 municipalities, 460 rural municipalities).

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: The Constitution of Nepal was promulgated on Answer: 3 Ashwin 2072. 3 Ashwin 2072 (20 September 2015). 15 Jestha 2065 is the day the republic was declared.

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: A village has a population of 5000 in the year 2019. If the population increases by 5% annually, what will be the population in 2021? Answer: $5512.5$. The population after two years at 5% annual growth is $5000 \times (1+0.05)^2 = 5512.5$.

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: The literacy rate of a region increased from 60% to 70%. What is the absolute increase in the literacy rate? Answer: $10\%$. The absolute increase in the literacy rate is $70\% - 60\% = 10\%$.

concepts.u: Unit 2: Development and the Foundations of Development
concepts.t: If a country's total agricultural output was 15 million tons last year and it increased to 18 million tons this year, what is the percentage increase in output? Answer: $20\%$. The percentage increase in output is $\frac{18-15}{15} \times 100 = 20\%$.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: How many World Heritage Sites does Nepal have, according to the book? Answer: 4. Kathmandu Valley, Sagarmatha National Park, Chitwan National Park and Lumbini.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: Lumbini was listed as a World Heritage Site in Answer: 1997. 1997 (Kathmandu Valley and Sagarmatha 1979; Chitwan 1984).

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: Which of these is a string instrument? Answer: sarangi. sarangi; madal and damphu are drums, bansuri a wind instrument, jhyali a cymbal.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: Unity Day is observed on Answer: 27 Poush. 27 Poush (Prithvi Narayan Shah's birthday).

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: Which of these is a folk song of Nepal? Answer: Asare. Asare, a folk song; Charya is a classical dance.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: In a survey, it was found that 40 out of 100 people believe in recycling. What percentage of people do not believe in recycling? Answer: 60%. If 40% of people believe in recycling, then 60% do not, since 100% - 40% = 60%.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: A village has a population of 200 people. If 3/4th of the population practices a certain belief, how many people practice this belief? Answer: 150. To find how many people practice the belief, calculate $\frac{3}{4} \times 200 = 150$ people.

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: During a festival, 500 candles were distributed among 50 families equally. How many candles did each family receive? Answer: 10. Dividing 500 candles by 50 families gives $\frac{500}{50} = 10$ candles per family.
The anti-corruption body of Nepal is the Answer: CIAA. CIAA, the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority.
The child helpline number is Answer: 1098. 1098 is the child helpline; 100 is the police number.
Chhaupadi is an example of Answer: a superstition. a harmful belief that keeps women out of the home during menstruation.
Of these, the number elected by first-past-the-post is Answer: 165. 165 (the other 110 by proportional representation).
The term of a National Assembly member is Answer: 6 years. 6 years; one-third retire every two years.

What is the term used to describe the active participation of citizens in the democratic processes of their country? Answer: Civic Engagement. Civic engagement refers specifically to active participation in the democratic processes.

What does the concept of civic consciousness primarily encourage among individuals? Answer: Social Involvement. Civic consciousness emphasizes the importance of social involvement and community service.

Which of the following best describes the principle of 'Rule of Law' in a democratic society? Answer: Every citizen must obey the laws of the land, including the government officials. Rule of law means that everyone, including government officials, must follow the established laws of the country.
The Panchayat system lasted from 2019 to Answer: 2046. 2046 (the Panchayat period was 2019–2046).
Nepal was declared a republic on Answer: 28 May 2008. 28 May 2008, declared by the first Constituent Assembly.

What was the primary economic activity during the early medieval period in Nepal? Answer: Agriculture. Agriculture was the mainstay of the economy during this era, supporting the growing population and trade.

The term 'Muluki Ain' refers to what type of historical document in Nepal? Answer: Legal Code. Muluki Ain is historically significant as the legal code that governed social and judicial matters in Nepal.

Who among the following was instrumental in unifying the small principalities into a single kingdom in the late 18th century? Answer: Prithvi Narayan Shah. Prithvi Narayan Shah led the campaigns that unified various small kingdoms into a larger state, laying the foundation of modern Nepal.
Nepal's hydropower potential in the book is about Answer: 83,000 MW. about 83,000 MW (about 42,000 MW viable).
The First Periodic Plan began in Answer: 2013 BS. 2013 BS (1956 AD), with the National Planning Commission (NPC) leading planning.

What is the term used to describe economic activities that involve the extraction of natural resources from the earth? Answer: Mining. Mining involves extracting natural resources such as minerals and metals from the earth.

Which of the following best describes primary economic activities? Answer: Activities involved in extracting or harvesting natural products. Primary economic activities are those directly involved with natural resources.

The principle that states that agricultural production should be carried out where it is most profitable due to natural conditions is known as: Answer: Thunen's Law of Agricultural Location. Thunen's Law of Agricultural Location explains how agricultural activities are distributed based on profitability and natural conditions.

concepts.u: Unit 9: Our International Relations and Cooperation
concepts.t: What is the primary purpose of the United Nations (UN)? Answer: To maintain international peace and security.. The primary purpose of the UN includes maintaining international peace and security.

concepts.u: Unit 9: Our International Relations and Cooperation
concepts.t: Which principle of international law states that a state cannot be sued without its consent? Answer: Sovereign Immunity. Sovereign immunity prevents a state from being sued without its consent under international law.

concepts.u: Unit 9: Our International Relations and Cooperation
concepts.t: Which international organization primarily focuses on environmental issues and sustainability? Answer: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is specifically established to address environmental issues.

concepts.u: Unit 9: Our International Relations and Cooperation
concepts.t: Which term describes the practice where a country extends its legal jurisdiction over actions taken outside its national boundaries? Answer: Long-arm Statute. A long-arm statute allows a state to extend its legal jurisdiction beyond its borders under certain circumstances.
Which ecological region is the most densely populated? Answer: Terai. Terai (460), then Hill 192 and Mountain 34.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Which of the following countries is not a member of SAARC? Answer: Japan. Japan is not a member of SAARC as it does not share geographical proximity to the South Asian region.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: What was the primary reason for the establishment of the United Nations in 1945? Answer: To prevent the outbreak of future wars. The United Nations was established primarily to maintain international peace and security, preventing the recurrence of global conflicts like World War II.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Which of the following is considered a renewable natural resource? Answer: Solar Energy. Solar energy is a renewable resource because it can be replenished naturally within a short period of time.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: The concept of 'Universal Human Rights' is primarily derived from which document? Answer: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948, sets out fundamental human rights to be universally protected.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'sustainable development'? Answer: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Sustainable development aims to balance current needs and the preservation of resources for future generations.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: The practice of dividing land into small plots to cultivate multiple crops simultaneously is known as: Answer: Intercropping. Intercropping involves growing different crops together on the same plot of land.
The most abundant organic compound found in nature is Answer: cellulose. cellulose is the wall material of every plant cell on Earth; starch is only a store.
The bond that joins two monosaccharide units is a Answer: glycosidic bond. the C–O–C link between two sugars is glycosidic; peptide belongs to protein, phosphodiester to nucleic acid.
Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar? Answer: sucrose. in sucrose both anomeric carbons are locked in the linkage, so no free aldehyde group remains.
The storage carbohydrate of animals and fungi is Answer: glycogen. glycogen is animal starch, stored in liver and muscle; inulin is a plant store (Dahlia).
The number of amino acids that commonly occur in natural proteins is Answer: 20. 20 standard amino acids; 64 is the number of codons, a classic swap.
A peptide bond is formed between Answer: a carboxyl group and an amino group. the –COOH of one residue condenses with the –NH₂ of the next, releasing one water molecule.

The secondary structure of a protein is held together mainly by Answer: hydrogen bonds. hydrogen bonds between C=O and N–H hold the α-helix and β-pleated sheet; peptide bonds give the primary structure.
Fats are esters of fatty acids with Answer: glycerol. one glycerol plus three fatty acids gives a triglyceride.
The lipid that forms the bilayer of a biological membrane is Answer: phospholipid. the phosphate head is hydrophilic and the two fatty-acid tails hydrophobic, so it forms a bilayer in water.
Which nitrogen base is present in RNA but not in DNA? Answer: uracil. uracil replaces thymine in RNA; the two differ only by a methyl group.

In a double-stranded DNA molecule, adenine is 30 per cent of the total bases. The percentage of guanine is Answer: 20. Chargaff: A = T = 30 %, so A + T = 60 % and G + C = 40 %, giving G = 20 %. Option (a) is chosen by students who think G = A.
The sugar present in DNA is Answer: deoxyribose. deoxyribose lacks the –OH at carbon 2, which is what makes DNA chemically stable.
The double-helix model of DNA was proposed by Answer: Watson and Crick. Watson and Crick, 1953, using Franklin's X-ray data.
Enzymes speed up a reaction by Answer: lowering the activation energy. the enzyme provides an alternative path of lower activation energy; it never shifts the equilibrium.
The three-domain system of classification was proposed by Answer: Carl Woese. Woese (1977, 1990), on the basis of 16S/18S rRNA sequences.
The three domains of life are Answer: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya. Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya; Whittaker's five kingdoms sit inside these.
In the name Oryza sativa L., the word sativa is the Answer: specific epithet. the second word is the specific epithet; the species name is the whole two-word phrase.
The five-kingdom system of classification was given in 1969 by Answer: R. H. Whittaker. Whittaker, 1969: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
Which kingdom in the five-kingdom system contains only prokaryotes? Answer: Monera. Monera alone; Protista are unicellular but eukaryotic.
The reserve food of fungi is Answer: glycogen. glycogen, exactly as in animals; answering "starch" here is the standard slip.
The cell wall of a typical fungus is made of Answer: chitin. chitin, a nitrogen-containing polysaccharide, again shared with animals (insect cuticle).
A fungal mycelium in which the hyphae have no cross walls is described as Answer: coenocytic. coenocytic (aseptate), as in Mucor and Rhizopus; a multinucleate tube with no cross walls.
The asexual spores produced inside a sporangium of Mucor are Answer: sporangiospores. sporangiospores are formed inside a sac; conidia are formed externally in chains (Penicillium).
Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was obtained from Answer: Penicillium notatum. Alexander Fleming, 1928, from Penicillium notatum.
Yeast (Saccharomyces) reproduces asexually mainly by Answer: budding. budding; a small outgrowth pinches off with a nucleus.
A lichen is a symbiotic association between Answer: a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium. mycobiont plus phycobiont, an obligate mutualism.
In a lichen the fungal partner is called the Answer: mycobiont. mycobiont; the alga is the phycobiont and makes the food.
Bacteria were first observed and described by Answer: Anton van Leeuwenhoek. Leeuwenhoek, 1676, with his own single-lens microscope; Pasteur and Koch came two centuries later.
A spherical bacterium is called a Answer: coccus. coccus (plural cocci); bacillus is rod-shaped.
Eight cocci arranged in a cube of two layers form a Answer: sarcina. sarcina is the 8-celled cube; a tetrad is a flat group of four.
A comma-shaped bacterium such as Vibrio cholerae belongs to the morphological type Answer: vibrio. vibrio, a curved comma; a spirochaete is a long flexible spiral.
A small extra-chromosomal circular DNA of a bacterium is a Answer: plasmid. plasmids carry genes for antibiotic resistance and are the vectors of genetic engineering.

Transfer of DNA from one bacterium to another through a bacteriophage is Answer: transduction. transduction is phage-mediated; transformation is uptake of naked DNA, conjugation is transfer through a pilus.
The commonest mode of asexual reproduction in bacteria is Answer: binary fission. binary fission, which under ideal conditions can occur every twenty minutes.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the root nodules of legumes belong to the genus Answer: Rhizobium. Rhizobium; Nitrosomonas is a free-living nitrifier and belongs to a different step of the cycle.

The term virus, meaning poison, and the discovery of the tobacco mosaic agent are credited to Answer: Ivanowsky and Beijerinck. Ivanowsky (1892) showed the agent passed a bacterial filter, Beijerinck (1898) named it contagium vivum fluidum.
The protein coat of a virus is called the Answer: capsid. the capsid is built of repeating protein subunits called capsomeres.

Viruses are regarded as being on the borderline of living and non-living because they Answer: can be crystallised yet multiply inside a host cell. outside a host a virus is an inert chemical that can be crystallised; inside one it replicates and mutates.
A virus that infects a bacterium is a Answer: bacteriophage. bacteriophage, literally "bacteria eater"; T₄ phage of E. coli is the standard example.
The genetic material of the tobacco mosaic virus is Answer: single-stranded RNA. TMV was the first virus discovered and contains single-stranded RNA.
Which of the following diseases is not caused by a virus? Answer: tuberculosis. tuberculosis is bacterial (Mycobacterium tuberculosis); the other three are viral.
The term ecosystem was coined in 1935 by Answer: A. G. Tansley. Tansley, 1935; Lindeman later quantified the energy flow.
The study of a single species in relation to its environment is Answer: autecology. autecology is one species, synecology a whole community.
Which of the following is an edaphic factor? Answer: soil pH. edaphic means soil-related; the other three are climatic.
Green plants of an ecosystem are called Answer: producers. producers, also called transducers of solar energy, but the standard CDC term is producers.
Decomposers are also known as Answer: saprotrophs. saprotrophs feed on dead organic matter by external digestion.
A food chain that begins with dead organic matter is a Answer: detritus food chain. the detritus food chain; in a forest it actually carries more energy than the grazing chain.
In the chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle, the frog occupies the trophic level Answer: third. grass 1st, grasshopper 2nd, frog 3rd. Counting the producer as zero is the usual error.

Food chains rarely exceed four or five links because Answer: so much energy is lost as heat at every transfer. only about a tenth passes on, so the fifth level has too little energy to support a viable population.

If the producers of an ecosystem store 20,000 kJ, the energy available to the tertiary consumers under the ten per cent law is Answer: 20 kJ. 20,000 → 2,000 (herbivore) → 200 (secondary) → 20 kJ (tertiary). Stopping one step early gives (b), the commonest wrong answer.
Gross primary productivity minus respiration of the producers equals Answer: net primary productivity. NPP = GPP - R; only NPP is available to the next level.

The pyramid of biomass in a pond ecosystem is inverted because Answer: the phytoplankton have a small standing crop but a very high turnover rate. the tiny algae are eaten as fast as they grow, so at any instant their standing biomass is less than that of the fish they support.
Energy flow in an ecosystem is Answer: unidirectional. unidirectional, by the second law of thermodynamics; only nutrients are cycled.
Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia is Answer: nitrogen fixation. nitrogen fixation, biological (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Anabaena) or physical (lightning).

The vegetation of Nepal is chiefly determined by Answer: altitude and the rainfall that goes with it. Nepal rises from about 60 m to 8848 m in under 200 km, so altitude compresses all the vegetation belts of Asia into one country.
Sal (Shorea robusta) forest is the characteristic vegetation of Answer: the Terai and Bhabar up to about 1000 m. sal is the dominant hardwood of the Terai, Bhabar and lower Siwalik.

The tropical vegetation zone of Nepal extends up to an altitude of about Answer: 1000 m. tropical up to about 1000 m, sub-tropical 1000–2000 m, temperate 2000–3000 m, sub-alpine 3000–4100 m, alpine above that.
Rhododendron arboreum, the national flower of Nepal, is typical of the Answer: temperate zone. Laligurans forms whole forests between about 2000 and 3500 m.
The zone above the tree line, dominated by low shrubs, herbs and cushion plants, is the Answer: alpine zone. the alpine zone lies above the tree line, roughly above 4100 m.
Abies, Betula and Juniperus are characteristic genera of the Answer: sub-alpine forest. fir, birch and juniper are the sub-alpine indicators.
Conservation of a species inside its own natural habitat is called Answer: in-situ conservation. in-situ: national parks, wildlife reserves, conservation areas, biosphere reserves.
Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation? Answer: the Central Zoo at Jawalakhel. a zoo keeps animals outside their habitat; the other three are protected areas, so in-situ.
A seed bank or gene bank is a method of Answer: ex-situ conservation. the material is stored away from the habitat, which is the definition of ex-situ.
The largest national park of Nepal by area is Answer: Shey Phoksundo National Park. Shey Phoksundo, 3555 km², in Dolpa and Mugu; Chitwan is the oldest (1973) but smaller.

Shifting cultivation, known in Nepal as khoriya, damages vegetation mainly by Answer: repeated burning and clearing that prevents forest regeneration. the fallow period is now too short for the soil and the forest to recover.

The most important direct cause of deforestation in the hills of Nepal is Answer: clearing for agriculture, fuelwood and fodder. a rural household needs land, firewood and fodder, and takes all three from the forest.

Community forestry in Nepal is significant because it Answer: hands over management of a patch of national forest to a local user group. a Community Forest User Group manages and harvests the forest and keeps the income; Nepal's programme is studied worldwide.
Shorea robusta is the dominant tree of the Answer: tropical zone. Sal is the dominant tree of the Terai, Bhabar and Dun valleys, below 1000 m.
The term biology was introduced independently in 1802 by Answer: Lamarck and Treviranus. Jean-Baptiste Lamarck and Gottfried Treviranus, both in 1802, from Greek bios (life) and logos (study).
Aristotle is called the Answer: father of zoology. Aristotle is the father of zoology and of biology as a whole; his pupil Theophrastus is the father of botany.
The branch of biology that deals with the functions of the parts of an organism is Answer: physiology. physiology is function; anatomy is internal structure revealed by dissection.
The study of the form and external structure of organisms is Answer: morphology. morphology; if you cut it open to see inside, it becomes anatomy.
The study of fossils is Answer: palaeontology. palaeontology supplies the direct evidence of evolution.
The study of birds is Answer: ornithology. ornithology; ichthyology is fish, herpetology reptiles and amphibians.
The study of insects is Answer: entomology. entomology. Note etymology, option (b), is the study of the origin of words — a deliberate trap.
The study of animal behaviour is Answer: ethology. ethology; ethnology, option (c), is the study of human races and cultures.

Which of the following is not a characteristic of all living things? Answer: locomotion from place to place. plants are living but do not move from place to place; all living things show the other three.
Biology is related to chemistry most directly through the branch Answer: biochemistry. biochemistry studies the molecules and reactions of life.

Sensitivity, or irritability, is best defined as Answer: the ability to detect and respond to a change in the surroundings. detecting a stimulus and responding to it; a plant bending towards light counts.
The term "biology" is derived from the Greek words Answer: bios and logos. bios = life, logos = study or discourse.
Aristotle is regarded as the Answer: Father of Zoology. Aristotle is the Father of Zoology (and of Biology as a whole); Theophrastus is the Father of Botany.
The theory that life originated from non-living matter under the conditions of the early Earth is Answer: chemical evolution. chemical or abiogenic evolution, the modern scientific account.
The theory of chemical origin of life was proposed by Answer: Oparin and Haldane. A. I. Oparin (1924) and J. B. S. Haldane (1929), independently; the "hot dilute soup".
The primitive atmosphere of the Earth is believed to have been Answer: reducing, with no free oxygen. reducing; free oxygen would have oxidised the organic molecules as fast as they formed.
The theory that life came to Earth as spores from outer space is Answer: cosmozoic or panspermia. the cosmozoic or panspermia theory of Richter and Arrhenius. It only moves the problem elsewhere.
Spontaneous generation was finally disproved by the swan-necked flask experiment of Answer: Louis Pasteur. Pasteur, 1864; the broth stayed sterile because dust could not climb the bend.

Organs of different animals that have the same basic structure and origin but different functions are Answer: homologous. homologous: same origin, different function, showing divergent evolution from a common ancestor.
The wing of a bird and the wing of an insect are Answer: analogous. analogous: same function (flight), completely different structure and origin.
Homologous organs are evidence of Answer: divergent evolution. divergent evolution, or adaptive radiation; analogous organs show convergent evolution. Swapping these two is the standard mistake.

The forelimbs of a whale, a bat, a horse and a human are a classic example of Answer: homologous organs. the same bones — humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges — put to swimming, flying, running and grasping.
The vermiform appendix in humans is an example of Answer: a vestigial organ. vestigial: reduced and functionless in humans, but a working cellulose-digesting caecum in a rabbit.

Archaeopteryx is important because it is a connecting link between Answer: reptiles and birds. it had feathers and a wishbone like a bird, and teeth, a long bony tail and clawed fingers like a reptile.
Peripatus is regarded as a connecting link between Answer: Annelida and Arthropoda. it has the segmented body and nephridia of an annelid with the tracheae and claws of an arthropod.
A living fossil among the following is Answer: Latimeria. Latimeria, the coelacanth, caught alive in 1938; the others are extinct fossils.
"Ontogeny repeats phylogeny" — the biogenetic law — was stated by Answer: Ernst Haeckel. Haeckel's recapitulation theory: the embryo passes through the ancestral stages.
Paramecium moves by means of Answer: cilia. some 10,000–14,000 cilia over the whole pellicle, beating in metachronal waves.
The locomotory organelle of Amoeba is the Answer: pseudopodium. temporary pseudopodia formed by sol–gel changes of the cytoplasm.
The osmoregulatory organelle of a freshwater protozoan is the Answer: contractile vacuole. the contractile vacuole pumps out the water that constantly enters by osmosis.
Paramecium is unusual among protozoans in having Answer: two kinds of nuclei, a macronucleus and a micronucleus. nuclear dimorphism: a large kidney-shaped macronucleus and one or more micronuclei.
Asexual reproduction in Paramecium is by Answer: transverse binary fission. transverse binary fission in Paramecium; Euglena divides longitudinally. Examiners set this pair together deliberately.

Conjugation in Paramecium is significant because it Answer: brings about nuclear reorganisation and genetic recombination. no increase in number takes place; conjugation only reshuffles genes and rejuvenates the animal, which is why Paramecium is said never to grow old.
The infective stage of Plasmodium injected into a human by the mosquito is the Answer: sporozoite. sporozoites from the mosquito's salivary gland; merozoites are produced later inside the human.
Malaria is transmitted by the bite of Answer: a female Anopheles mosquito. only the female takes a blood meal, which she needs for her eggs.

In the life cycle of Plasmodium, the human being is the Answer: secondary or intermediate host. the mosquito is the primary host because the sexual cycle takes place in it; the human is secondary. This is inverted by most students.
The most dangerous species of malarial parasite, causing malignant tertian malaria, is Answer: Plasmodium falciparum. P. falciparum causes cerebral malaria and most malarial deaths.

The bursting of red blood cells that releases merozoites and toxins causes Answer: the periodic chill and fever of malaria. the synchronous rupture of the infected erythrocytes releases haemozoin, which triggers the chill-and-fever paroxysm.
Animals in which the cells are not organised into tissues show the Answer: cellular level. the cellular level, as in Porifera, where the cells are loosely aggregated.
Radial symmetry is characteristic of Answer: Cnidaria. Cnidaria; Porifera are mostly asymmetrical, Annelida and Arthropoda bilateral.
The body cavity lined on all sides by mesoderm is a Answer: true coelom. a true coelom or eucoelom, lined entirely by mesodermal peritoneum.
The change in an organism that fits it better to its surroundings is Answer: adaptation. adaptation is heritable and evolutionary; acclimatisation is a reversible adjustment within one lifetime.

Streamlined body, fins and a swim bladder in a fish are adaptations for Answer: aquatic life. the streamlined shape cuts drag, the fins steer and the swim bladder holds the fish at any depth without effort.
Pneumatic (hollow) bones and air sacs are flight adaptations of Answer: birds. birds; pneumatic bones cut weight and the air sacs give a one-way flow of air through the lungs.
The blubber of a whale or a seal is an adaptation for Answer: buoyancy and heat insulation. a thick subcutaneous fat layer that insulates in cold water and makes the animal buoyant.
Cryptic colouration, in which an animal matches its background, is an example of Answer: camouflage. camouflage; mimicry is resembling another organism, not the background.
An innate, unlearned, stereotyped response of the whole animal to a stimulus is Answer: instinct. instinct is inborn and needs no practice, unlike all forms of learning.
The waggle dance by which a honeybee tells the hive the direction and distance of food was decoded by Answer: Karl von Frisch. von Frisch, who shared the 1973 Nobel Prize with Lorenz and Tinbergen.

A duckling following the first moving object it sees after hatching shows Answer: imprinting. imprinting, described by Konrad Lorenz; it happens only in a short critical period and cannot be reversed.

Pavlov's dog salivating at the sound of a bell is an example of Answer: classical conditioning. classical conditioning: a neutral stimulus is paired with a natural one until it alone produces the response.
The seasonal, two-way movement of animals along a regular route is Answer: migration. migration is periodic and two-way; emigration is one-way and permanent.
A fish that lives in the sea and migrates into rivers to breed, such as the salmon, is called Answer: anadromous. anadromous, "running up" the river to breed.
