Which of the following is a vector quantity? Answer: torque. torque has a direction given by the right-hand rule; work and charge are scalars.
The magnitude of $\hat{i}\times\hat{j}$ is Answer: 1. $\sin 90^{\circ} = 1$ and both are unit vectors.
Two equal vectors of magnitude $P$ give a resultant of magnitude $P$. The angle between them is Answer: $120^{\circ}$. $P^{2} = 2P^{2}(1 + \cos\theta)$ gives $\cos\theta = -1/2$.
The area of the triangle formed by $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ as two of its sides is Answer: $\frac{1}{2}AB\sin\theta$. the cross product gives the parallelogram area; the triangle is half of it.

From the velocity–time graph above, the total displacement of the body in $10\ \text{s}$ is Answer: $140\ \text{m}$. triangle A $= \tfrac12(4)(20) = 40$, rectangle B $= 4\times20 = 80$, triangle C $= \tfrac12(2)(20) = 20$; total $140\ \text{m}$. Option (d) is $20\times10$, the area of the whole rectangle — the error of treating a varying velocity as constant.

The area under an acceleration–time graph gives Answer: change in velocity. area $= \int a\,dt = \Delta v$. Option (a) is the area under a velocity–time graph; mixing the two graphs up is the standard slip.

A stone is dropped from a height and another is thrown horizontally from the same height at the same instant. They Answer: reach the ground together. vertical motion is identical and independent of the horizontal motion; $t = \sqrt{2h/g}$ contains no $u$.

Two cars move towards each other at $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The speed of one relative to the other is Answer: $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. opposite directions, so $v_{AB} = 10-(-20) = 30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Option (a) subtracts the speeds, which is right only for the same direction.

A body is projected with speed $u$ at $30^{\circ}$. Another has the same range with the same speed at Answer: $60^{\circ}$. complementary angles give equal range, and $90^{\circ}-30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.
The quantity $s_n = u + \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$ has the SI unit Answer: $\text{m}$. it is the distance travelled during one particular second, so a metre. The "per second" in the wording tempts (a).

Which law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the force applied? Answer: Newton's Second Law. Newton's Second Law relates the net force acting on a body to its acceleration and thus to the rate of change of momentum.

If a particle moves with uniform circular motion, what is true about its velocity? Answer: Its direction changes continuously.. In uniform circular motion, the speed remains constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously, pointing tangentially to the circle.
What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent? Answer: Displacement. The area under a velocity-time graph corresponds to the displacement of the object during the given time interval.
Newton's second law of motion in its most general form is Answer: $F = dp/dt$. $F = ma$ follows from $F = dp/dt$ only when the mass is constant, which fails for a rocket.

A rocket moves forward because Answer: of conservation of linear momentum. the gas carries momentum backwards, so the rocket carries an equal momentum forwards. Option (a) is the classic error: a rocket works in vacuum, where there is nothing to push against.
A body of mass $2\ \text{kg}$ at rest is acted on by a force of $10\ \text{N}$ for $3\ \text{s}$. The impulse is Answer: $30\ \text{N s}$. $J = F\Delta t = 10\times3 = 30\ \text{N s}$.

Which statement about action and reaction is correct? Answer: they act on different bodies and never cancel. they are equal and opposite but act on different bodies, so they can never be added together to cancel.

A man of mass $60\ \text{kg}$ stands in a lift accelerating upwards at $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ($g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$). The reading of the weighing machine is Answer: $720\ \text{N}$. $N = m(g+a) = 60(12) = 720\ \text{N}$. Option (b) is the true weight, chosen by anyone who forgets the lift is accelerating; the machine reads the normal reaction, not the weight.
The coefficient of kinetic friction is Answer: less than it. it always takes a larger force to start sliding than to keep it going.
If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes Answer: four times. $K = p^{2}/2m$, so $K \propto p^{2}$. Option (b) comes from assuming $K \propto p$.

In a perfectly elastic head-on collision between two bodies of equal mass, one at rest, Answer: they exchange velocities. put $m_1 = m_2$ and $u_2 = 0$ in the elastic-collision result: $v_1 = 0$, $v_2 = u_1$. Option (a) describes a perfectly inelastic collision.

A man of mass $60\ \text{kg}$ climbs a $5\ \text{m}$ staircase in $10\ \text{s}$ ($g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$). His power output is Answer: $300\ \text{W}$. $W = mgh = 60\times10\times5 = 3000\ \text{J}$, so $P = 3000/10 = 300\ \text{W}$. Option (c) is the work, not the power.
In an inelastic collision, the quantity that is not conserved is Answer: kinetic energy. momentum and total energy always survive; the missing kinetic energy has become heat, sound and deformation.
The area under a force–displacement graph represents Answer: work done. $W = \int F\,dx$ is exactly the area under the curve.
Which of the following is a non-conservative force? Answer: viscous force. viscous drag depends on the path and dissipates energy as heat.
In a perfectly inelastic collision, the quantity that is not conserved is Answer: kinetic energy. momentum and total energy are conserved; kinetic energy is lost to heat and deformation.

Which of the following does NOT conserve mechanical energy in a system? Answer: A car accelerating up a hill. Mechanical energy is not conserved when there is an external non-conservative force like friction or when work is done against gravity by an engine.

The difference between the tensions at the lowest and the highest point of a vertical circle is Answer: $6mg$. subtracting the two force equations and using $v_2^2 = v_1^2 + 4gr$ gives $6mg$, independent of the speed.

A body completes $60$ revolutions per minute. Its angular velocity is Answer: $2\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. $60\ \text{rpm} = 1\ \text{rev s}^{-1} = 2\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. Option (c) is the trap: rpm read straight off as rad s⁻¹.
The angle of banking of a road of radius $r$ for a design speed $v$ is given by Answer: $\tan\theta = v^{2}/rg$. from $N\sin\theta = mv^2/r$ and $N\cos\theta = mg$.
A stone of mass $0.5\ \text{kg}$ moves in a circle of radius $2\ \text{m}$ at $4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The centripetal force is Answer: $4\ \text{N}$. $F = mv^2/r = 0.5\times16/2 = 4\ \text{N}$.
The angular velocity of a body making $300$ revolutions per minute is Answer: $10\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. $\omega = 2\pi N/60 = 2\pi(300)/60 = 10\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$.
The angle of banking of a road is independent of Answer: mass of the vehicle. $\tan\theta = v^2/rg$ contains no mass term.
The escape velocity and the orbital velocity close to the Earth's surface are related by Answer: $v_e = \sqrt{2}\,v_o$. $v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R}$ and $v_o = \sqrt{GM/R}$.

An astronaut inside an orbiting satellite feels weightless because Answer: the astronaut and the satellite are in free fall together. gravity is still about $89\%$ of its surface value at $400\ \text{km}$; what vanishes is the normal reaction. Option (a) is the single commonest misconception in this unit.
Escape velocity from a planet does not depend on Answer: the mass of the escaping body. $m$ cancels out of $\tfrac12mv_e^2 = GMm/R$.
Gravitational potential at a point is Answer: always negative. with $V = 0$ chosen at infinity and gravity always attractive, $V = -GM/r$ is negative everywhere.
The dimensional formula of the universal gravitational constant $G$ is Answer: $[M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2}]$. from $G = Fr^2/m_1m_2$, $[MLT^{-2}][L^2]/[M^2] = [M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$.
The escape velocity from the Earth's surface does not depend on Answer: the mass of the body. $v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$ contains no term for the mass of the escaping body.
A GPS receiver needs a minimum of how many satellites to fix its position and time? Answer: 4. three for the three spatial coordinates, a fourth for the receiver clock error.

If the radius of the Earth decreases while its mass remains constant, what will happen to the acceleration due to gravity at its surface? Answer: It will increase. Since $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, decreasing $R$ increases $g$ if $M$ is constant.

Which of the following statements is true regarding the escape velocity from Earth? Answer: It is independent of the mass of the object being launched. Escape velocity is derived from energy equations and is independent of the object's mass.
Which elastic modulus is defined for liquids and gases? Answer: bulk modulus. fluids have no fixed shape, so they cannot sustain a shear or a tensile stress.
The theoretical limits of Poisson's ratio are Answer: $-1$ to $0.5$. practical materials sit in $0.2$–$0.4$; the negative half of the range belongs to rare auxetic materials.
The energy stored per unit volume of a stretched wire is Answer: $\tfrac12\times$ stress $\times$ strain. from $U = \tfrac12Fe$ divided by the volume $AL$.
Breaking stress of a wire depends on Answer: the material only. breaking stress is a material property; breaking force is what depends on the area.

Hooke's law is obeyed only up to the Answer: proportional limit. beyond the proportional limit the stress–strain graph is no longer a straight line, even though the wire may still return to its original length up to the elastic limit.
The SI unit of stress is Answer: N m⁻². stress is force per unit area, N m⁻² = Pa.
The zeroth law of thermodynamics gives a physical basis for the concept of Answer: temperature. it guarantees that "same temperature" is a consistent labelling of bodies.

The mean translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule depends only on Answer: the absolute temperature. $\bar E_k = \tfrac32k_BT$ contains no mass term, so at the same temperature a heavy and a light molecule have the same mean translational energy (the heavy one simply moves more slowly).
The temperature at which the Celsius and Fahrenheit readings are numerically equal is Answer: $-40^{\circ}$. set $C = F$ in $C/100 = (F-32)/180$; both scales read $-40$.

Mercury is preferred to water as a thermometric liquid mainly because Answer: it expands uniformly and does not wet glass. plus a wide liquid range and good visibility. Option (d) is wrong twice over: mercury's specific heat capacity is low, which is an advantage.

Heat flows between two bodies in contact because of a difference in their Answer: temperatures. a large cold lake holds far more thermal energy than a matchstick flame, yet heat still flows from the flame to the lake.
The thermometric property used in a constant-volume gas thermometer is Answer: pressure. the volume is held fixed by definition, so pressure is the quantity that varies.
A body at $27\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ has an absolute temperature of Answer: $300.15\ \text{K}$. $K = C + 273.15$. Option (b) is $273 + 0$, a careless subtraction.
Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium when they have the same Answer: temperature. equal temperature is the definition; equal heat content is neither necessary nor sufficient.

Heat flows from body $A$ to body $B$ when placed in contact because $A$ has Answer: higher average molecular kinetic energy. temperature, i.e. average molecular KE, decides the direction; the total heat content does not.
The law of thermodynamics that makes temperature a measurable quantity is the Answer: zeroth law. the zeroth law guarantees a common value shared by bodies in equilibrium.
The temperature at which the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales read the same is Answer: $-40^{\circ}$. solving $x = \frac{9}{5}x+32$ gives $x = -40$.
The thermometric property of a mercury-in-glass thermometer is the Answer: length of the mercury column. the measured quantity is the length of the thread in the uniform bore.

When a metal plate with a circular hole is heated, the hole Answer: becomes larger. every linear dimension of the plate, including the diameter of the hole, is multiplied by $(1+\alpha\Delta\theta)$. Option (a) is the standard misconception: students picture the metal "closing in".

Dulong and Petit's method is preferred for a liquid because it Answer: needs no correction for the expansion of the vessel. the two liquid columns balance in a single U-tube, so the glass cancels out.
The SI unit of the coefficient of linear expansion is Answer: $\text{K}^{-1}$. a fractional change in length per kelvin; the metres cancel.
A pendulum clock with a metal rod is taken from winter to summer. It will Answer: lose time. the rod lengthens, so $T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$ increases and the clock ticks too slowly.
When a metal plate with a hole in it is heated, the hole Answer: gets larger. a cavity expands like the material that would fill it.
The real expansivity of a liquid equals its apparent expansivity plus the Answer: cubical expansivity of the vessel. $\gamma_r = \gamma_a + \gamma_g$, where $\gamma_g = 3\alpha_g$.
Dulong and Petit's method directly determines the Answer: real expansivity. it balances pressures, so the vessel's expansion cancels out.
The SI unit of specific heat capacity is Answer: $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$. energy per kilogram per kelvin. Option (a) is the unit of specific latent heat; the two are swapped constantly.
The specific latent heat of fusion of ice is about Answer: $3.34\times10^{5}\ \text{J kg}^{-1}$. option (b) is $L_v$; option (d) is the old value in cal g⁻¹ misread as SI.
Newton's law of cooling holds well only when Answer: the excess of temperature over the surroundings is small. for large excess temperatures the loss follows Stefan's $T^4$ law instead.

While ice at $0\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ is melting, the heat supplied Answer: breaks the bonds of the solid lattice at constant temperature. the temperature stays fixed during a phase change, which is why "heat always raises temperature" is false.

Steam at $100\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ causes a worse burn than water at $100\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ because Answer: steam releases its latent heat of vaporisation on condensing. each kilogram of steam gives up $2.26\times10^{6}\ \text{J}$ before its temperature even starts to fall.
At the triple point of water Answer: ice, water and vapour coexist. a single point on the phase diagram, at $273.16\ \text{K}$ and $611.66\ \text{Pa}$.
While a solid is melting, the heat supplied to it Answer: increases the potential energy of its molecules. the bonds are broken, so molecular potential energy rises while the temperature stays fixed.
Newton's law of cooling is best obeyed when Answer: the excess temperature is small. the law is a linear approximation valid only for a small excess temperature.

The specific heat capacity of a substance is defined as the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of the substance by $1^\circ$C. Which of the following represents the correct formula for specific heat capacity? Answer: $c = \frac{Q}{m\Delta T}$. Specific heat capacity is calculated by dividing the heat added by the product of mass and temperature change.

According to Joule's law of heating, the heat produced in a conductor when an electric current passes through it depends on which factor(s)? Answer: Current squared ($I^2$), resistance ($R$) and time ($t$). Joule's law states that the heat generated is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which the current flows.

What is the unit of thermal conductivity in the International System of Units (SI)? Answer: $\text{W/mK}$. Thermal conductivity measures the rate at which heat can pass through a material, and its SI unit is watts per meter-kelvin.

The SI unit of thermal conductivity is Answer: $\text{W m}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$. from $H = kA\Delta\theta/L$, $k$ has units $\text{W}\times\text{m}/(\text{m}^2\text{K})$. Option (b) is Stefan's constant.
Wien's displacement law states that Answer: $\lambda_m T =$ constant. the peak wavelength shifts inversely with temperature; option (a) is the sign of the relation reversed.
According to Kirchhoff's law of radiation, a good absorber is Answer: a good emitter. at a given temperature the emissivity equals the absorptance.

Searle's method is used to measure the thermal conductivity of Answer: good conductors. a good conductor needs a long bar and a large temperature gradient; a bad conductor needs the thin disc of Lee's apparatus.
A body radiates most when it is Answer: dull and black. a dull black surface has $e$ close to $1$; a polished surface reflects and barely emits.
The SI unit of thermal conductivity is Answer: W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. from $H = kA\Delta\theta/L$, $k$ has units W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Heat transfer by convection cannot take place in Answer: a solid. convection needs the material itself to move, which a solid cannot do.
The wavelength of maximum emission from a black body at 2000 K is about 1450 nm. At 4000 K it will be about Answer: 725 nm. $\lambda_m \propto 1/T$, so doubling $T$ halves $\lambda_m$.

According to kinetic theory, the pressure exerted by an ideal gas is Answer: $\tfrac13\rho\overline{c^{2}}$. the factor $\tfrac13$ comes from $\overline{u^2} = \tfrac13\overline{c^2}$, the three equivalent directions.

If the absolute temperature of a gas is made four times, the rms speed of its molecules becomes Answer: $2$ times. $c_{rms} \propto \sqrt{T}$, and $\sqrt{4} = 2$. Option (b) is the trap of reading the relation as linear.
The ratio $\gamma = C_p/C_v$ for a monatomic ideal gas is Answer: $1.67$. three translational degrees of freedom only.
The mean kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas at temperature $T$ is Answer: $\tfrac32kT$. per molecule; option (c) is the value per mole, the commonest confusion here.
According to the law of Dulong and Petit, the molar heat capacity of a simple solid is about Answer: $3R$. $3R \approx 25\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
The focal length of a spherical mirror of radius of curvature $R$ is Answer: $R/2$. paraxial rays from infinity cross the axis half way to the centre of curvature.
The image formed by a convex mirror is always Answer: virtual, erect and diminished. the reflected rays always diverge, so the image is caught behind the mirror; no object position changes this.

An object is placed $15\ \text{cm}$ from a concave mirror of focal length $10\ \text{cm}$. The image distance is Answer: $30\ \text{cm}$ in front. with $u = -15\ \text{cm}$, $f = -10\ \text{cm}$: $1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/10 + 1/15 = -1/30$, so $v = -30\ \text{cm}$, i.e. $30\ \text{cm}$ in front of the mirror and real.

A convex mirror is used as a driver's rear-view mirror because it Answer: gives a wide field of view with an erect image. the diminished virtual image packs a wider scene into the same glass, at the price of making cars look further away than they are.
An object is placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror. The image is Answer: virtual, erect, magnified. inside the focus a concave mirror acts as a magnifying mirror.
A convex mirror of focal length $f$ forms, of a real object, an image that is always Answer: virtual and erect. the reflected rays always diverge, so the image is virtual, erect and diminished.

When light passes from air into glass, the quantity that does not change is its Answer: frequency. the source sets the frequency; the medium sets the speed, and therefore the wavelength through $v = f\lambda$.
For glass of refractive index $1.5$, the critical angle is about Answer: $41.8^{\circ}$. $C = \sin^{-1}(1/1.5) = 41.8^{\circ}$. Option (c) is the value for water, a frequent swap.

A pond is $4\ \text{m}$ deep. To an observer looking vertically down, its apparent depth ($n = 4/3$) is Answer: $3\ \text{m}$. apparent depth $= 4/(4/3) = 3\ \text{m}$. Option (a) multiplies by $n$ instead of dividing.
A ray entering an optically denser medium bends Answer: towards the normal. into the slower medium, the wavefront turns towards the normal.

Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from Answer: glass to air at an angle greater than the critical angle. both conditions are needed; option (b) drops the angle condition, option (a) has the media the wrong way round.
The refractive index of a medium in which light travels at $2.0\times10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ is Answer: $1.5$. $n = c/v = (3\times10^{8})/(2\times10^{8}) = 1.5$.
The critical angle for a glass of refractive index $1.5$ is about Answer: $42^{\circ}$. $\sin C = 1/1.5 = 0.667$, $C = 41.8^{\circ}$.
The lateral shift produced by a parallel-sided glass slab is zero when the angle of incidence is Answer: $0^{\circ}$. $d = t\sin(i-r)/\cos r$ and $i = r = 0$ gives $d = 0$.

A coin lies at the bottom of a beaker containing water ($n = 4/3$) $8\ \text{cm}$ deep. Seen from directly above it appears to be at a depth of Answer: $6\ \text{cm}$. apparent depth $= 8/(4/3) = 6\ \text{cm}$.
On passing from air into glass, the quantity that does not change is the Answer: frequency. frequency is set by the source; speed and wavelength both fall by the factor $n$.

What is Snell's Law used to determine? Answer: The angle of refraction between two different media. Snell's Law relates the angles of incidence and refraction when light passes through the interface between two different media.

Which of the following best describes the principle of reversibility of light? Answer: If light follows a certain path through a system of plane surfaces, it can follow the reverse path in the reverse direction. The principle of reversibility states that if light travels from A to B along a certain path, then it can travel back from B to A along the exact reverse path.
At the position of minimum deviation, the ray inside the prism is Answer: parallel to the base. the symmetry $r_1 = r_2$ is exactly what makes the internal ray parallel to the base.
For a prism of angle $60^{\circ}$ with a minimum deviation of $30^{\circ}$, the refractive index is Answer: $1.414$. $n = \sin45^{\circ}/\sin30^{\circ} = 0.7071/0.5 = 1.414$.
A thin prism of angle $5^{\circ}$ and refractive index $1.5$ produces a deviation of Answer: $2.5^{\circ}$. $\delta = (1.5-1)\times5^{\circ} = 2.5^{\circ}$.

As the angle of incidence on a prism is increased from a small value, the deviation Answer: first decreases to a minimum then increases. the deviation curve is U-shaped, which is why $\delta_m$ exists at all.
At minimum deviation the ray inside the prism is Answer: parallel to the base. symmetrical passage makes the internal ray parallel to the base.
The deviation produced by a thin prism of refracting angle $6^{\circ}$ made of glass of $n = 1.5$ is Answer: $3^{\circ}$. $\delta = (n-1)A = 0.5\times6^{\circ} = 3^{\circ}$.
The refractive index of the material of an equilateral prism whose minimum deviation is $30^{\circ}$ is Answer: $1.41$. $n = \sin45^{\circ}/\sin30^{\circ} = 1.414$.
A ray cannot emerge from the second face of a prism if the refracting angle $A$ is Answer: greater than $2C$. then $r_2 = A - r_1 > C$ for every $r_1$, so the ray is totally internally reflected.

What is the angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray when light passes through a prism called? Answer: Angle of deviation. The angle of deviation is defined as the angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray after passing through the prism.

Which of the following materials would result in the greatest deviation for a given prism angle when monochromatic light passes through it? Answer: Diamond. Diamond has the highest refractive index among the options, leading to the greatest deviation.

What is the condition for minimum deviation in a prism? Answer: The angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence. For minimum deviation, the angles of incidence and emergence are equal, resulting in symmetric paths within the prism.
The SI unit of the power of a lens is Answer: dioptre. one dioptre is one reciprocal metre of focal length.

When a convex glass lens is immersed in water, its focal length Answer: increases. the lens maker's formula uses the relative index $n_{glass}/n_{water} \approx 1.13$, so $(n-1)$ shrinks and $f$ grows.

An equiconvex glass lens ($n = 1.5$) has focal length $20\ \text{cm}$ in air. Immersed in water ($n = 4/3$), its focal length becomes Answer: $80\ \text{cm}$. $(1.5/1.333-1)/(1.5-1) = 0.25$, so $f$ is multiplied by $4$.
For a real object, a concave lens always forms an image that is Answer: virtual, erect and diminished. the emergent rays always diverge, so the image is virtual, erect and smaller.

A ray directed at the optical centre of a thin lens Answer: emerges undeviated. the two faces are locally parallel there, so the ray is only laterally shifted, and for a thin lens that shift is negligible.
What is the power of a lens whose focal length is 50 cm? Answer: 2 diopters. Power of a lens is given by $P = \frac{1}{f}$, where $f$ is in meters. Thus, $P = \frac{1}{0.5} = 2$ diopters.
Dispersive power has the unit Answer: no unit. it is a ratio of two angles (or of two refractive-index differences).
Which colour is deviated most by a glass prism? Answer: violet. violet has the shortest wavelength and the largest $n$.

Dispersion of white light by a prism occurs because Answer: the speed of light in glass depends on wavelength. a wavelength-dependent speed means a wavelength-dependent $n$, hence a wavelength-dependent deviation. Option (b) is the classic wrong picture: the prism does not create or filter the colours.
The condition for an achromatic combination of two thin lenses in contact is Answer: $\dfrac{\omega_1}{f_1} + \dfrac{\omega_2}{f_2} = 0$. the two dispersions cancel while some net power survives.

For a thin prism of angle $5^{\circ}$ with $n_V = 1.52$ and $n_R = 1.50$, the angular dispersion is Answer: $0.1^{\circ}$. $\theta = (1.52-1.50)\times5^{\circ} = 0.02\times5 = 0.1^{\circ}$. Option (a) drops the factor $A$.

Spherical aberration in a lens can be reduced by Answer: using a stop to block marginal rays. spherical aberration is a geometry problem, not a colour problem, so an achromatic doublet (option a) is the answer to the other defect.
Dispersive power of a prism material depends on Answer: the material of the prism only. $\omega$ contains only refractive indices; $A$ cancels out of the ratio.
The dispersive power of the material of a prism depends on Answer: the material only. $A$ cancels in $\omega = (n_V-n_R)/(n_Y-1)$.
The condition for achromatism of two thin lenses in contact is Answer: $\dfrac{\omega_1}{f_1}+\dfrac{\omega_2}{f_2}=0$. obtained by setting $F_V = F_R$ for lenses in contact.
Chromatic aberration in a lens is caused by Answer: the dependence of refractive index on wavelength. $n_V > n_R$ makes $f_V < f_R$; it persists even with perfect surfaces.

Spherical aberration of a lens can be reduced by Answer: placing a stop to cut off marginal rays. a stop blocks the marginal rays that focus too near the lens. (Option (d) cures chromatic, not spherical, aberration.)

What is the phenomenon called when white light separates into different colors after passing through a prism? Answer: Dispersion. Dispersion is the separation of white light into its component colors by a refractive medium.

Which law states that the sine of the angle of incidence divided by the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant for a given pair of media and color of light? Answer: Snell's Law. Snell's Law defines the relationship between angles of incidence and refraction when light passes through two different mediums.
In dispersion, which color of light travels at the slowest speed through glass? Answer: Violet. Violet light has the shortest wavelength and thus travels the slowest in denser media like glass.

What term describes the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in a material? Answer: Refractive index. Refractive index is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in a given medium.
The value of $1/4\pi\varepsilon_0$ in SI units is Answer: $9\times10^{9}$. option (b) is $\varepsilon_0$ itself, which is what the $9\times10^{9}$ is built from.
The force between two point charges is inversely proportional to Answer: $r^{2}$. the inverse-square law, like gravitation.
If the distance between two charges is halved, the force between them becomes Answer: four times. $F \propto 1/r^2$, so halving $r$ multiplies $F$ by $4$. Option (b) treats the law as $1/r$.
When a charged body is brought near an uncharged conductor, the near face of the conductor acquires Answer: the opposite kind of charge. charging by induction; the far face takes the like charge.
The charge on a body is always an integral multiple of $e$. This is called Answer: quantisation of charge. no free charge smaller than $e$ has ever been isolated.

Coulomb's law in a medium of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r$ gives a force that is Answer: $1/\varepsilon_r$ times the vacuum value. the medium screens the field, so the force is always reduced.
Which of the following is not a property of electric charge? Answer: variation with speed. charge is invariant; it is the mass that changes with speed.
The number of electronic charges in one coulomb is about Answer: $6.25\times10^{18}$. $1/(1.6\times10^{-19}) = 6.25\times10^{18}$.
A body charged by induction acquires a charge Answer: of the opposite sign. electrons are driven away or attracted, leaving the opposite charge behind.
If the distance between two point charges is halved, the force between them Answer: becomes four times. $F \propto 1/r^{2}$, so halving $r$ multiplies $F$ by $4$.

The SI unit of electric field strength is Answer: both $\text{N C}^{-1}$ and $\text{V m}^{-1}$. $\text{N C}^{-1}$ and $\text{V m}^{-1}$ are the same combination of base units. Option (d) is the unit of potential.
The electric field due to an infinitely long straight charged wire varies as Answer: $1/r$. a cylindrical Gaussian surface has area $\propto r$, so $E \propto 1/r$; only a point charge gives $1/r^2$.
Two electric lines of force can never intersect because Answer: the field would then have two directions at one point. the tangent at a point gives the unique direction of $\vec E$ there.
The electric field at $3\ \text{m}$ from a point charge of $1\ \mu\text{C}$ is Answer: $1000\ \text{N C}^{-1}$. $E = 9\times10^{9}\times10^{-6}/9 = 1000\ \text{N C}^{-1}$.
For an infinitely long charged straight wire, $E$ varies with distance $r$ as Answer: $1/r$. the cylindrical Gaussian surface gives $E = \lambda/2\pi\varepsilon_0 r$.
Two electric field lines can never intersect because Answer: the field would have two directions at one point. a unique tangent means a unique field direction.

concepts.u: Potential, potential difference and potential energy
concepts.t: Electric potential is a Answer: scalar quantity. which is why potentials add algebraically while fields must be added as vectors. That single fact makes most potential problems easier than the matching field problem.

concepts.u: Potential, potential difference and potential energy
concepts.t: The potential at a distance $r$ from a point charge $Q$ varies as Answer: $1/r$. one power of $r$ less than the field, because potential is the integral of the field.

concepts.u: Potential, potential difference and potential energy
concepts.t: The potential at $0.3\ \text{m}$ from a charge of $3\ \text{nC}$ is Answer: $90\ \text{V}$. $V = 9\times10^{9}\times3\times10^{-9}/0.3 = 27/0.3 = 90\ \text{V}$.

concepts.u: Potential, potential difference and potential energy
concepts.t: At the midpoint of the line joining two equal and opposite charges, the potential and the field are respectively Answer: zero and non-zero. the two potentials cancel, but the two fields point the same way and add.
The SI unit of capacitance is the Answer: farad. one farad is one coulomb per volt, an enormous unit, which is why real capacitors are in μF and pF.

Three capacitors of $3\ \mu\text{F}$ each are joined in series. The equivalent capacitance is Answer: $1\ \mu\text{F}$. $1/C = 3/3$, so $C = 1\ \mu\text{F}$. Option (a) applies the parallel rule; capacitor combination rules are the exact mirror image of the resistor rules, and that inversion is the commonest error in this unit.
The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance $C$ charged to a potential difference $V$ is Answer: $\tfrac12CV^{2}$. the $\tfrac12$ comes from integrating $V\,dq$ as the capacitor charges up.
A $2\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is charged to $100\ \text{V}$. The energy stored is Answer: $0.01\ \text{J}$. $U = \tfrac12\times2\times10^{-6}\times100^{2} = 0.01\ \text{J}$.

A dielectric slab is inserted into a parallel-plate capacitor that stays connected to a battery. The charge on the plates Answer: increases. $V$ is held fixed by the battery and $C$ has increased, so $Q = CV$ must rise. With the battery removed the answer would be (c).
Capacitors are connected in parallel to obtain Answer: a larger capacitance. parallel adds plate area in effect. Series is used to share a high voltage.
Three capacitors each of $3\ \mu\text{F}$ are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is Answer: $1\ \mu\text{F}$. $1/C = 3/3 = 1$, so $C = 1\ \mu\text{F}$.
The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance $C$ at a p.d. $V$ is Answer: $\frac{1}{2}CV^{2}$. the area of the triangle under the $Q$–$V$ line.
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor does not depend on Answer: the charge on the plates. $C$ is fixed by geometry and medium alone.
Three resistors of $6\ \Omega$ each are joined in parallel. The equivalent resistance is Answer: $2\ \Omega$. $6/3 = 2\ \Omega$; $n$ equal resistors in parallel give $R/n$.

Two bulbs are rated $100\ \text{W}$ and $60\ \text{W}$ at the same voltage. Compared with the $60\ \text{W}$ bulb, the $100\ \text{W}$ bulb has Answer: a lower resistance. $P = V^2/R$ at fixed $V$, so more power means less resistance. Students reliably answer (a) because "brighter feels like more resistance".
Three resistors of $6\ \Omega$ each are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is Answer: $2\ \Omega$. $1/R_{eq} = 3/6$, so $R_{eq} = 2\ \Omega$.
A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting Answer: a low resistance in parallel. a low shunt in parallel carries the excess current.

A $100\ \text{W}$ and a $60\ \text{W}$ bulb, both rated $220\ \text{V}$, are joined in series across $220\ \text{V}$. Then Answer: the $60\ \text{W}$ bulb is brighter. same current in series, and $P = I^{2}R$ with $R_{60} > R_{100}$.

If two identical capacitors are connected in parallel across a battery, how does the equivalent capacitance compare to that of a single capacitor? Answer: Doubled. When identical capacitors are connected in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is the sum of the individual capacitances.

Which statement is true about the voltage drop across each resistor in a parallel circuit? Answer: It is the same across all resistors.. In a parallel circuit, the voltage drop across each branch is the same.

What happens to the total power consumed by a circuit when a second identical bulb is added in parallel to the first? Answer: Doubles.. Adding another identical bulb in parallel doubles the total current, thus doubling the power consumed if the voltage remains constant.
The radius of a nucleus of mass number $A$ is proportional to Answer: $A^{1/3}$. volume is proportional to $A$, so radius goes as the cube root.
The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei of mass number about Answer: $56$. iron and nickel, which is why both fusion below and fission above release energy.
The energy released in the fission of one uranium-235 nucleus is about Answer: $200\ \text{MeV}$. the number worth memorising for reactor numericals.
Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment established that Answer: the nucleus is small, massive and positive. large-angle scattering can only come from a concentrated positive charge.
The energy equivalent of $1\ \text{u}$ is about Answer: $931.5\ \text{MeV}$. $(1.6605\times10^{-27})c^{2} = 1.49\times10^{-10}\ \text{J} = 931.5\ \text{MeV}$.
The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei with mass number near Answer: $56$. the peak of the $B/A$ curve is ⁵⁶Fe at $8.79\ \text{MeV}$.
Two nuclides with the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called Answer: isobars. same $A$ means isobars, e.g. ⁴⁰Ar and ⁴⁰Ca.
The moderator in a nuclear reactor is used to Answer: slow down fast neutrons. slow (thermal) neutrons are captured by ²³⁵U far more readily; the control rods, not the moderator, do the absorbing.

According to which law does the half-life of a radioactive substance remain constant regardless of its initial quantity? Answer: Law of radioactive decay. The Law of radioactive decay states that the half-life of a radioactive substance remains constant and does not depend on the initial quantity of the substance.

What phenomenon is described by the equation $E = mc^2$, where $m$ is the mass defect and $c$ is the speed of light? Answer: Mass-energy equivalence. $E = mc^2$ represents the principle of mass-energy equivalence, showing that energy can be converted to mass and vice versa.
The forbidden energy gap of silicon at room temperature is about Answer: $1.1\ \text{eV}$. option (a) is germanium, the standard mix-up.

The resistance of a pure semiconductor with rising temperature Answer: decreases. more electrons are thermally excited across the gap; semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient of resistance, unlike metals.
In an extrinsic semiconductor at equilibrium Answer: $n_en_h = n_i^{2}$. the mass-action law holds for both types; option (a) is true only for an intrinsic sample.
A material with a forbidden gap greater than about $3\ \text{eV}$ behaves as Answer: an insulator. see the figure: the gap is too wide for thermal excitation at room temperature.

An n-type semiconductor crystal is Answer: electrically neutral. each donor atom contributes one electron and one fixed positive ion core, so the crystal stays neutral. Option (a) is the most popular wrong answer in this unit.
The majority charge carriers in a p-type semiconductor are Answer: holes. a trivalent dopant leaves a vacancy in the bonding, which behaves as a mobile positive carrier.
On heating a semiconductor its resistance Answer: decreases. the exponential rise in carrier number beats the extra scattering.
A pure semiconductor at $0\ \text{K}$ behaves as Answer: a perfect insulator. every covalent bond is intact, so both bands are full or empty.
In n-type silicon the phosphorus atom forms Answer: 4 covalent bonds and has 1 spare electron. silicon offers only four neighbours, so the fifth electron of P has no bond to join.
The quark composition of a proton is Answer: $uud$. $\tfrac23+\tfrac23-\tfrac13 = +1$; option (b) is the neutron, whose charges sum to zero.
A baryon is made of Answer: three quarks. protons and neutrons are the familiar examples; option (c) defines a meson.
Hubble's law states that the recession speed of a galaxy is Answer: proportional to its distance. the linear law that is the observational basis of the expanding universe.
The temperature of the cosmic microwave background radiation is about Answer: $2.7\ \text{K}$. the cooled relic of the hot early universe.
The present estimate of the age of the universe is about Answer: $13.8$ billion years. option (a) is the age of the Earth, offered to catch a hurried reader.
The neutrino belongs to the family of Answer: leptons. it feels only the weak and gravitational interactions and has no quark content.

In quantum computing, what does a qubit represent? Answer: A quantum bit that can be in superposition of 0 and 1.. A qubit is a quantum bit that can exist in a state of 0, 1, or any quantum superposition of these states.

According to the theory of relativity, which statement is true when approaching the speed of light? Answer: Time dilation occurs, meaning time appears to slow down for objects moving near the speed of light.. As an object approaches the speed of light, time dilation causes time to slow down relative to a stationary observer.

What is the significance of Bell's Theorem in quantum mechanics? Answer: It demonstrates that local hidden variable theories cannot reproduce all predictions of quantum mechanics.. Bell's Theorem shows that no local hidden variable theory can reproduce all of the predictions of quantum mechanics, supporting non-locality.
A body thrown vertically upwards has, at the highest point, Answer: zero velocity and acceleration $g$ downwards. the velocity is instantaneously zero but gravity never switches off.

Two resistors of $4\ \Omega$ and $12\ \Omega$ are joined in parallel. The equivalent resistance is Answer: $3\ \Omega$. $4\times12/16 = 3\ \Omega$; the parallel value is always smaller than the smaller resistor.
The specific latent heat of vaporisation of water is about Answer: $2.26\times10^{6}\ \text{J kg}^{-1}$. option (a) is the latent heat of fusion.
A p-type semiconductor is obtained by doping silicon with Answer: boron. boron is trivalent; the other three are pentavalent and would give n-type.

Which of the following defines the principle of conservation of momentum? Answer: Total momentum before collision equals total momentum after collision. Conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.

What does Hooke's Law describe? Answer: The relationship between the force applied to a spring and its extension. Hooke's Law describes how the force applied to a spring is directly proportional to the extension of the spring.

According to Charles's Law, what happens to the volume of a gas when its temperature is increased while keeping the pressure constant? Answer: The volume increases proportionally to the increase in temperature.. Charles's Law states that the volume of a gas increases linearly with an increase in temperature at constant pressure.

Which statement best describes the Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics? Answer: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.. The Zeroth Law defines thermal equilibrium and the concept of temperature.

What does the Second Law of Thermodynamics imply about the direction of heat transfer? Answer: Heat will spontaneously flow from a hotter body to a colder body.. The Second Law states that heat naturally flows from hot to cold objects.
What is the unit of magnetic flux density? Answer: Tesla (T). Tesla (T) is the SI unit of magnetic flux density.

According to Planck's quantum theory, the energy of a photon is directly proportional to its frequency. What is the proportionality constant in this relation? Answer: $h$. Planck's constant ($h$) is the proportionality constant in the equation $E = hf$.
What does the de Broglie hypothesis state about particles? Answer: All particles have wave properties.. De Broglie hypothesized that all particles exhibit wave-like behavior.

The uncertainty principle implies which of the following about the measurement of a particle’s properties? Answer: The more accurately we know a particle's momentum, the less accurately we can know its position.. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states there is an inherent limit to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties can be known simultaneously.
Which law describes the emission spectrum of hydrogen? Answer: Rydberg's Law. Rydberg's law predicts the wavelengths of spectral lines of various chemical elements, especially hydrogen.
A projectile has its maximum range when the angle of projection is Answer: $45^{\circ}$. $R \propto \sin2\theta$, maximum at $\theta = 45^{\circ}$.

If an object is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of $20\,ms^{-1}$, how high does it go before starting to fall back down? Answer: $20.4\,m$. At the highest point, final velocity is $0$. Using the equation $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$, we substitute $v=0$, $u=20\,ms^{-1}$, and $g=9.8\,ms^{-2}$ to find $h = \frac{u^2}{2g} = 20.4\,m$.

According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, what is the relationship between force ($F$), mass ($m$), and acceleration ($a$)? Answer: $F = ma$. Newton's Second Law states that the net force acting on an object equals the product of its mass and acceleration.

What does Hooke's Law describe? Answer: The relationship between stress and strain in elastic materials. Hooke's Law defines the linear relationship between stress and strain within the elastic limit of a material.

In the context of conservation of energy, which statement best describes the law? Answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. The law of conservation of energy asserts that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
Which equation represents Ohm's Law? Answer: $V = IR$. Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.

concepts.u: Physics: Model Question Sets and Predicted Questions
concepts.t: The maximum range of a projectile launched at $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ ($g = 10$) is Answer: $40\ \text{m}$. $R_{max} = u^{2}/g = 400/10 = 40\ \text{m}$.

concepts.u: Physics: Model Question Sets and Predicted Questions
concepts.t: Two $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitors in parallel give Answer: $12\ \mu\text{F}$. parallel capacitances add: $6 + 6 = 12$.

concepts.u: Physics: Model Question Sets and Predicted Questions
concepts.t: The minimum speed at the top of a vertical circle of radius $1.6\ \text{m}$ ($g = 10$) is Answer: $4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. $\sqrt{gr} = \sqrt{16} = 4\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
The quark composition of a neutron is Answer: $udd$. $udd$ gives $\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{3} = 0$.
Flat rotation curves of spiral galaxies are evidence for Answer: dark matter. the extra unseen mass keeps the outer stars moving fast.

What basis would you apply to distinguish a meristematic tissue from a permanent tissue? Answer: activating cell division. meristematic cells are the ones that activate cell division; option (d) describes a permanent cell, the very opposite.

Which parenchyma makes aquatic plants light and helps them to float? Answer: aerenchyma. aerenchyma has large air spaces. Stellate parenchyma is a kind of aerenchyma with star-shaped cells (banana petiole), but the general tissue that gives buoyancy is aerenchyma. Assimilatory parenchyma (chlorenchyma) is for photosynthesis.

What is the role of the endodermis in the roots of a plant? Answer: to regulate the movement of water and minerals into the root. endodermal cells with Casparian strips force water to pass through the living protoplast, so the endodermis controls what enters the stele. Option (a) is the starch sheath of a stem, a different endodermis.

What is the name of the lateral meristem responsible for secondary growth in stems? Answer: vascular cambium. the vascular cambium adds secondary xylem and phloem. Cork cambium is also a lateral meristem, but it makes periderm, not the vascular tissue that the word "stem growth" usually means; apical meristem gives primary growth only.

A botanist observes scattered vascular bundles throughout the ground tissue of a stem. What is the most appropriate conclusion? Answer: the plant is a monocot. scattered bundles in undifferentiated ground tissue are the signature of a monocot stem. Option (c) is the opposite: monocot bundles are closed.
Which tissue is dead at maturity and has a heavily lignified wall? Answer: sclerenchyma. sclerenchyma cells are dead and lignified. Collenchyma is living, parenchyma is living.
The only living component of xylem is Answer: xylem parenchyma. xylem parenchyma stores food and is alive; tracheids, vessels and fibres are dead at maturity.

A sieve tube element has no nucleus. It stays alive because of the help of Answer: companion cell. the companion cell, sister cell of the sieve element, supplies ATP and proteins. Bulliform and passage cells are in leaf and endodermis.
Casparian strips are bands of Answer: suberin on the radial and transverse walls of endodermal cells. suberin on radial and transverse walls; option (a) puts it on the epidermis, which is wrong.

Heartwood differs from sapwood because it Answer: is dead, plugged with tyloses, tannin and resin, and gives only support. heartwood is non-conducting. Option (d) describes sapwood, which is the living conducting region beneath the bark.

Which leaf has mesophyll that is not differentiated into palisade and spongy tissue? Answer: isobilateral leaf of a monocot. isobilateral leaves of monocots have similar mesophyll on both sides. Ligustrum (privet) is a dicot with a dorsiventral leaf.
Xylem and phloem lying on alternate radii is characteristic of Answer: a root. radial bundles are the defining feature of a root; stems and leaves have conjoint bundles.
The Casparian strip is found in the Answer: endodermis. the strip of suberin and lignin lies on the radial and tangential walls of the endodermis.
Bulliform cells occur in the Answer: upper epidermis of a grass leaf. large thin-walled motor cells in the upper epidermis of grasses; they lose turgor and roll the leaf.

Two cells P and Q lie in contact, separated by a semi-permeable membrane. The osmotic pressure of P is 15 atm and of Q is 12 atm; the turgor pressure of P is 10 atm and of Q is 6 atm. In which direction will water move? Answer: from P to Q. DPD of P = 15 - 10 = 5 atm, of Q = 12 - 6 = 6 atm. Water moves towards the larger DPD, so P → Q. Option (c) is the trap of comparing only the osmotic pressures or only the turgor pressures: P is larger in both, which gives a false "P is stronger" instinct. It is the difference that matters.

Which one of the following parts is not responsible for transpiration in plants? Answer: root. transpiration is loss from aerial parts; roots absorb water. Option (d) is true of transpiration, not its opposite.
A cell has an osmotic pressure of 12 atm and a turgor pressure of 8 atm. Its DPD is Answer: 4 atm. DPD = OP - TP = 12 - 8 = 4 atm. Option (a) adds instead of subtracting.
The cohesion–tension theory of the ascent of sap was proposed by Answer: Dixon and Joly. Dixon and Joly (1894). Münch proposed the pressure-flow hypothesis for phloem; Went is auxin.
Loss of liquid water from leaf margins through hydathodes at night is Answer: guttation. guttation is from hydathodes and needs root pressure. Bleeding is from a cut stem.

Stomata open in the morning because Answer: K⁺ enter the guard cells, water follows and they become turgid. in light, K⁺ and malate accumulate, the guard cells take in water and bulge, pulling the stoma open. Option (c) is the closing signal.

A plant cell is placed in a 10 % NaCl solution. The cell will Answer: become plasmolysed. the outside solution is hypertonic, water leaves, the protoplast shrinks away from the wall: plasmolysis. Bursting (a) is what animal cells do in hypotonic water.

Some C4 plants show the diagnostic feature of Kranz anatomy. Which of these plants has it? Answer: maize. maize is a C4 plant with a wreath (Kranz) of bundle-sheath cells. Wheat, barley and oats are C3 grasses, a favourite distractor set.
The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from Answer: water. photolysis of water (Hill reaction; ¹⁸O in water appears in O₂). Students pick CO₂ because it is the gas that is "used".
The reaction-centre chlorophyll a of photosystem I is Answer: P700. P700 for PS I, P680 for PS II. P870 is bacterial.
Cyclic photophosphorylation produces Answer: ATP only. electrons return to PS I, so there is no NADPH and, with no photolysis, no O₂.
For the fixation of one molecule of CO₂ in the Calvin cycle the plant needs Answer: 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. 3 ATP + 2 NADPH per CO₂, so 18 ATP and 12 NADPH for one glucose.

In a C4 plant the enzyme that first fixes CO₂ in the mesophyll cell is Answer: PEP carboxylase. PEP carboxylase, which has no affinity for O₂, fixes HCO₃⁻ into oxaloacetate; RuBisCO works later, in the bundle sheath.
The net gain of ATP from glycolysis of one glucose molecule is Answer: 2. 4 ATP made, 2 spent: net 2. Option (b) is the gross yield.

Two pea plants with red flowers, genotypes unknown, are crossed and give red and white flowers in the ratio 3: 1. What are the genotypes of the parents? Answer: both heterozygous. Rr × Rr gives 3 red: 1 white. Two homozygotes (a) or one of each (b) would give no white offspring at all.

Which of the following genetic disorders is caused by a point mutation? Answer: sickle-cell anaemia. sickle-cell anaemia is one base change (GAG → GTG), Glu → Val. Down, Turner and Klinefelter are chromosome-number changes.

In the Hershey–Chase experiment the DNA of the bacteriophage was labelled with Answer: ³²P. phosphorus is in DNA; sulphur is in protein, so ³⁵S labels the protein coat. Choosing ³⁵S is the classic slip.
A DNA sample contains 30 % adenine. The percentage of guanine is Answer: 20. A = T = 30 %, so G + C = 40 %, G = 20 %.
One complete turn of B-DNA is Answer: 3.4 nm with 10 bp. 10 bp × 0.34 nm = 3.4 nm; (d) is the diameter.

E. coli grown for many generations in ¹⁵N medium is shifted to ¹⁴N medium. After two generations of division the DNA is Answer: half hybrid and half light. the first generation is all hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N); the second is half hybrid and half light. Semi-conservative replication never gives all-heavy after a shift.
Short fragments formed on the lagging strand are joined by Answer: DNA ligase. DNA ligase seals the nicks between Okazaki fragments. Primase makes the primers; helicase unwinds.
Which of these is a stop codon? Answer: UGA. the stop codons are UAA, UAG, UGA. AUG is the start codon and also codes Met; UGG is Trp.
If the codon on the mRNA is GCA, the anticodon of the tRNA is Answer: CGU. the anticodon pairs with the codon: G–C, C–G, A–U gives CGU. Option (b) contains T, which tRNA does not have.
The enzyme that synthesises mRNA from a DNA template is Answer: RNA polymerase. transcription uses RNA polymerase; reverse transcriptase makes DNA from RNA.

The grandson of a colour-blind man can receive the gene only through Answer: his carrier mother, who got it from the colour-blind man. the colour-blind man gives his X only to his daughters; she passes it to her son (criss-cross). Option (a) is wrong because a father gives his son a Y.

Drosophila melanogaster was chosen for genetic studies mainly because it Answer: has a short life cycle, few chromosomes and many progeny. 2n = 8, a life cycle of about 10–14 days, and hundreds of offspring per mating.

Which of the following cells of an embryo sac degenerate after fertilisation? Answer: synergids and antipodal cells. synergids and antipodals have done their job and disappear; the primary endosperm cell divides to form endosperm. Option (a) is the trap: the endosperm cell is the busiest cell after fertilisation.

What is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg called? Answer: parthenogenesis. parthenogenesis is about the egg; parthenocarpy (a) is about the fruit. The two words differ by one syllable and exam setters exploit it.

In porogamy, through which structure does the pollen tube enter the ovule? Answer: micropyle. micropylar entry is porogamy. In 2082 the question was reversed: "which term describes entry through the micropyle" with options mesogamy, chalazogamy, syngamy, porogamy.

Which type of artificial vegetative propagation induces roots on a branch while it is still attached to the parent plant, and suits plants with soft branches lying near the soil? Answer: soil layering. in simple (soil) layering the branch is bent into the soil while still attached and roots then form. Air layering works on upright branches, and grafting and cutting detach the piece at once.
The number of cells and nuclei in a mature Polygonum-type embryo sac are Answer: 7 cells, 8 nuclei. seven cells but eight nuclei because the central cell carries two polar nuclei.

Double fertilisation in angiosperms was discovered by Answer: Nawaschin. Nawaschin (1898, Fritillaria and Lilium), confirmed by Guignard. Strasburger described the embryo sac and fertilisation, not the double event.

The hard outer layer of the pollen grain, resistant to acid, alkali and heat, is made of Answer: sporopollenin. sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials. Callose is found around microspore mother cells and in pollen tubes.
The nutritive layer of the anther wall that supplies food to developing pollen grains is the Answer: tapetum. the tapetum; the endothecium helps dehiscence.

Pollen grains from the anther of a flower reach the stigma of another flower of the same plant. This is Answer: geitonogamy. the flowers are on the same plant, so it is geitonogamy; it is genetically autogamy but ecologically cross-pollination. Xenogamy needs two plants.

Which feature is typical of a wind-pollinated flower? Answer: light dry pollen and feathery stigma. wind-pollinated flowers are small, dull and produce huge amounts of light dry pollen. Colour, scent and sticky pollen are insect-pollination features.
The single cotyledon of a monocot embryo is called Answer: scutellum. scutellum; coleoptile and coleorhiza are protective sheaths of the plumule and radicle.
In the dicot embryo the portion between the plumule and the radicle is the Answer: hypocotyl. the hypocotyl lies below the cotyledons and ends in the radicle; the epicotyl lies above them.
The layer of the anther wall that nourishes the developing microspores is the Answer: tapetum. the tapetum supplies food and sporopollenin; the endothecium only helps in dehiscence.
A typical angiosperm embryo sac is Answer: 7-celled and 8-nucleate. 3 antipodals + 2 synergids + 1 egg + 1 central cell with 2 nuclei = 7 cells, 8 nuclei.

In an economically important plant species embryo mortality is very high. Which method would you suggest to check the mortality? Answer: embryo culture. embryo culture rescues weak or aborting embryos by growing them on medium. Meristem culture (d) gives virus-free plants, a different aim.
Who proposed the concept of totipotency of plant cells? Answer: Haberlandt. Gottlieb Haberlandt (1902). Skoog and Miller found kinetin; Murashige and Skoog gave the medium.

A high concentration of cytokinin relative to auxin in the medium promotes Answer: shoot formation. high cytokinin: auxin → shoots; the reverse → roots; a balance → callus. Reversing the ratio is the usual error.
Virus-free plants are obtained by culturing Answer: shoot-tip meristem. the apical meristem is usually free of virus because it has no vascular connection.
Haploid plants are produced in the laboratory by Answer: anther culture. anther (or pollen) culture gives haploids, which doubling then turns into homozygous diploids.
Somatic hybrids are produced by the fusion of Answer: two protoplasts from different species. protoplast fusion bypasses sexual barriers (pomato). Fusion of gametes is ordinary fertilisation.
The first generation of a cross between two pure lines often grows better than both parents. This is called Answer: heterosis. heterosis or hybrid vigour; inbreeding depression is the opposite.
The cry gene in Bt cotton comes from Answer: Bacillus thuringiensis. the cry gene codes Cry protein, toxic to bollworm. Agrobacterium supplies the vector, which is why (a) tempts.
A common vector used to introduce a foreign gene into a dicot plant is Answer: the Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium. the Ti plasmid transfers T-DNA into dicot cells.
The enzyme that cuts DNA at specific base sequences is Answer: restriction endonuclease. restriction endonuclease; ligase joins, it does not cut.
Which of the following is used as a green manure crop in Nepal? Answer: Sesbania. Sesbania (dhaincha) is ploughed in while green; wheat and maize are grain crops.
Azolla is used as a biofertiliser because it lives with a nitrogen-fixing Answer: Anabaena. Azolla fixes nitrogen through Anabaena azollae. Rhizobium lives in legume nodules.
Golden Rice was developed to overcome the deficiency of Answer: vitamin A. Golden Rice makes β-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A.
Food that is free from toxins and disease-causing organisms is a matter of Answer: food safety. safety is about hazards; security (a) is about availability and access.

Which of the following tissues possesses fat globules? Answer: adipose tissue. adipose tissue stores fat globules. Areolar tissue (a) is the commoner distractor because it is also loose and sits beside fat.
Which of the following tissues lacks a blood supply? Answer: cartilage. cartilage is avascular and is fed by diffusion from the perichondrium. Bone (c) has Haversian canals full of vessels.

Which pair of white blood cells contains phagocytic cells? Answer: monocytes and neutrophils. neutrophils and monocytes (which become macrophages) are the professional phagocytes; eosinophils are weakly phagocytic, lymphocytes are not.

Which epithelium forms the inner lining of the vagina? Answer: stratified non-keratinised squamous. the vagina is a moist internal passage, so its stratified squamous epithelium is non-keratinised. Keratinised squamous (c) is the epidermis.
Which epithelium lines the air sacs (alveoli) of the lung? Answer: simple squamous. a single flat layer keeps the diffusion distance small. Cuboidal lines kidney tubules.
The epithelium that can stretch when the urinary bladder is filled is Answer: transitional. transitional epithelium lets the cells slide over one another.

Tendon and ligament are both Answer: dense regular connective tissue. both are dense regular connective tissue rich in collagen; they differ in what they join. Fibrocartilage (d) is found in the disc.
A ligament connects Answer: bone to bone. ligament is bone to bone; tendon is muscle to bone (option a).
The cartilage in the external ear (pinna) is Answer: elastic. elastic cartilage springs back; hyaline is at the articular ends and trachea.
The cells of bone that lie in lacunae are Answer: osteocytes. osteocytes sit in lacunae. Osteoblasts make matrix and become osteocytes; chondrocytes belong to cartilage.
Muscle fibres that are striated and branched and join end to end through intercalated discs are Answer: cardiac. cardiac muscle. Skeletal fibres are long, unbranched and multinucleate.

The fatty insulating sheath around an axon in peripheral nerves is formed by Answer: Schwann cells. Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system; oligodendrocytes do the same in the central nervous system.
The type of cell that makes up about 99 % of the formed elements of blood is Answer: RBC. red cells outnumber white cells by about 600: 1.

Squamous epithelium is also called pavement epithelium because Answer: its flat cells fit edge to edge like paving stones. flat cells, tightly joined, resemble a paved floor. The word has nothing to do with a pavement outside.

What are the sequential steps involved in gametogenesis? Answer: multiplication, growth, maturation. multiplication, growth, maturation. Option (c) puts growth first; it is tempting because in ordinary life "growth" precedes "maturity".

In the frog, the coelom is derived from which embryonic layer? Answer: mesoderm. the coelom is a mesodermal cavity (it forms by a split in the mesoderm). Mesogloea (d) is a jelly layer of cnidarians, not a germ layer.

What happens during spermiogenesis in spermatogenesis? Answer: spermatozoa form from spermatids. spermiogenesis is the conversion of a spermatid into a spermatozoon (no division). Options (a)–(c) are the division steps of the multiplication and maturation phases.

Which is the correct sequence of embryonic development in a frog? Answer: morula, blastula, gastrula. morula → blastula → gastrula. The blastula follows the morula because the cavity forms inside the solid ball.
Immediately after fertilisation, a frog zygote undergoes Answer: cleavage. cleavage is the first series of mitoses, without growth. Gastrulation comes several stages later.
One primary spermatocyte gives rise to Answer: four sperms. meiosis I and II give four haploid spermatids, each becoming a sperm.
One primary oocyte finally gives rise to Answer: one ovum and three polar bodies. oogenesis is unequal: one large ovum and three small polar bodies.
In humans the secondary oocyte is arrested at Answer: metaphase II. the secondary oocyte stops at metaphase II and completes meiosis only after the sperm enters.

The cleavage of a frog egg is holoblastic and unequal because Answer: the yolk is concentrated in the vegetal half and slows division there. yolk slows the cleavage furrows, so vegetal cells are larger. Microlecithal (c) means little yolk.
The cavity of the blastula is called Answer: blastocoel. blastocoel is the cavity of the blastula; archenteron belongs to the gastrula.
The cavity formed inside the embryo during gastrulation is the Answer: archenteron. the archenteron becomes the gut. Students confuse it with the blastocoel, which it gradually replaces.
The nervous system of the frog develops from Answer: ectoderm. the neural plate, then the neural tube, arises from ectoderm; the notochord is mesodermal and induces it.
Metamorphosis of a frog tadpole into an adult is controlled by Answer: thyroxine. thyroxine from the thyroid; if the gland is removed, tadpoles remain tadpoles.
Fertilisation in the frog is Answer: external, in water. the male clasps the female (amplexus) and sperm are shed over the eggs in water.

Which enzyme is needed for the digestion of milk protein in human beings? Answer: rennin. rennin curdles casein in infants; lactase (b) digests the milk sugar, which is the trap. Pepsin also acts on protein but the classic milk-protein answer is rennin.

If the cerebellum of a person is injured, which physiological function is affected? Answer: body movement. the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance. Respiration belongs to the medulla, memory to the cerebrum, smell to the olfactory bulb.

The vas deferens carries spermatozoa from the cauda epididymis to the ejaculatory duct. What happens if it is surgically disconnected? Answer: seminal fluid is without sperms. sperms are still made and still stored, so the semen carries none; the fluid from the seminal vesicles and prostate still comes. Option (d) is wrong because spermatogenesis goes on in the testis.

In the middle ear of a human being there are three ear ossicles. Which set is arranged in the correct sequence? Answer: malleus, incus, stapes. malleus, incus, stapes from the tympanum inward. The cochlea and saccule are not ossicles.

Pancreas is a gland with exocrine and endocrine functions; its exocrine part is the pancreatic acini. What is the endocrine part? Answer: islets of Langerhans. the islets of Langerhans make insulin and glucagon. Zona glomerulosa and zona reticularis are adrenal cortex layers, adenohypophysis is the anterior pituitary.

Show the correct path of origin and conduction of the heart beat in the human heart. Answer: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres. SA node (pacemaker) → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres.

Which enzymes are likely to act in order on soyabean sprouts eaten by a man as they move down the alimentary canal? Answer: pepsin, trypsin, peptidases. pepsin (stomach) → trypsin (duodenum) → peptidases (intestinal brush border). Reversing the stomach and the intestine gives (b)–(d).

What would happen if the frontal lobe of the cerebrum were accidentally damaged? Answer: loss of memory and learning. the frontal lobe handles thinking, planning and memory. Option (a) is the occipital and temporal lobes; (b) the medulla; (c) the hypothalamus.

What is the primary role of a surrogate mother in the context of IVF? Answer: to carry the pregnancy to full term. a gestational surrogate carries the embryo to term. Donating ova is the role of an egg donor, and fertilisation happens in the laboratory.

What would happen if the oxyntic cells of the gastric glands became non-functional? Answer: protein digestion does not take place. oxyntic (parietal) cells make the HCl; without it pepsinogen is not converted to active pepsin and the acidity needed for protein digestion in the stomach is lost. Option (d) is the nearest distractor: the chief cells still release pepsinogen, so the real failure is activation, not secretion.
Show the correct path for the flow of urine. Answer: renal pelvis, ureter, urinary bladder, urethra. pelvis → ureter → bladder → urethra. The bladder lies between the ureter and the urethra.

A person has a puffy appearance, a moon face, low body temperature and intolerance to cold. What is he suffering from? Answer: myxoedema. myxoedema is adult hypothyroidism: puffy face, cold intolerance, low metabolic rate. Graves' is hyperthyroidism. Hashimoto's is an autoimmune cause of hypothyroidism, but the puffy-face description is the textbook picture of myxoedema.

What is the substance sampled during amniocentesis? Answer: amniotic fluid. a needle takes amniotic fluid to test for chromosome and gene disorders. Placental cells are sampled in chorionic villus sampling.
After digestion in the duodenum, the fat-rich milky fluid absorbed into the lacteals is called Answer: chyle. chyle. Chyme is the acidic food mass leaving the stomach, bolus is the swallowed mass.

When an organ transplantation occurs between two genetically identical individuals, what is the type of transplantation? Answer: isograft. genetically identical individuals (identical twins) give an isograft. Autograft (a) is from the same individual, allograft (b) from the same species, heterograft (c) from another species.

Overpopulation has adverse consequences in society. Which of the following can control it? Answer: family planning. family planning controls birth. Early marriage and polygamy raise births; food supply supports growth.

Which organ transplant has the lowest risk of rejection because the tissue lacks blood vessels? Answer: cornea. the cornea has no blood vessels and sits behind the immune system's surveillance; rejection is rare.
The movement of individuals into a population from outside, which increases its size, is Answer: immigration. immigration increases and emigration decreases the population; natality is births only.

A population has 1000 individuals. In a year there are 40 births, 10 deaths, 5 immigrants and 15 emigrants. The net increase is Answer: 20. births - deaths = 30; immigration - emigration = -10; net = 30 + (-10) = 20. Option (b) forgets the net migration.
A population pyramid with a broad base and a narrow top represents Answer: an expanding population. a broad base means many young people: an expanding population. A narrow base would be declining.
The skin graft transferred from one part of the body of a burn patient to another part is an Answer: autograft. same individual, so an autograft; no immune rejection.
HIV mainly destroys Answer: CD4 helper T cells. HIV binds CD4 on helper T cells; as they fall, infections take over.
The vector of the malaria parasite is Answer: female Anopheles. the female Anopheles bites at night; the male feeds on plant juices. Aedes carries dengue.
The antibodies received by a baby through breast milk give Answer: natural passive immunity. antibodies come ready-made from the mother (natural) and the baby made none (passive).
Kwashiorkor is caused by the deficiency of Answer: protein. protein deficiency with adequate energy gives oedema and a swollen belly; marasmus is protein and energy lack.
Which is the most common reason for adolescents to start smoking? Answer: peer pressure. peer pressure; the question type also appears as a planning task (see the subjective chapter).
The definitive host of the malarial parasite is Answer: female Anopheles. fertilisation and sporogony occur in the female Anopheles.
AIDS is diagnosed when the CD4⁺ T-cell count falls below Answer: 200 mm⁻³. below 200 cells mm⁻³ the patient is defined as having AIDS.

Which one of the following sets contains bacterial diseases only? Answer: tuberculosis, typhoid, cholera. tuberculosis, typhoid and cholera are all bacterial. Candidiasis is a fungal disease and hepatitis and influenza are viral, so every other option hides one wrong member.

Which pair of diseases is spread through contaminated food and water? Answer: typhoid and cholera. typhoid and cholera spread by the faeco-oral route. Tuberculosis and influenza are airborne; candidiasis is fungal.
The indigenous honeybee of Nepal, kept in log and box hives, is Answer: Apis cerana. Apis cerana is the hive bee of Nepal's hills. A. mellifera is the introduced European bee.
In a honeybee colony, drones develop from Answer: unfertilised eggs. drones are haploid, from unfertilised eggs (parthenogenesis); queen and workers are diploid.
A larva becomes a queen bee because it is fed throughout on Answer: royal jelly. royal jelly for the whole larval life makes a queen; workers get it only for the first days.
The silkworm Bombyx mori is fed on the leaves of Answer: mulberry. mulberry (Morus). Castor feeds the eri silkworm.
The two proteins of the raw silk thread are Answer: fibroin and sericin. fibroin forms the thread and sericin glues it.

In composite fish culture catla, rohu and mrigal are stocked together because they Answer: feed at different depths of the pond. catla is a surface feeder, rohu a column feeder, mrigal a bottom feeder, so they use the whole pond without competing.
The earthworm commonly used for vermicomposting is Answer: Eisenia fetida. Eisenia fetida (red wiggler) is an epigeic composting worm. Pheretima is a burrower.
Lac is obtained from Answer: Kerria lacca. the lac insect Kerria lacca secretes lac on twigs.
The causative organism of typhoid is Answer: Salmonella typhi. Salmonella typhi. Vibrio cholerae causes cholera.
The test used for the diagnosis of typhoid is Answer: Widal test. Widal detects antibodies to S. typhi antigens; Mantoux is for TB.
The first line of treatment of dehydration in cholera is Answer: oral rehydration solution. ORS replaces water and salts; antibiotics are secondary.

The equivalent weight of H₃PO₃ in the reaction 2NaOH + H₃PO₃ → Na₂HPO₃ + 2H₂O is Answer: 41. H₃PO₃ is dibasic, and here both replaceable H are used (Na₂HPO₃), so E = 82/2 = 41. Option (a) forgets to divide; (c) divides by 3 because the formula has three H, but one of them is bonded to P and is not acidic.

The normality of a 5 % (w/v) Na₂CO₃ solution, taking Na₂CO₃ as a dibasic base of molar mass 106, is Answer: 0.94 N. 5 g per 100 mL = 50 g L⁻¹; equivalent weight = 106/2 = 53; N = 50/53 = 0.94. Option (c) is the molarity (50/106), which forgets the n-factor, and (d) doubles the n-factor.

For the titration of H₂SO₄ against Na₂CO₃ the indicator to be recommended is Answer: methyl orange. Na₂CO₃ is a weak base; at complete neutralisation the solution holds H₂CO₃ (pH about 4), which methyl orange signals. Phenolphthalein changes colour at the half-way stage, NaHCO₃, so it would give a wrong end point.

The equivalent weight of K₂Cr₂O₇ (M = 294) acting as an oxidising agent in acidic medium is Answer: 49. Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O takes six electrons, so E = 294/6 = 49. Option (b) uses three electrons, the n-factor of dilute-acid reduction of a different oxidant.
The equivalent weight of KMnO₄ (M = 158) in acidic medium is Answer: 31.6. MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, so E = 158/5 = 31.6. Option (c) is the neutral-medium value (three electrons).

A liquor ammonia sample is 25 % (w/w) NH₃ and has specific gravity 0.91. Its molarity is Answer: 13.4 M. M = (10 × 0.91 × 25)/17 = 227.5/17 = 13.4 mol L⁻¹. Option (d) uses 34 as the molar mass, which is 2 × 17.

100 cc of N/2 HCl, 20 cc of N/10 HNO₃ and 50 cc of N/5 H₂SO₄ are mixed. The pH of the mixture is about Answer: 0.44. equivalents = 100 × 0.5 + 20 × 0.1 + 50 × 0.2 = 50 + 2 + 10 = 62 milli-equivalents in 170 mL, so N = 0.3647 and pH = -log 0.3647 = 0.44. Option (c) is the pH if the volumes were forgotten and the three normalities were simply averaged.

3.15 g of oxalic acid crystals (H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O) are dissolved to make 500 mL of solution. Its normality is Answer: 0.10 N. E = 126/2 = 63; N = (3.15/63)/0.5 = 0.05/0.5 = 0.10 N. Option (a) forgets that the volume is 0.5 L, not 1 L.

In the titration of oxalic acid against KMnO₄ in acidic medium the indicator is Answer: KMnO₄ itself. one drop of excess MnO₄⁻ makes the solution permanently pink, so KMnO₄ is a self-indicator. The solution is warmed to about 60–70 °C because the first reaction is slow at room temperature, and dilute H₂SO₄ supplies the H⁺ the half-reaction needs.

25.0 mL of 0.100 N HCl exactly neutralises 20.0 mL of NaOH solution. The normality of the alkali is Answer: 0.125 N. N₁V₁ = N₂V₂ gives N₂ = (0.100 × 25.0)/20.0 = 0.125 N. Option (a) inverts the ratio of the volumes.
The equivalent weight of KMnO₄ in acidic medium is Answer: 31.6. MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons, so $E = 158/5 = 31.6$.
Which of the following is a primary standard substance? Answer: K₂Cr₂O₇. K₂Cr₂O₇ is pure, non-hygroscopic, stable and of high equivalent weight.
The concentration unit that does not change with temperature is Answer: molality. molality uses the mass of solvent, and mass does not expand on heating.
A 0.1 M solution of H₂SO₄ is the same as Answer: 0.2 N. $N = M \times n = 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2$ N.

Equal volumes of 1 M NaNO₃ and 1 M KCl are mixed. The concentration of nitrate ions in the mixture is Answer: 0.5 M. mixing doubles the volume and NaNO₃ is diluted from 1 M to 0.5 M. Neither KCl nor the spectator ions contribute nitrate. Option (c) forgets the dilution.

The ionic product of water at 393 K is Answer: greater than 1 × 10⁻¹⁴. ionisation of water is endothermic, so Kw rises with temperature (about 3.8 × 10⁻¹³ at 100 °C). Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ is valid only at 25 °C.

The solubility product of chalk (CaCO₃, M = 100) is 9.3 × 10⁻⁸. Its solubility is about Answer: 3.05 × 10⁻² g L⁻¹. s = √(9.3 × 10⁻⁸) = 3.05 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹; multiplying by M = 100 gives 3.05 × 10⁻² g L⁻¹. Option (a) stops at mol L⁻¹.
A buffer contains 0.2 M ethanoic acid and 0.1 M sodium ethanoate (pKa = 4.74). Its pH is Answer: 4.44. pH = 4.74 + log(0.1/0.2) = 4.74 - 0.30 = 4.44. Option (b) inverts the ratio of salt to acid.
The conjugate base of H₂PO₄⁻ is Answer: HPO₄²⁻. the conjugate base is formed by removing one proton: H₂PO₄⁻ → HPO₄²⁻ + H⁺. Option (a) is the conjugate acid.

Equal volumes of 2 × 10⁻⁴ M BaCl₂ and 2 × 10⁻⁴ M Na₂SO₄ are mixed (Ksp of BaSO₄ = 1 × 10⁻¹⁰). A precipitate Answer: forms, because the ionic product is 1 × 10⁻⁸. after mixing, [Ba²⁺] = [SO₄²⁻] = 1 × 10⁻⁴ M, so Qsp = 10⁻⁸ > 10⁻¹⁰ and BaSO₄ precipitates. Option (b) forgets to halve each concentration.
The aqueous solution of sodium ethanoate is Answer: alkaline. CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻; the salt of a weak acid and a strong base hydrolyses to an alkaline solution.
The conjugate base of HSO₄⁻ is Answer: SO₄²⁻. removing one proton from HSO₄⁻ leaves SO₄²⁻.
Which of the following is a Lewis acid but not a Bronsted acid? Answer: BF₃. BF₃ has no proton to donate but an empty p orbital to accept a lone pair.
The pH of a 0.001 M solution of NaOH at 25 °C is Answer: 11. $pOH = -\log 10^{-3} = 3$, so $pH = 14 - 3 = 11$.
On dilution, the degree of ionisation of a weak electrolyte Answer: increases. Ostwald's law, $\alpha = \sqrt{K/C}$, and $C$ falls on dilution.
An aqueous solution of ammonium chloride is Answer: acidic. NH₄⁺ hydrolyses to give H⁺ (salt of strong acid + weak base).
The indicator most suitable for the titration of acetic acid against sodium hydroxide is Answer: phenolphthalein. the equivalence pH is about 8.7, inside the phenolphthalein range 8.3–10.0.
What is the pH of a 0.1 M solution of a strong acid HA in water? Answer: 1.0. The pH is calculated as -log[HA] for a strong acid, which equals 1 when [HA] = 0.1 M.
