F₁ self: gametes T, t from each parent; Punnett square gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt. F₂: 3 tall: 1 dwarf, genotypic ratio 1: 2: 1.

In a dihybrid cross of RrYy × RrYy, find the phenotypic ratio. If there are 800 offspring, how many are wrinkled green? Model answer: 9 round yellow: 3 round green: 3 wrinkled yellow: 1 wrinkled green. Wrinkled green = 1/16 × 800 = 50.

Differentiate between voluntary and reflex actions. Model answer: A voluntary action is controlled by the cerebrum and is done by will (writing). A reflex action is rapid, involuntary and controlled by the spinal cord (withdrawing a hand from a hot pan).
Name two hormones and the glands that secrete them. Model answer: Insulin from the pancreas; thyroxine from the thyroid gland (also adrenaline from the adrenal gland).

Describe the path of blood through the human heart, naming the four chambers and the main vessels. Model answer: Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium from the vena cava, passes to the right ventricle, then through the pulmonary artery to the lungs. Oxygenated blood returns by the pulmonary vein to the left atrium, goes to the left ventricle and is pumped to the body through the aorta. Valves keep the flow in one direction.

Explain how the kidney removes waste from the blood. Model answer: Blood enters each kidney by the renal artery. In each nephron, the glomerulus filters water, glucose, salts and urea into the Bowman's capsule. As the filtrate passes along the tubule, useful substances (all glucose, most water and salts) are reabsorbed into the blood. The remaining water, urea and excess salts form ur

What is a reflex action? Give two examples. Model answer: A reflex action is a quick, automatic response to a stimulus controlled by the spinal cord without thinking. Examples: pulling the hand from a hot object; blinking.
Why is the pituitary called the master gland? Model answer: It controls the work of many other endocrine glands (thyroid, adrenal, gonads) through its hormones.

Differentiate between an artery and a vein (two points). Model answer: An artery carries blood away from the heart; its wall is thick and it has no valves. A vein carries blood to the heart; its wall is thin and it has valves.

Define homeostasis. How does sweating help in homeostasis? Model answer: Homeostasis is the keeping of a constant internal environment. Sweat evaporates from the skin and takes heat from the body, so the temperature stays near 37 °C.

Draw and label a neuron. Describe the path of a reflex arc. Model answer: Neuron: dendrites, cell body with nucleus, axon with myelin sheath, axon terminals. Reflex arc: stimulus → receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord (relay neuron) → motor neuron → effector (muscle) → response.

Describe the 28-day menstrual cycle. Model answer: Days 1–5: menstruation. Days 6–13: the uterus lining rebuilds and an egg ripens under FSH and oestrogen. Day 14: ovulation. Days 15–28: the lining thickens under progesterone; if there is no fertilisation, hormone levels fall and menstruation begins again.

A person's heart beats 75 times per minute and pumps 68 mL per beat. Calculate the cardiac output in litres per minute and the blood pumped in one hour. Model answer: Cardiac output = 75 × 68 = 5,100 mL = 5.1 L per minute. In one hour: 5.1 × 60 = 306 litres.

Explain how urine is formed in the nephron. Model answer: Ultrafiltration of blood in the glomerulus to Bowman's capsule (about 180 L/day); selective reabsorption of glucose, water, amino acids and salts in the tubule; tubular secretion of extra wastes. The remaining fluid is urine (about 1.5 L/day), sent to the bladder via the ureter.

Describe how blood sugar is kept constant in the body. Model answer: When blood sugar rises after a meal, the pancreas releases insulin and the liver stores glucose as glycogen. When blood sugar falls, the pancreas releases glucagon and the liver turns glycogen into glucose. This is negative feedback; lack of insulin causes diabetes.
Write two measures to reduce solid waste at home. Model answer: Follow the 3R principle: reduce use of single-use plastics, reuse containers and bags, and compost kitchen waste.

What is acid rain? Write its causes, two harmful effects and two preventive measures. Model answer: Acid rain is rain with a pH below 5.6. Cause: sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen from factories, vehicles and burning coal dissolve in rain to form sulphuric and nitric acids. Effects: it damages buildings and statues, harms crops and forests, and acidifies lakes so fish die. Prevention: use low-sulphur fuel, insta

Describe the causes and effects of ozone layer depletion. Model answer: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays. CFCs from old refrigerators, air-conditioners and aerosol sprays rise to the stratosphere; ultraviolet light breaks them to release chlorine, which destroys ozone. Effects: more UV reaches Earth, causing skin cancer and eye cataracts, reducing crop yield and h

Define ecosystem and food chain. Model answer: An ecosystem is a community of living things interacting with each other and with the non-living environment. A food chain is the sequence of organisms in which each is eaten by the next, so that energy passes along.
What is the greenhouse effect? Name two greenhouse gases. Model answer: The trapping of the Earth's heat by gases in the atmosphere, which keeps the Earth warm. Two gases: carbon dioxide and methane.

Differentiate between in-situ and ex-situ conservation with one example each. Model answer: In-situ: protecting the species in its natural home, e.g. Chitwan National Park. Ex-situ: protecting outside its home, e.g. the Central Zoo.

Explain the causes, effects and control of air pollution. Model answer: Causes: vehicle smoke, brick kilns, factories, burning of waste, dust, firewood smoke. Effects: asthma, lung disease, eye irritation, acid rain, smog, global warming, damage to crops and buildings. Control: public and electric vehicles, vehicle testing, clean stoves and biogas, filters on chimneys, tree planting, ban o

What is global warming? Describe its causes and four effects. Model answer: Global warming is the rise of the average temperature of the Earth due to the increase of greenhouse gases. Causes: burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture (methane, nitrous oxide), CFCs. Effects: glaciers melt; sea level rises; floods and droughts; harm to crops and biodiversity; spread of diseases.

In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle, 50,000 kJ of energy is stored in the grass. Find the energy received by the snake and by the eagle. Draw an energy pyramid. Model answer: Grasshopper = 10% of 50,000 = 5,000 kJ; frog = 500 kJ; snake = 50 kJ; eagle = 5 kJ. Pyramid: widest base grass (50,000), then grasshopper (5,000), frog (500), snake (50), top eagle (5).

Describe the methods of waste management that can be used at home and in the community. Model answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle; segregate waste at source into biodegradable, recyclable and hazardous; compost kitchen waste or use vermicompost; make biogas from dung and kitchen waste; sanitary landfill for the remaining waste; avoid open burning; treat sewage; e-waste to authorised recyclers.

State Newton's third law of motion with an example. Model answer: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, and they act on different bodies. Example: a rocket pushes gases down and the gases push the rocket up.

Find the weight of a 50 kg body on Earth ($g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$) and on the Moon ($g=1.67\ \text{m s}^{-2}$). Model answer: Earth: $W=mg=50\times10=500$ N. Moon: $W=50\times1.67=83.5$ N. (Mass stays 50 kg.)

A car of mass 1500 kg accelerates uniformly from rest to $20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ in 10 s. Find the acceleration and the force acting on it. Model answer: $a=\dfrac{v-u}{t}=\dfrac{20-0}{10}=2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. $F=ma=1500\times2=3000$ N.

A bullet of mass 20 g is fired from a gun of mass 4 kg with a velocity of $300\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the recoil velocity of the gun and state the principle used. Model answer: Principle: conservation of linear momentum. Total momentum before firing is zero, so $m_1v_1+m_2v_2=0$.

Why do passengers fall forward when a moving bus stops suddenly? Model answer: The passengers' bodies are moving with the bus. When the bus stops, the feet stop with the floor, but the upper body keeps moving forward because of inertia of motion.

State Newton's third law and give one example. Model answer: To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Example: when a gun fires a bullet forward, the bullet pushes the gun backward (recoil).
Define momentum. What is its SI unit? Model answer: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity, $p = mv$. Unit: kg m s⁻¹.

Differentiate between mass and weight (any two points). Model answer: Mass is the quantity of matter and is measured in kg; weight is the force of gravity on the body and is measured in N. Mass is constant everywhere; weight changes with $g$.

Why does a cricketer pull his hands back while catching a fast ball? Model answer: Pulling back the hands increases the time of stopping the ball. Since $F = \Delta p / t$, a longer time means a smaller force on the hands, so they do not get hurt.

A force of 30 N acts on a body of mass 6 kg for 4 s. Starting from rest, find Model answer: (a) $a = F/m = 30/6 = 5$ m s⁻². (b) $v = u + at = 0 + 5 \times 4 = 20$ m s⁻¹. (c) $p = mv = 6 \times 20 = 120$ kg m s⁻¹ (also $Ft = 30 \times 4 = 120$ N s).

A bullet of mass 25 g leaves a rifle of mass 5 kg at 400 m s⁻¹. Calculate the recoil velocity of the rifle. Model answer: $m_b = 0.025$ kg. Momentum is conserved: $0 = 0.025 \times 400 + 5 v$, so $v = -10/5 = -2$ m s⁻¹. The rifle recoils at 2 m s⁻¹.

State Newton's law of gravitation and derive an expression for the acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface. Model answer: Law: $F = Gm_1m_2/d^2$ (state in words). Derivation: pull of the Earth on mass $m$ is $GMm/R^2$; this equals $mg$; cancelling $m$ gives $g = GM/R^2$.

A ball is thrown upward with a velocity of 30 m s⁻¹ ($g = 10$ m s⁻²). Find the maximum height it reaches and the time taken to return to the thrower. Model answer: $H = u^2/2g = 900/20 = 45$ m. Time up $= u/g = 3$ s; total time $= 6$ s.

Why does a nail with a sharp point go into wood more easily than a blunt one? Model answer: The pointed tip has a very small area, so for the same force the pressure ($P=F/A$) is much greater and the nail penetrates.

In a hydraulic press, the small piston has an area of 5 cm² and the large piston 500 cm². A force of 100 N is applied to the small piston. Find the force on the large piston. Model answer: By Pascal's law, $\dfrac{F_1}{A_1}=\dfrac{F_2}{A_2}$, so $F_2=F_1\dfrac{A_2}{A_1}=100\times\dfrac{500}{5}=10\,000$ N.

A block of volume $0.002\ \text{m}^3$ is completely immersed in water ($\rho=1000\ \text{kg m}^{-3}$). Find the upthrust. If the block weighs 30 N in air, what is its apparent weight in water? Model answer: Upthrust $=V\rho g=0.002\times1000\times10=20$ N. Apparent weight $=30-20=10$ N.

State Pascal's law. Write one application. Model answer: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions. Application: the hydraulic jack (or hydraulic brake).

Why does a nail have a pointed tip and a broad head? Model answer: The pointed tip has a very small area, so a small force gives a large pressure that helps it enter the wood. The broad head has a large area, so the pressure on the hand is small and does not hurt.
Why does the pressure of the atmosphere decrease with height? Model answer: The column of air above becomes shorter and the air becomes thinner, so there is less weight of air above.

A box weighing 400 N rests on a floor with a contact area of 0.5 m². Calculate the pressure it exerts. If it is turned to rest on a face of area 0.2 m², what is the new pressure? Model answer: $P_1 = 400/0.5 = 800$ Pa. $P_2 = 400/0.2 = 2000$ Pa. The pressure is larger on the smaller area.
Derive the expression $P = h\rho g$ for the pressure at a depth in a liquid. Model answer: See the derivation box: volume $Ah$, mass $\rho Ah$, weight $\rho Ahg$, divide by $A$ to get $P = h\rho g$.

The areas of the small and large pistons of a hydraulic press are 10 cm² and 1000 cm². A force of 50 N is applied to the small piston. Find Model answer: (a) $F = f \times A/a = 50 \times 1000/10 = 5000$ N. (b) Mechanical advantage $= 1000/10 = 100$.

A solid cube of side 10 cm and mass 0.5 kg is placed in water. Will it float or sink? Find the upthrust when it floats. ($\rho_w = 1000$ kg m⁻³, $g = 10$ m s⁻².) Model answer: Volume $= (0.1)^3 = 0.001$ m³. Density $= 0.5/0.001 = 500$ kg m⁻³, which is less than 1000, so it floats. Upthrust = weight $= 0.5 \times 10 = 5$ N. Half the cube is under water.
Define specific heat capacity and write its SI unit. Model answer: Specific heat capacity is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C (or 1 K). Unit: J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

Why does water in a pond freeze from the top while the bottom stays at about 4 °C? Model answer: Water is densest at 4 °C. On cooling, water above 4 °C sinks until the whole pond reaches 4 °C; below 4 °C the cooler water becomes lighter and stays on top, so ice forms at the surface while the bottom stays near 4 °C.
Define specific heat capacity and state its SI unit. Model answer: It is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C (or 1 K). Unit: J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Why are gaps left between railway rails? Model answer: Rails expand in hot weather. Gaps give room to expand freely; otherwise they would bend and damage the track.

Why does the sea breeze blow during the day? Model answer: Land has a lower specific heat capacity, so it gets hot faster than the sea. Air over the land rises and cool air from the sea moves in to take its place.
Why do we wear white clothes in summer? Model answer: White surfaces reflect most of the heat and absorb little, so we stay cooler.

Why does a steam burn hurt more than a burn from boiling water at the same temperature? Model answer: Steam at 100 °C gives out its latent heat of vaporisation (2.26×10⁶ J kg⁻¹) when it condenses on the skin, in addition to the heat from cooling, so it supplies much more heat.

Explain the anomalous expansion of water and state its importance for aquatic life. Model answer: On heating from 0 °C to 4 °C water contracts; above 4 °C it expands. So its density is maximum at 4 °C. In a cold lake, 4 °C water sinks to the bottom and colder water stays on top and freezes. The ice layer insulates the water below, which stays at about 4 °C, so fish survive.

Compare conduction, convection and radiation with an example of each. Model answer: Use the comparison table: conduction in solids (iron rod), convection in fluids (sea breeze, boiling water), radiation without a medium (sunlight).

Differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves. Model answer: In a transverse wave the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of the wave (light, waves on a string). In a longitudinal wave they vibrate parallel to it (sound).

State the laws of reflection of light. Model answer: (i) The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. (ii) The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence lie in the same plane.

A ship sends an ultrasonic pulse towards the sea bed and receives the echo after 0.8 s. If the speed of sound in sea water is $1500\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, find the depth of the sea. Model answer: The pulse travels down and back, so the distance is $2d=vt$:

An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the image distance and the magnification. Model answer: Using $\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{u}+\dfrac{1}{v}$ with real distances positive: $\dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{10}-\dfrac{1}{30}=\dfrac{3-1}{30}=\dfrac{1}{15}$, so $v=15$ cm (a real image beyond the lens). Magnification $m=\dfrac{v}{u}=\dfrac{15}{30}=0.5$, so the image is real, inverted and half the size.
Why can sound not travel in a vacuum? Model answer: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs particles to pass the vibration on. A vacuum has no particles.

What is total internal reflection? Write its two conditions. Model answer: Complete reflection of light back into a denser medium at its boundary with a rarer one. Conditions: light goes from denser to rarer medium, and the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.

Why does a diamond sparkle? Model answer: Diamond's refractive index (2.42) is very high, so its critical angle (24.4°) is very small. Light entering it is totally internally reflected many times inside before coming out, making it sparkle.

A man fires a gun and hears the echo from a hill after 3 s. If the speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹, find the distance of the hill. Model answer: Distance travelled $= 340 \times 3 = 1020$ m; hill distance $= 1020/2 = 510$ m.

Write two differences between a motor and a generator. Model answer: A motor converts electrical energy to mechanical energy (works on Fleming's left-hand rule); a generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy (works on electromagnetic induction).

Explain the working of a step-down transformer. A transformer has 1000 primary turns on a 220 V mains. How many secondary turns are needed for 11 V? Model answer: A step-down transformer has fewer turns on the secondary than on the primary. An alternating current in the primary produces a changing magnetic flux in the iron core, which induces a smaller alternating emf in the secondary (electromagnetic induction). $\dfrac{V_p}{V_s}=\dfrac{N_p}{N_s}\Rightarrow\dfrac{220}{11}=\dfra
Why are household appliances connected in parallel? Model answer: Each appliance receives the full supply voltage (220 V) and can be switched on or off independently of the others.

What is a fuse? Where is it connected in a circuit? Model answer: A fuse is a wire of low melting point that melts and breaks the circuit when the current is too large. It is connected in series with the live wire.
State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. Model answer: The emf induced in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linked with it.
Why is electricity transmitted at high voltage? Model answer: At high voltage the current is small for the same power, so the heat loss $I^2R$ in the wires is much smaller.

An electric iron of 1000 W, 220 V is used for 3 hours a day. Find the energy used in 30 days and the cost at Rs 12 per unit. Model answer: Energy per day $= 1 \text{ kW} \times 3 \text{ h} = 3$ kWh. In 30 days: 90 kWh. Cost $= 90 \times 12 =$ Rs 1080.

A step-down transformer has 1000 turns in the primary and 50 turns in the secondary. If the input voltage is 220 V, find the output voltage. If the output current is 4 A, find the input current. Model answer: $V_s = 220 \times \dfrac{50}{1000} = 11$ V. $I_p = \dfrac{V_sI_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{11 \times 4}{220} = 0.2$ A.

Explain the working of a DC motor with the help of Fleming's left-hand rule. Model answer: Describe the coil in the magnetic field, split-ring commutator, brushes. Forces on the two sides are opposite by the left-hand rule, which turn the coil; the commutator reverses the current each half turn, so the rotation continues in one direction.
Write any two uses of artificial satellites. Model answer: Telecommunication (TV, phone and internet signals) and weather forecasting; also GPS navigation and remote sensing.

Describe the Big Bang theory and give two pieces of evidence for it. Model answer: The universe began about 13.8 billion years ago from an extremely hot, dense point that expanded rapidly; as it expanded it cooled, and matter formed atoms, stars and galaxies. Evidence: (i) galaxies are moving apart, so the universe is expanding (red shift of light from distant galaxies); (ii) cosmic microwave backgro

Define a light year. How long does light from the Sun take to reach the Earth? Model answer: A light year is the distance travelled by light in one year in vacuum ($9.46\times10^{12}$ km). Sunlight takes about 8 min 20 s (500 s).

Why do stars twinkle but planets do not? Model answer: The light of stars is refracted by the moving layers of the atmosphere, so its apparent position and brightness keep changing. Planets are nearer and look like small discs; the changes from different points average out.
Name the types of galaxy. To which type does the Milky Way belong? Model answer: Spiral, elliptical and irregular. The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.
Why is Pluto not called a planet? Model answer: Pluto has not cleared its orbit of other bodies, so in 2006 it was classified as a dwarf planet.
Give any two uses of artificial satellites. Model answer: Any two: communication, weather forecasting, navigation (GPS), remote sensing, TV broadcast.

Describe the life cycle of a star like the Sun and of a massive star. Model answer: Sun-like: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf. Massive: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole.

State the Big Bang theory and give two pieces of evidence for it. Model answer: Statement: the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago from a hot, dense state and has been expanding. Evidence: red shift of distant galaxies (they recede, faster if farther); cosmic microwave background of 2.7 K; abundance of hydrogen and helium.

A star is 8.6 light years away. Find its distance in kilometres and the time light from it takes to reach us. Model answer: $d = 8.6 \times 9.46\times10^{12} = 8.14\times10^{13}$ km. Time $= 8.6$ years.

What is a geostationary satellite? Write the conditions it must satisfy and two uses. Model answer: A satellite that appears fixed above one point of the Earth. Conditions: orbit above the equator at about 36,000 km, revolves west to east, period 24 h. Uses: TV and communication, weather watching.

Differentiate between RAM and ROM. Model answer: RAM is temporary (volatile) memory used while a program runs and is lost when power goes off. ROM is permanent (non-volatile) memory holding start-up instructions.

What is cyber crime? Mention three safe-use rules for the internet. Model answer: Cyber crime is a crime committed using computers or the internet, such as hacking, phishing or spreading viruses. Rules: use strong, private passwords; do not share personal details or open links from unknown senders; keep anti-virus software updated; log out of public computers.

Differentiate between hardware and software. Model answer: Hardware is the physical, touchable parts of a computer (monitor, keyboard); software is the set of programs that instruct the hardware (Windows, MS Word).

What is the difference between the internet and the WWW? Model answer: The internet is the worldwide network of connected computers; the WWW is the collection of linked web pages that we view through a browser, one of the services on the internet.

Define e-commerce. Give two examples of e-commerce websites in Nepal. Model answer: E-commerce is buying and selling of goods and services over the internet. Examples: Daraz, Sastodeal (also Hamrobazar).
What is cyber crime? Give two examples. Model answer: A crime done using a computer or the internet. Examples: hacking, phishing, online fraud.
Write two uses of ICT in the field of health. Model answer: Telemedicine (consulting doctors by video) and digital medical imaging or electronic patient records.
A video file of 600 MB is downloaded at 16 Mbps. How long does it take? Model answer: $600\ \text{MB} = 600 \times 8 = 4800$ megabits. Time $= 4800/16 = 300$ s $= 5$ minutes.

List four advantages and two disadvantages of e-commerce. Model answer: Advantages: 24-hour service, saves time and travel, wide choice, home delivery. Disadvantages: risk of fraud, cannot touch the goods before buying, depends on the internet.

Why is cyber ethics necessary? Explain any four rules of good conduct on the internet. Model answer: Cyber ethics protects users and keeps the internet safe and respectful. Rules: be polite; do not spread false news; respect copyright and do not plagiarise; do not enter other people's accounts; protect privacy.
State the modern periodic law. Model answer: The physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
Why are noble gases chemically inert? Model answer: Their outermost shells are complete (2 electrons in helium, 8 in the rest), so they neither gain, lose nor share electrons.

The atomic numbers of X and Y are 11 and 17. Write their electronic configurations, groups and periods, and the formula and type of bond in the compound they form. Model answer: X (11): 2, 8, 1 — group 1, period 3 (sodium). Y (17): 2, 8, 7 — group 17, period 3 (chlorine). X loses one electron to become X⁺ and Y gains it to become Y⁻, giving XY (NaCl) with an ionic bond.

Describe how atomic size and metallic character change across a period and down a group. Model answer: Across a period (left to right): nuclear charge increases while the shell number is the same, so atomic size decreases and metallic character decreases. Down a group: extra shells are added, so atomic size increases and metallic character increases.

Write any two limitations of Newlands' law of octaves. Model answer: (i) It worked only up to calcium. (ii) It did not leave places for new elements such as the noble gases; unlike elements were placed together.

Why does atomic size decrease from left to right in a period? Model answer: The number of shells remains the same, but the nuclear charge increases by one at every step. The stronger pull draws the electrons nearer to the nucleus.

Define ionisation energy. How does it change down a group? Model answer: It is the minimum energy needed to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom. It decreases down a group because the outer electron is farther away and shielded by more inner shells.

Write the electronic configuration of Mg (Z = 12) and Cl (Z = 17). State the period, group and valency of each, and write the formula of the compound they form. Model answer: Mg: 2, 8, 2; period 3, group 2, valency 2. Cl: 2, 8, 7; period 3, group 17, valency 1. Mg loses two electrons, Cl gains one each, so two Cl atoms combine with one Mg: MgCl₂.

Describe the merits and demerits of Mendeleev's periodic table. Model answer: Merits: similar elements in one group; gaps left and properties of Ga, Sc, Ge predicted correctly. Demerits: position of hydrogen uncertain; no place for isotopes; some higher-mass elements placed before lower-mass ones (Co before Ni); unlike elements in one group.

Compare the elements Na, Mg, Al in terms of atomic size, ionisation energy and metallic character. Give reasons. Model answer: All are in period 3, so the number of shells is constant while the nuclear charge increases from Na (+11) to Al (+13). Atomic size decreases (Na > Mg > Al); ionisation energy increases (Na < Mg < Al, roughly); metallic character decreases (Na > Mg > Al).

The atomic masses of Li and K are 7 and 39. Using Dobereiner's law, find the atomic mass of Na and state whether it fits. Model answer: Mass of Na = (7 + 39) / 2 = 46 / 2 = 23. The actual atomic mass of sodium is 23, so it fits the law exactly.

Write four factors that affect the rate of a chemical reaction, with one example each. Model answer: (i) Temperature: milk sours faster in a warm room. (ii) Concentration: concentrated acid reacts faster with marble than dilute acid. (iii) Surface area: powdered marble reacts faster than a lump. (iv) Catalyst: MnO₂ speeds the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.
Why does powdered zinc react faster with acid than a lump of zinc? Model answer: Powder has a larger surface area, so more particles are exposed to the acid and more collisions occur per second.
Distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions with one example each. Model answer: Exothermic: releases heat (burning of coal). Endothermic: absorbs heat (decomposition of CaCO₃).

Explain with examples four factors that affect the rate of a chemical reaction. Model answer: Concentration (more concentrated acid reacts faster with marble); surface area (powdered chalk faster than a lump); temperature (food cooks faster at higher temperature); catalyst (MnO₂ speeds up decomposition of H₂O₂). Each is explained by more or harder collisions.

Describe the properties of acids with the help of equations. Model answer: Sour taste; blue litmus turns red; reaction with metals gives hydrogen (Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂); with carbonates gives CO₂ (CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂); with bases gives salt and water (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O).

Write the steps to balance Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃ and give the balanced equation. Model answer: Fe₂O₃ has 2 Fe and 3 O. Put 2 before Fe: 2Fe. Oxygen is 3 on the right and 2 on the left; take the lowest common multiple 6: 3O₂ on the left and 2Fe₂O₃ on the right; then Fe is 4, so 4Fe. 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.

Explain the pH scale and state how you would find whether a liquid is acidic, basic or neutral using litmus paper. Model answer: pH is a scale from 0 to 14 that shows acidity or basicity: below 7 acidic, 7 neutral, above 7 basic. With litmus: if blue litmus turns red, the liquid is acidic; if red litmus turns blue, it is basic; if neither changes, it is neutral.
Write the chemical test for carbon dioxide. Model answer: Pass the gas through lime water: it turns milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms. Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ ↓ + H₂O.
A gas has volume 500 cm³ at 1 atm. What is its volume at 2 atm if the temperature is constant? Model answer: $P_1V_1=P_2V_2\Rightarrow1\times500=2\times V_2\Rightarrow V_2=250\ \text{cm}^3$.
State Boyle's law and write its mathematical form. Model answer: At constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure; $P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$.
Why is the Kelvin scale used in Charles' law? Model answer: The volume of a gas is proportional to the absolute temperature; the Kelvin scale starts from absolute zero, so that V/T is a constant.
How is lime water used to test CO₂? Write the equation. Model answer: Passing CO₂ through lime water makes it milky: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ ↓ + H₂O.
Why is dilute sulphuric acid not used to prepare CO₂ from marble? Model answer: Calcium sulphate is slightly soluble and forms a coat on the marble that stops the acid reaching it.

Describe the laboratory preparation of oxygen. Give the equation, one test and two uses. Model answer: Heat KClO₃ with MnO₂ in a hard glass tube; collect over water. 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂ ↑. A glowing splinter relights. Uses: respiration support, welding.

A gas occupies 250 cm³ at 17 °C. At what temperature will it occupy 300 cm³ at constant pressure? Model answer: $T_1 = 17 + 273 = 290$ K. $T_2 = V_2T_1/V_1 = 300 \times 290/250 = 348$ K. In °C: 348 - 273 = 75 °C.
Why is sodium stored under kerosene? Model answer: Sodium is very reactive and reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture of air, so it is kept under kerosene to keep air and water away.
Why do aluminium utensils not corrode easily? Model answer: Aluminium forms a thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide on its surface, which protects the metal below from further attack.

What is rusting? State the conditions needed and two methods to prevent it. Model answer: Rusting is the slow corrosion of iron in damp air to form reddish-brown hydrated iron(III) oxide. It needs both oxygen and water. Prevention: painting or oiling; galvanising (zinc coating); making alloys like stainless steel.

Describe the extraction of aluminium from its ore by electrolysis. Model answer: The ore is bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O), purified to alumina (Al₂O₃). Alumina is dissolved in molten cryolite (which lowers the melting point) and electrolysed in a steel tank lined with carbon (cathode) using carbon anodes. At the cathode, Al³⁺ gains electrons to give molten aluminium that collects at the bottom; at the anode
Differentiate between a mineral and an ore. Model answer: A mineral is any natural substance that contains a metal compound; an ore is a mineral from which the metal can be extracted profitably.
Why are sodium and potassium kept under kerosene? Model answer: They react violently with oxygen and moisture of the air; kerosene keeps them away from both.
Why does aluminium not corrode easily even though it is reactive? Model answer: Aluminium forms a thin, strong layer of Al₂O₃ on its surface that protects the metal beneath.
Write two differences between metals and non-metals. Model answer: Metals are good conductors, malleable and ductile; non-metals are poor conductors and brittle.

Describe the extraction of iron from haematite in a blast furnace. Give the reactions. Model answer: Charge: haematite, coke, limestone from the top; hot air from bottom. C + O₂ → CO₂; CO₂ + C → 2CO; Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂; CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag). Molten iron and slag are tapped from the bottom.

What is corrosion? Explain the conditions for rusting of iron and four methods of prevention. Model answer: Corrosion: slow destruction of a metal by air, moisture or chemicals. Rusting needs oxygen and water together (nail experiment). Prevention: painting or oiling, galvanising with zinc, electroplating, alloying (stainless steel), sacrificial protection.

What is the reactivity series? Explain two of its uses with an example for each. Model answer: The reactivity series ranks metals by decreasing reactivity. (i) Displacement: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. (ii) Reaction with acid: Mg and Zn give H₂ with dilute acids but Cu does not. (iii) It chooses the extraction method.
Find the mass of aluminium obtainable from 204 kg of alumina (Al = 27, O = 16). Model answer: Molar mass of Al₂O₃ = 102; it contains 54 of aluminium. Mass of Al = (54 / 102) × 204 = 54 × 2 = 108 kg.

What is a homologous series? Give one example. Model answer: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar properties, in which successive members differ by CH₂. Example: alkanes (CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈).
Write the molecular formulae of the first four alkanes. Model answer: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀ (general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$).

How is ethanol converted to ethanoic acid? Name the acid's functional group, and state how it reacts with ethanol. Model answer: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is oxidised by an oxidising agent such as acidified potassium dichromate to ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH. The functional group is carboxyl, –COOH. With ethanol, in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄, it forms an ester and water: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.

What is a homologous series? Give two characteristics. Model answer: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, in which successive members differ by CH₂. Characteristics: gradual change in physical properties; similar chemical properties.
How would you distinguish ethane from ethene in the laboratory? Model answer: Shake each with bromine water: ethene decolourises it; ethane does not.

Write the preparation, two properties and two uses of ethanol. Model answer: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ with yeast. Properties: colourless liquid, miscible with water; reacts with sodium giving H₂; burns with a blue flame. Uses: solvent, sanitiser, fuel.

Describe the laboratory preparation of ethyne and write two of its reactions. Model answer: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂, gas collected over water. Reactions: 2C₂H₂ + 5O₂ → 4CO₂ + 2H₂O; C₂H₂ + 2H₂ → C₂H₆ (Ni).

Write the formulae of the alkane, alkene and alkyne with 6 carbon atoms and calculate the molecular mass of the alkane (C = 12, H = 1). Model answer: Alkane C₆H₁₄, alkene C₆H₁₂, alkyne C₆H₁₀. Mass of C₆H₁₄ = 72 + 14 = 86.
Why is gypsum added to cement? Model answer: Gypsum slows down the setting of cement so that the mortar can be worked before it hardens.

Write any two differences between soap and detergent. Model answer: Soap is the sodium salt of a fatty acid; detergent is a synthetic salt of sulphonic acid. Soap forms scum in hard water; detergent does not, and works in hard and soft water.

Describe the manufacture of soap (saponification). Model answer: Oil or fat is heated with sodium hydroxide solution. The ester bonds break (saponification) to give glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids (soap): fat + 3NaOH → glycerol + 3 soap. Common salt is added to make the soap separate as a layer (salting out); it is then moulded, perfumed and dried.

Name the three main nutrients in NPK fertilisers and state one function of each. Mention two harmful effects of overuse. Model answer: Nitrogen (N) promotes leaf and stem growth; phosphorus (P) helps roots and flowering; potassium (K) improves disease resistance and fruit quality. Overuse pollutes water (eutrophication), harms soil organisms and can burn crops.
What is a fertiliser? Name the three primary nutrients. Model answer: A substance added to soil to supply nutrients to plants. Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium.
Why is annealing done in glass making? Model answer: The glass is cooled slowly to remove internal stress, so that it does not break easily.

Differentiate between thermoplastic and thermosetting plastic. Model answer: A thermoplastic softens on heating and can be re-moulded (polythene); a thermosetting plastic sets permanently after heating once (Bakelite).
Why does soap not lather well in hard water? Model answer: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions react with soap to form insoluble scum, so soap is wasted before it can lather.
Write two problems caused by the excess use of plastics. Model answer: Plastics are non-biodegradable and pollute soil; they block drains and harm animals; burning releases toxic gases.

Describe the manufacture of soap. Explain the cleaning action of soap. Model answer: Saponification: boil oil or fat with NaOH; add salt to separate soap (salting out); wash, add perfume and mould. Cleaning: tails dissolve in grease, heads stay in water, grease is broken into micelles and rinsed away.

Describe how Portland cement is made, stating the raw materials and the role of gypsum. Model answer: Limestone and clay are ground, mixed and heated at 1400 to 1500 °C in a rotary kiln to form clinker; clinker is ground with 2 to 3 % gypsum. Gypsum slows the setting.
A farmer needs 92 kg of nitrogen. How much Model answer: (a) Urea = 92 / 0.46 = 200 kg. (b) Ammonium nitrate = 92 / 0.35 = 262.9 kg (about 263 kg).

What is a polymer? Explain the types of plastics with two examples each and suggest four ways to manage plastic waste. Model answer: A polymer is a large molecule formed from many monomers. Thermoplastics (polythene, PVC) soften on heating; thermosetting plastics (Bakelite, melamine) do not. Management: reduce, reuse, recycle, refuse; ban thin bags; use jute or paper bags.

Describe the diversity of Nepal and explain why unity in diversity matters. Model answer: Introduction. Nepal is a small country with a very large variety of people. Points. (i) Census 2021 counted 29,164,578 people. (ii) They belong to 142 caste and ethnic groups. (iii) They speak 124 mother tongues. (iv) They follow 10 religions. (v) The land has mountain, hill and Terai regions with different ways of lif

National pride projects are very large strategic projects chosen to speed up growth and bring national pride. Examples. Melamchi drinking water, Upper Tamakoshi hydropower (456 MW), Budhi Gandaki hydropower, the Kathmandu–Terai/Madhesh Fast Track, new international airports and the highways. Importance. (

concepts.u: Unit 3: Our Social Values and Beliefs
concepts.t: Describe the contributions of Gandhi, Mandela, Mother Teresa and Martin Luther King Jr. Model answer: Introduction. These four persons served humanity beyond their own countries. Gandhi led India's freedom struggle by non-violence and truth. Mandela fought apartheid in South Africa, spent many years in prison, became president and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993. Mother Teresa served the poor, the sick and the dying

Describe the composition of the Federal Parliament and explain how a bill becomes law. Model answer: Composition. The Federal Parliament is the President together with two houses. The House of Representatives has 275 members: 165 elected by first-past-the-post and 110 by proportional representation, for five years. The National Assembly has 59 members for six years, and one-third retire every two years. How a bill bec

Describe the relief, climate and economic importance of the continent of Africa. Model answer: Introduction. Africa is the second largest continent, about 30.3 million km². Relief. It has the Sahara in the north, the Nile (the great river) and the highest peak, Kilimanjaro (5,895 m). Climate. The equator crosses the middle, so the continent has equatorial rainforest, savanna grassland and hot desert; the north a

Explain the causes and results of the revolution of 2007 BS. Model answer: Introduction. The revolution of 2007 BS ended 104 years of Rana rule. Causes. (i) The Ranas ruled by family and kept people poor and uneducated. (ii) Political parties such as the Nepali Congress worked for democracy. (iii) King Tribhuvan supported the movement and left for India. (iv) Indian independence in 1947 encou

How can tourism be promoted in Nepal? Explain. Model answer: Introduction. About 1.2 million tourists visited Nepal in 2019, and tourism gives 6 to 7% of GDP. Ways to promote. (i) Build infrastructure: roads, airports, hotels. (ii) Market Nepal abroad through the Nepal Tourism Board (1998). (iii) Ensure the safety of visitors. (iv) Offer a variety of products: trekking, wildlife

concepts.u: Unit 9: Our International Relations and Cooperation
concepts.t: Explain the role of the United Nations in world peace and development. Model answer: Introduction. The UN was founded on 24 October 1945, has 193 members and its headquarters in New York. Nepal joined in 1955. Role. (i) The Security Council acts for peace and security; its five permanent members hold the veto. (ii) UN peacekeeping missions keep ceasefires, and Nepal contributes troops. (iii) Specialise

Explain the relationship between population and environment. Model answer: Introduction. Population and environment affect each other. Effects of population on environment. (i) More people need more land and firewood, causing deforestation. (ii) Urban growth causes air, water and noise pollution and waste. (iii) Greater use of fossil fuel adds to climate change. Effects of environment on popu

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Differentiate between weather and climate. Model answer: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere in a place; climate is the long-term (30-year) average. Weather changes hour by hour, climate changes slowly; weather is studied in forecasts, climate in climate records.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: State four causes of human trafficking. Model answer: Poverty; illiteracy and lack of awareness; fake job and marriage offers; open borders and weak control.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Define sustainable development. Name its three pillars. Model answer: Sustainable development meets the present need without harming the future (Brundtland, 1987). Pillars: economic, social, environmental.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: State four causes of domestic violence. Model answer: Unequal gender power, poverty, alcohol and drugs, and lack of education and awareness.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Explain the importance of the Constitution of Nepal 2072. Model answer: Introduction: the Constitution was promulgated on 3 Ashwin 2072 (20 September 2015). Importance: it makes Nepal a federal democratic republic with 7 provinces and 753 local levels; it divides power among the legislature, executive and judiciary; it gives 31 fundamental rights; it protects diversity and equality; it gua

concepts.u: Social Studies: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Describe the results of the First World War. Model answer: Introduction: the war lasted from 1914 to 1918. Results: the Treaty of Versailles (1919) punished Germany; the League of Nations was formed; the empires of Germany, Austria-Hungary, Russia and Turkey collapsed; new countries were created; millions died; the war's bitterness helped lead to the Second World War. Conclusi

concepts.u: Social Studies: Model Question Sets and Predicted Questions
concepts.t: Find the compound interest on Rs 20,000 at 10% a year for 2 years. Model answer: A = 20,000 × (1.1)² = 20,000 × 1.21 = Rs 24,200. Compound interest = 24,200 - 20,000 = Rs 4,200.

concepts.u: Social Studies: Model Question Sets and Predicted Questions
concepts.t: State four effects of climate on human life. Model answer: Climate and relief decide vegetation and wildlife, the density of population (monsoon plains hold the densest populations), clothing and food, and the kind of work people do.

A double-stranded DNA molecule contains 1200 base pairs, of which 30 % of the bases are guanine. Calculate the number of adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine bases in it, and the length of the molecule in nanometres. Model answer: Total bases $= 2 \times 1200 = 2400$. Guanine is 30 % of all bases, so $G = 0.30 \times 2400 = 720$, and by Chargaff $C = 720$. The remaining bases are $2400 - 1440 = 960$, shared equally, so $A = T = 480$. Length $=$ number of base pairs $\times\ 0.34\ \text{nm} = 1200 \times 0.34 = 408\ \text{nm}$.

What is an enzyme? Describe the effect of temperature and of pH on enzyme activity. Model answer: Definition: a protein catalyst that lowers activation energy and is unchanged at the end. Temperature: activity roughly doubles for each 10 °C rise up to the optimum (about 37 °C in mammals) as molecular collisions increase; above it the tertiary structure denatures and activity falls steeply and irreversibly. pH: each

Give any four general characters of Bryophyta and explain why bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom. Model answer: Any four of: the plant body is a haploid gametophyte, thalloid or leafy, with no true roots (only rhizoids) and no vascular tissue; sex organs are multicellular and jacketed (antheridium and archegonium); fertilisation needs external water; the zygote forms an embryo and then a sporophyte of foot, seta and capsule whic

What is a lichen? Name its two components, state the contribution of each, and give two uses of lichens. Model answer: A lichen is a stable symbiotic association of a fungus and a photosynthetic partner forming a thallus unlike either alone. The mycobiont (usually an Ascomycete, 90–95 % of the thallus) forms the body, absorbs and retains water and minerals, and protects the alga from desiccation and intense light; the phycobiont (a gre

Describe the family Solanaceae under the headings habit, leaf, inflorescence, flower (calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium), fruit and floral formula, and give four points of economic importance with named examples. Model answer: Habit: mostly annual or perennial herbs and shrubs, rarely small trees, with a tap root; potato has an underground stem tuber and Solanum xanthocarpum is prickly. Leaf: alternate, simple, exstipulate, entire or lobed, with bicollateral vascular bundles. Inflorescence: usually a cymose inflorescence (helicoid or scorpio

Why is a virus said to lie on the borderline between living and non-living? Give two characters of each kind. Model answer: Living: they possess nucleic acid and so show heredity and mutation, and they multiply to give thousands of progeny inside a host. Non-living: they can be crystallised and stored like a chemical, and they have no cytoplasm, no respiration and no enzyme system of their own, so they cannot grow on a nutrient medium.

Define an ecosystem and describe its biotic components with one example of each. Model answer: Definition as in the text. Producers — autotrophs that fix solar energy, e.g. grass, Hydrilla. Consumers — heterotrophs: primary (herbivore, e.g. chital deer), secondary (primary carnivore, e.g. frog), tertiary (top carnivore, e.g. Royal Bengal tiger). Decomposers — saprotrophic bacteria and fungi that mineralise dead

The producers of a pond fix $8000\ \text{kJ m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$, of which they respire $5600\ \text{kJ m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$. Calculate the net primary productivity, and the energy that would reach a fish at the Model answer: $\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R = 8000 - 5600 = 2400\ \text{kJ m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$. The energy passed on is taken from the NPP, so the second trophic level receives $0.10 \times 2400 = 240\ \text{kJ m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$ and the third trophic level receives $0.10 \times 240 = 24\ \text{kJ m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$.

List any four morphological and anatomical adaptations of xerophytes, naming a plant that shows each. Model answer: (i) Long, deeply penetrating branched roots — Acacia catechu. (ii) Leaves reduced to spines with a photosynthetic phylloclade — Opuntia. (iii) Very thick cuticle and multilayered epidermis with sclerenchymatous hypodermis — Nerium oleander. (iv) Stomata few and sunken in hairy pits — Nerium, Casuarina. A fifth, physiol

Name the six altitudinal vegetation zones of Nepal with their altitude ranges, and give one indicator species of each. Model answer: Tropical, below 1000 m — Shorea robusta. Subtropical, 1000–2000 m — Schima wallichii or Pinus roxburghii. Temperate, 2000–3000 m — Quercus semecarpifolia or Rhododendron arboreum. Subalpine, 3000–4000 m — Abies spectabilis or Betula utilis. Alpine, 4000–5000 m — Rhododendron anthopogon with Kobresia meadow. Nival, abov

Differentiate between in-situ and ex-situ conservation, giving two named Nepali examples of each. Model answer: In-situ = conserved inside the natural habitat, so the whole ecosystem is saved and the species keeps evolving; cheap per species but needs large areas. Examples: Chitwan National Park, Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve. Ex-situ = conserved outside the natural habitat, under human care; useful for species too rare to surviv

The mean annual temperature at Pokhara (altitude 820 m) is 20 °C. Using a lapse rate of 6 °C per 1000 m, estimate the temperature at Ghorepani (2,870 m), and name the vegetation zone and the indicator tree species you wo Model answer: Height gained $= 2870 - 820 = 2050\ \text{m}$. Temperature fall $= 6 \times 2050/1000 = 12.3\ ^\circ\text{C}$, so $T = 20 - 12.3 = 7.7\ ^\circ\text{C}$. At 2,870 m Ghorepani lies in the temperate zone, where the expected species are Quercus semecarpifolia (khasru), Rhododendron arboreum (lali gurans) and Pinus wallichi

List any four human activities that degrade the vegetation of Nepal, and state one control measure for each. Model answer: (i) Deforestation and encroachment — hand the forest to community forest user groups and register boundaries. (ii) Overgrazing — fix a stocking limit and rotate the kharka, and promote stall feeding on fodder trees. Define biology, and name any four branches of biology based on the aspect of life studied, with one line on each. Model answer: Biology is the science that deals with living organisms — their structure, function, origin, growth, reproduction, classification, behaviour, evolution and relation with the environment. Analogous — different structure and origin, same function, by convergent evolution: wing of a bird and of an

Describe the Miller–Urey experiment and state precisely what it proved. Model answer: Sealed glass system: boiling water feeds vapour into a chamber charged with CH₄, NH₃ and H₂, tungsten electrodes spark for a week at about 800 °C, a condenser returns the products to a U-trap. Result: amino acids (glycine, alanine, aspartic acid) with urea, sugars and fatty acids. It proved that the monomers of life fo

What is industrial melanism, and how does it demonstrate natural selection? Model answer: Industrial melanism is the rise in frequency of a dark form in a polluted area. In Biston betularia the melanic carbonaria was almost unknown before 1848; soot killed the lichens and by 1895 about 98 % of Manchester moths were black. Kettlewell's 1955 mark–recapture recovered 27.5 % of carbonaria against 13.0 % of typi

State the Hardy–Weinberg principle and the conditions under which a population stays in genetic equilibrium. Model answer: In a large, randomly mating population the allele and genotype frequencies at a locus stay constant across generations, with $p + q = 1$ and $p^{2} + 2pq + q^{2} = 1$. Conditions: very large population, random mating, no mutation, no migration, no natural selection. Breaking any one makes the population evolve.

State the postulates of Darwin's theory of natural selection. Explain the long neck of the giraffe first on Lamarck's theory and then on Darwin's, and say why only one explanation is accepted. Model answer: (a) Prodigality of reproduction; struggle for existence (intraspecific, interspecific, environmental); variation; natural selection, or survival of the fittest; inheritance of the useful variations; origin of new species by their accumulation. (b) Lamarck: the short-necked ancestor stretched its neck for high foliage,

Give an account of human evolution from Dryopithecus to Homo sapiens sapiens with the approximate age and cranial capacity of each stage, and list four trends shown by the series. Model answer: Stages, ages and cranial capacities as in the table of section 7.4, in that order, with the branching of the figure. Trends: erect posture and complete bipedalism, which came before the large brain; progressive increase in cranial capacity; shortening of the jaws and face with reduced canines, loss of the brow ridges a

Distinguish between acoelomate, pseudocoelomate and coelomate animals, giving one example of each. Model answer: Acoelomate — no body cavity, the space packed with mesodermal parenchyma (Planaria). Pseudocoelomate — a cavity present but a persistent blastocoel, lined by mesoderm on the body-wall side only (Ascaris). Coelomate — a true coelom within the mesoderm, lined by peritoneum on both body wall and gut (Pheretima).

How does Paramecium keep its water content constant in pond water? Model answer: Pond water is hypotonic, so water enters by osmosis. Two contractile vacuoles, each fed by radiating canals, collect it and discharge through a temporary pore, contracting alternately every 10–20 s. Their role is osmoregulation, not excretion: ammonia leaves by diffusion.

State four diagnostic characters of phylum Arthropoda and name two examples. Model answer: (i) Jointed appendages. (ii) A chitinous exoskeleton that is moulted (ecdysis). (iii) A haemocoel with an open circulation. (iv) Segmented body, typically head, thorax and abdomen, with compound eyes. Examples: Periplaneta americana, Palaemon.

List the external apertures of Pheretima posthuma with their positions. Model answer: Mouth on the peristomium (segment 1); anus on the last segment; female genital pore mid-ventral on segment 14; one pair of male genital pores on segment 18; four pairs of spermathecal pores in grooves 5/6, 6/7, 7/8 and 8/9; many nephridiopores; mid-dorsal pores from groove 12/13 backwards.

Describe the three types of nephridia found in the earthworm. Model answer: Septal nephridia, on both faces of the septa from segment 15 backwards, open into the intestine (enteronephric). Integumentary nephridia, on the inner body wall from segment 3 back and most numerous in the clitellum, open on the skin (exonephric). The earthworm is hermaphrodite, yet it cannot fertilise itself, and its fertilisation is external. Explain. Model answer: Both sets of gonads occur in one worm, but it is protandrous — sperm mature before the ova of the same animal — so cross-fertilisation is obligatory. During copulation each worm charges the other's spermathecae. Later the clitellum secretes a cocoon; as the worm backs out, the cocoon collects ova at segment 14 and stor

Explain the three modes of respiration in the frog and state when each is used. Model answer: Cutaneous respiration through the moist vascular skin works in water and air, is the only method during hibernation and aestivation, and accounts for most of the year's gas exchange. Buccopharyngeal respiration across the buccal lining is used at rest on land. Pulmonary respiration serves the active animal, air being d

Describe any four adaptations of a bird for aerial life, stating the function of each. Differentiate between innate and learned behaviour, with two examples of each. Model answer: Innate: inherited, present at birth, identical in all members, rigid, needs no practice (a spider spinning its first web; a herring gull chick pecking the red spot). Learned: acquired by experience, differs between individuals, flexible, can be forgotten (Pavlov's dog salivating at a bell; a monkey opening a latch by t

A herd of 500 blue sheep grows exponentially with an intrinsic rate of natural increase $r = 0.08\ \text{yr}^{-1}$. Calculate Model answer: (a) $N_t = N_0e^{rt} = 500\,e^{0.08\times 10} = 500\,e^{0.8} = 500 \times 2.2255 = 1113$ animals (to the nearest animal). (b) $t_d = \dfrac{\ln 2}{r} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.08} = 8.66\ \text{years}$.

What is eutrophication? Explain, step by step, how it kills the fish of a lake. Model answer: Eutrophication is the over-enrichment of a water body with nutrients, chiefly nitrate and phosphate. Sequence: fertiliser, detergent and sewage run in → algae and water hyacinth bloom → the surface mat blocks light so submerged plants die → aerobic bacteria decompose the huge dead mass → BOD rises sharply and dissolved

Distinguish between bioaccumulation and biomagnification, and give one example of a pollutant that shows both. Model answer: Bioaccumulation is the gradual build-up of a persistent pollutant within a single organism, because intake exceeds excretion. Biomagnification is the stepwise rise in its concentration from one trophic level to the next along a food chain, because each consumer eats many individuals of the level below and retains almos

Define adaptation and distinguish it from acclimatisation. With the help of a labelled diagram, describe the adaptations of a bony fish for aquatic life. Model answer: (a) Adaptation is an inherited, population-level feature produced by natural selection over generations; acclimatisation is a reversible physiological adjustment made by one individual within its own lifetime (extra red cells at high altitude). (b) Expect the labelled fish diagram plus streamlining and mucus, fins for

Explain the logistic model of population growth and sketch the curve, marking the carrying capacity. Define conservation biology and state its three levels of biodiversity with one Nepali example of each. Model answer: Conservation biology is the applied science that studies the loss of biological diversity and develops methods to protect, restore and sustainably manage species, habitats and ecosystems. Model answer: Give the seven postulates of §7.1, then $PV = \frac{1}{3}mNc^{2}$, where $P$ is pressure, $V$ volume, $m$ the mass of one molecule, $N$ the number of molecules and $c$ the root-mean-square speed.

Define vapour pressure and boiling point. Explain why water boils at about $95\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ in Kathmandu but at $100\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$ in Biratnagar. Model answer: Definitions as in §7.5. Kathmandu (≈1,350 m) has a lower atmospheric pressure (≈86 kPa) than Biratnagar (≈100 kPa, near sea level). A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure, so in Kathmandu that condition is reached at a lower temperature.

Explain why the first ionization energy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen, and why that of magnesium is higher than that of aluminium. Model answer: N: $2p^{3}$ is half-filled and extra stable; O: $2p^{4}$ has a paired electron, and pair repulsion makes it easier to remove, so $\text{IE}_{N} > \text{IE}_{O}$. Mg: $3s^{2}$ is a full subshell; Al: the outer electron is in the higher-energy, better shielded $3p$, so $\text{IE}_{Mg} > \text{IE}_{Al}$.

Using VSEPR theory, predict and explain the shapes of $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and account for their bond angles. Model answer: Electron pairs around the central atom repel and arrange as far apart as possible. $\text{NH}_3$: four pairs (three bond, one lone), tetrahedral arrangement, trigonal pyramidal shape, angle $107^{\circ}$. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$: four pairs (two bond, two lone), tetrahedral arrangement, bent shape, angle $104.5^{\circ}$.

concepts.t: State the modern periodic law. Explain, in terms of orbital filling, why the second period contains 8 elements while the fourth contains 18. Model answer: Properties are periodic functions of atomic number. Period 2 fills 2s and 2p only: 1 + 3 = 4 orbitals × 2 electrons = 8 elements. Period 4 fills 4s, then 3d, then 4p: 1 + 5 + 3 = 9 orbitals × 2 = 18 elements.

concepts.t: Define ionization energy. Why is the second ionization energy of sodium (4562 kJ mol⁻¹) nearly nine times the first (496 kJ mol⁻¹)? Model answer: IE₁ removes the 3s¹ electron from a neutral atom. IE₂ must break into the filled 2s²2p⁶ neon core of Na⁺, where the electron is in a lower shell, feels a much larger $Z_{\text{eff}}$ and must be pulled away from a positive ion. Hence the huge jump, and hence sodium's valency of 1.

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Write the difference between RAM and ROM. Give any three points. Model answer: RAM is read-write and volatile (it loses data at power off), holds programs and data in use, and is made of SRAM and DRAM. ROM is read-only in normal use, non-volatile, and stores start-up instructions such as the BIOS; its types are PROM, EPROM and EEPROM. RAM is also usually larger and faster to write than ROM.

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Differentiate between a compiler and an interpreter. Model answer: A compiler translates the whole program into object code before it runs, reports all errors together, and the code then runs fast without the compiler (C is compiled). An interpreter translates and runs one statement at a time, stops at the first error, and needs the interpreter present each time (BASIC and Python are

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: What is a Trojan horse? State how it differs from a worm. Model answer: A Trojan horse is a program that looks useful or harmless but secretly performs harmful acts, such as stealing passwords or opening a back door. It does not copy itself. A worm copies itself automatically across a network without a host program and without user action, and consumes bandwidth.

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank
concepts.t: Draw the truth table of the XOR gate with its Boolean expression, and prove $A + AB = A$ using a truth table. Model answer: XOR: output is 1 when the inputs differ. Boolean expression: $Y = A \oplus B = A'B + AB'$.

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Differentiate between 1's complement and 2's complement. Model answer: The 1's complement inverts every bit; the 2's complement is the 1's complement plus 1. The 1's complement has two zeros (+0 and -0) while the 2's complement has one. In subtraction the 1's complement needs an end-around carry; the 2's complement just discards the carry. The 2's complement is therefore the one used insi

concepts.u: Computer Science: Unit-wise Subjective Question Bank
concepts.t: Write the differences between compiler and interpreter. Model answer: Compiler: translates the whole program at once; reports all errors after translation; faster execution; the object code is saved; C and C++. Interpreter: translates and executes line by line; stops at the first error; slower execution; no object code is produced; Python and BASIC.

concepts.u: Computer Science: Model Question Sets and Predicted Question
concepts.t: Explain why NAND is called a universal gate. Model answer: A gate is universal if every other gate can be made from it alone. With NAND: NOT is a NAND with both inputs joined ($A \cdot A$ complemented gives $A'$); AND is a NAND followed by a NOT; OR is a NAND of the two inverted inputs, since $(A' B')' = A + B$ by De Morgan. Because NOT, AND and OR can form any logic function,

concepts.u: Computer Science: Model Question Sets and Predicted Question
concepts.t: Write any five differences between a virus and a worm. Model answer: A virus needs a host file; a worm is stand-alone. A virus spreads when a user runs or shares the infected file; a worm spreads by itself through network weaknesses. A virus mainly corrupts or deletes files; a worm mainly consumes bandwidth and memory. A virus is activated by human action; a worm needs none. Removing a

What is a bus? Describe the three types of bus in a computer system, stating the direction of each. Model answer: A bus is a set of parallel wires carrying bits between the units of a computer. The address bus is unidirectional (CPU → memory/I/O) and carries the address of the location being accessed; $n$ lines give $2^{n}$ locations. The data bus is bidirectional and carries the actual data or instruction; its width normally equa

(c) One transfer takes $5 \times 0.25 = 1.25\ \text{ns}$ and moves 64 bits = 8 bytes, so the rate is $8/(1.25\times10^{-9}) = 6.4\times10^{9}\ \text{B s}^{-1} = 6.4\ \t

Distinguish between OMR, OCR and MICR, giving one application of each. Model answer: OMR senses whether a mark has been made in a fixed position by measuring reflected light — used for MCQ answer sheets. OCR recognises the shape of printed or handwritten characters and converts them to editable text — used to digitise books and forms. MICR reads characters printed in magnetic ink in the E-13B font — us

Explain the memory hierarchy of a computer. Compare cache, primary memory and secondary memory on speed, cost, capacity and volatility, and explain with an example why cache memory improves performance. Model answer: Sketch the pyramid: registers, L1/L2/L3 cache, RAM, SSD, HDD, tape/cloud. Going down, capacity and cost per byte improve but access time worsens by roughly a factor of ten per level. Cache is small, fast, volatile SRAM; primary memory is larger, slower, volatile DRAM; secondary memory is largest, slowest and non-volati

Simplify $F = \bar{A}\bar{B}C + \bar{A}BC + A\bar{B}C + ABC$ using the laws of Boolean algebra, and draw the logic circuit of the simplified expression. Model answer: $F = C(\bar{A}\bar{B} + \bar{A}B + A\bar{B} + AB) = C\left[\bar{A}(\bar{B}+B) + A(\bar{B}+B)\right] = C(\bar{A}+A) = C\cdot 1 = C$. The "circuit" is a single wire from input $C$ to the output — all the gates can be removed.

Simplify $F(A,B,C,D) = \sum m(0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11,13,15)$ using a Karnaugh map. Show the map, the groupings and the final simplified expression, and draw the resulting logic circuit. Model answer: Plot the minterms on a four-variable map with rows $AB$ = 00, 01, 11, 10 and columns $CD$ = 00, 01, 11, 10.

Define software. Explain the five categories of software given in the syllabus with two examples of each. Model answer: Software is a set of programs, procedures and documentation that tells hardware what to do. System: Windows 11, device drivers. Utility: antivirus, WinRAR. Application: MS Word, Photoshop. Web-based: Gmail, Google Docs. Mobile apps: eSewa, Khalti.

What is an operating system? Explain any five functions of an operating system. Model answer: An OS is system software that acts as an interface between the user and the hardware and manages all resources. Five functions: process management, memory management, file management, device (I/O) management, and security and protection. (User-interface provision and error detection also earn the mark.)

Differentiate between multiprogramming and multitasking, and between multiprocessing and distributed processing. Model answer: Multiprogramming vs multitasking — both keep several programs in memory on one CPU, but multiprogramming switches only when the running program waits for I/O and aims at CPU utilisation, whereas multitasking switches after a fixed time slice and aims at response time. Multiprocessing vs distributed — multiprocessing us

What is open source software? Write any four advantages of it and name four Linux distributions. Model answer: Open source software publishes its source code under a licence allowing anyone to run, study, modify and redistribute it. Advantages: no licence cost; security flaws are found and fixed quickly because the code is public; it can be customised (for example for Nepali); no vendor lock-in. Distributions: Ubuntu, Debian, F

Define an operating system and explain its role as a resource manager and as an extended machine. Explain in detail any five functions of an operating system, and name one Windows tool associated with each. Model answer: (b) Process management — scheduling the CPU among processes (Task Manager). Memory management — allocating RAM and virtual memory (Task Manager → Performance). File management — creating, organising and protecting files (File Explorer). Device management — drivers, buffering and spooling (Device Manager). Security — ac

With a suitable diagram, explain the parts of a window in a Windows application. Explain the steps to install a new printer, and the steps to uninstall an unwanted program from a Windows computer. Model answer: (b) Installing a printer: connect the printer by USB or to the Wi-Fi network and switch it on → Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Printers & scanners → Add device → Windows searches and installs the driver → if it is not found, click Add manually and supply the driver from the manufacturer's disc or website → print a te

What is open source software? Compare Windows and Linux under any five headings. What is a mobile operating system? Explain any three types with their owners and note how a mobile OS differs from a desktop OS. Model answer: (b) A mobile OS is an operating system for handheld devices, designed for a touch screen, limited battery and cellular connectivity. Android (Google, Linux kernel, open source, apps from Google Play); iOS (Apple, Darwin kernel, closed, runs only on Apple hardware); HarmonyOS (Huawei) or KaiOS (for feature phones). Diff

Define cell, range, worksheet and workbook. Write the formulas to find the total, the average, the largest and the smallest of the marks stored in cells C3 to C20. Model answer: A cell is the box where one column meets one row, addressed as C3. A range is a rectangular block of cells, written C3:C20. A worksheet is one page of the grid; a workbook is the whole file containing several worksheets. Total =SUM(C3:C20); average =AVERAGE(C3:C20); largest =MAX(C3:C20); smallest =MIN(C3:C20).

Differentiate between a relative, an absolute and a mixed cell reference with one example of each, and explain why absolute references are needed. Model answer: Relative (B2) changes when the formula is copied — copying =B2*2 from C2 to C3 gives =B3*2. Absolute ($B$2) never changes, because the dollar signs lock both the column and the row. Mixed (B$2 or $B2) locks only one of the two. Absolute references are needed when a formula must always refer to one fixed cell, such as a

Define database, DBMS, field, record and primary key. Name two DBMS packages. Model answer: A database is an organised collection of related data; a DBMS is the software that creates and manages it; a field is one column or attribute; a record is one complete row about one entity; a primary key is a field whose value is unique and never empty, so it identifies a record. Examples of a DBMS: MS Access and MySQL

What is a spreadsheet package? Explain any four of its features. A worksheet stores the names of 20 students in column A and their marks in five subjects in columns B to F, in rows 2 to 21. Write the formulas for the tot Model answer: (b) With the first student in row 2: total G2 =SUM(B2:F2); average H2 =AVERAGE(B2:F2); percentage I2 =G2/500*100; result J2 =IF(H2>=40,"Pass","Fail"); highest total K2 =MAX($G$2:$G$21). Model answer: (b) Tables store the data in rows and columns and are the only object that actually holds data. Queries ask questions of one or more tables — select, filter, sort, calculate — and can also update or delete records. Forms provide a friendly on-screen layout for entering and editing one record at a time. Reports produce

Model answer: (b) School management: inputs — admission forms, daily attendance, exam marks, fee receipts; processing — validation, totalling, grading, dues calculation; outputs — grade sheets, mark ledgers, attendance and fee reports, SMS to parents. Payroll: inputs — employee master data, attendance, overtime, leave, loans; proces

Model answer: See the comparison table in §5.2: unit translated (whole program / one statement), errors reported (all together / stops at the first), object file (produced / not produced), execution speed (fast / slow), memory (more / less), examples (C, C++ / Python, BASIC).

Define syntax error, semantic error and runtime error with one example of each. Model answer: Syntax error — breaks a grammar rule, found by the compiler, no program is produced; example: int a = 5 with no semicolon. Semantic (logical) error — grammatically correct but wrong meaning; example: f = c * 5 / 9 + 32; for a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion, which prints 52.6 instead of 98.6 for 37 °C. Runtime error —

Define an array. Write a C program to read 10 numbers into an array and print their sum and average. Model answer: An array is a collection of a fixed number of elements of the same data type stored in consecutive memory locations under one name, each reached by an index starting at 0.

Explain the three control structures of structured programming with a flowchart fragment for each.
