Write formulas for the total, the percentage (out of 500), the highest and lowest marks, and a result that is "Pass" only if every mark is at least 40 Model answer: Total: =SUM(B2:F2) = 64 + 38 + 75 + 81 + 57 = 315. Percentage: =SUM(B2:F2)/500*100 (or the total's cell /500100) = 63. Highest: =MAX(B2:F2) = 81. Lowest: =MIN(B2:F2) = 38. Result: =IF(MIN(B2:F2)>=40,"Pass","Fail") gives Fail*, because the lowest mark, 38, is below 40.

What is presentation software? Name two examples. Model answer: Presentation software is application software used to create slides containing text, pictures, charts, audio and video and to show them one by one to an audience. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress, Google Slides.

What is a placeholder? What is a slide layout? Model answer: A placeholder is a dotted box on a slide that holds a title, text, a picture or a chart ("Click to add title"). A slide layout is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide, such as Title Slide, Title and Content, or Two Content.

What is a slide master? Why is it useful? Model answer: The slide master (View → Slide Master) is the top slide that stores the design of all slides — background, fonts, colours, logo and placeholder positions. A change made on it appears on every slide at once, which saves time and keeps the slides consistent.

Write two ways to start a slide show and the keys used. Model answer: Press F5 (or Slide Show → From Beginning) to start from the first slide; press Shift + F5 (or From Current Slide) to start from the slide on screen. Esc ends the show.

Write the steps to make a five-slide presentation about your school with a title slide, a picture, a chart and a transition, and to run it. Model answer: (1) Open PowerPoint → Blank Presentation, choose a theme on the Design tab. (2) Slide 1 (Title Slide layout): type the school's name and address. (3) Add slides with Home → New Slide: history, facilities (Insert → Pictures, the school photo), results (Insert → Chart, a column chart of pass percentages), and a thank-you

Write any four rules for designing an effective presentation. Model answer: Any four: use one simple theme throughout; keep about six lines of six words per slide (the 6 × 6 rule); use a large, clear font (at least 24 points) with strong contrast between text and background; use pictures and charts instead of long paragraphs; use only a few, gentle animations and transitions; check spelling; e

Write any four features of presentation software. Model answer: Any four: layouts and themes; placeholders; pictures, tables, charts, audio and video; transitions and animations; several views; slide master; speaker notes and Presenter View; rehearse timings; export to PDF or video.

Define slide layout and theme. Model answer: A slide layout is the arrangement of placeholders on a slide, such as Title and Content. A theme is a ready-made design of background, colours, fonts and effects applied to all the slides.

Differentiate between a transition and an animation. Model answer: A transition is the effect when moving from one slide to the next and is set on the Transitions tab; an animation is an effect on an object (text, picture) within a slide and is set on the Animations tab. A slide has one transition but may have many animations.
Write the steps to apply the same transition to all slides. Model answer: Select a slide → Transitions tab → click an effect such as Fade → set Effect Options and Duration → click Apply To All.

Write the steps to insert a video stored on the computer into a slide. Model answer: Select the slide → Insert tab → Video → This Device → find and select the video file → Insert; then set Start (On Click or Automatically) on the Playback tab.

What is the slide master? Why is it useful? Model answer: The slide master is the top master slide that stores the design of the presentation — background, fonts, colours, placeholder positions, logo and footer. It is useful because a change made on it appears on every slide at once, saving time and keeping all slides consistent.

Name four views of PowerPoint and write the use of any two. Model answer: Normal, Outline View, Slide Sorter, Notes Page, Reading View, Slide Show (any four). Normal — editing one slide; Slide Sorter — reordering and deleting slides; Notes Page — writing speaker notes; Slide Show — presenting full screen (any two uses).

Write the keys used to start a slide show from the beginning, start from the current slide, show a black screen and end the show. Model answer: F5 — from the beginning; Shift + F5 — from the current slide; B — black screen; Esc — end the show.

Write any four rules for making effective slides. Model answer: Any four: one idea per slide; keywords not paragraphs (6 × 6 rule); large type (title 36–44 pt, body at least 24 pt); strong contrast between text and background; one consistent theme; relevant pictures and charts; few animations; check spelling; rehearse.

Write the steps to create a four-slide presentation on "Tourism in Nepal" with a title slide, a picture, a table and a transition on every slide. Model answer: Open PowerPoint → Blank Presentation. Slide 1 (Title Slide): type Tourism in Nepal and your name. Ctrl + M for slide 2 (Title and Content): type four points about tourist places. Ctrl + M for slide 3: Insert → Pictures → This Device → choose a photo of Pokhara → Insert, and add a title. Ctrl + M for slide 4: Insert → T

Explain the four types of animation effect and the three ways an animation can start. Model answer: Entrance (green) — the object appears, e.g. Fly In, Fade. Emphasis (yellow) — draws attention while visible, e.g. Pulse, Spin. Exit (red) — the object leaves, e.g. Fly Out, Disappear. Motion Paths — the object moves along a line, arc or custom path. Start options: On Click — waits for a click; With Previous — starts to

Describe any four slide views with the use of each. Model answer: Any four. Normal — one slide large with thumbnails and notes, for creating and editing. Outline — the text of all slides as an outline, for writing content. Slide Sorter — thumbnails of all slides, for reordering, deleting, hiding and setting transitions. Notes Page — the slide with its notes, for preparing the speaker

Differentiate between a web page and a website. Model answer: A web page is a single document on the World Wide Web, written in HTML and opened in a browser. A website is a collection of related web pages under one domain name, linked together, such as all the pages of neb.gov.np.

What is a URL? Name its parts in the example address https://www.myschool.edu.np/results.html. Model answer: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the full address of a resource on the web. In https://www.myschool.edu.np/results.html: https is the protocol, www.myschool.edu.np is the domain name (the server), and /results.html is the path to the page on that server.

What is a URL? Name its parts in https://www.moecdc.gov.np/index.html. Model answer: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the unique address of a resource on the web. Parts: protocol https://, domain name www.moecdc.gov.np, file name index.html.

Differentiate between the Internet and the World Wide Web. Model answer: The Internet is the worldwide network of networks — the cables, routers and computers joined by TCP/IP. The World Wide Web is one service that runs on the Internet: the collection of linked web pages opened in a browser. E-mail and video calls also use the Internet but are not the Web.

What do To, Cc and Bcc mean in an e-mail? Model answer: To: the main receivers of the message. Cc (carbon copy): others who get a copy; every receiver can see their addresses. Bcc (blind carbon copy): receivers whose addresses are hidden from all the others.

What is cloud storage? Give two examples. Model answer: Cloud storage keeps files on servers on the Internet instead of on your own device, so they can be opened from any device and are safe if a phone is lost. Examples: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud.

What is the digital divide? Write two ways to reduce it. Model answer: The digital divide is the gap between people who have devices, the Internet and the skills to use them and those who do not — for example, in the 2021 census 45.7% of households in municipalities but only 21.5% in rural municipalities had the Internet. Ways to reduce it: extend cheap broadband and mobile data to rural

What is e-governance? Explain G2C, G2B and G2G with Nepali examples. Model answer: E-governance is the use of ICT by the government to give its services and information to people quickly and openly (1 mark). G2C (government to citizen): the Nagarik App, launched in 2021, gives citizens their PAN, driving licence and other records on the phone. G2B (government to business): companies file taxes and re

Write two advantages and two disadvantages of ICT. Model answer: Advantages: quick and cheap communication across the world; online banking, shopping and learning from home; faster government services. Disadvantages: cyber crime, fraud and loss of privacy; addiction and health problems; the digital divide leaves poorer and rural people behind (any two of each).

Define ICT. Name any four components of an ICT system. Model answer: ICT is the use of computers, telecommunication equipment, networks and software to collect, store, process, send and receive information. Components (any four): hardware, software, data, network, people, procedures.

Write any two differences between radio and television. Model answer: Radio carries sound only, while television carries moving pictures and sound. A radio set is cheap and runs on batteries, so it reaches remote villages; a TV set costs more and needs more power. (Any two.)

What is a communication satellite? Write any two uses of satellites. Model answer: A communication satellite is a machine in orbit that receives signals from a ground station (uplink), strengthens them and sends them back to a wide area of the Earth (downlink). Uses (any two): satellite TV (DTH), satellite phones, Internet in remote places (VSAT), GPS navigation, weather forecasting.

Differentiate between the Internet and the WWW. Model answer: The Internet is the worldwide network of computer networks — the cables, devices and rules — and carries every service. The WWW is a collection of linked web pages that is only one service running on the Internet; e-mail and video calls use the Internet without using the Web.

What is video conferencing? Name two programs used for it. Model answer: Video conferencing is a live meeting over the Internet in which people at different places see and hear each other at the same time using cameras and microphones. Programs (any two): Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Jitsi Meet.

What is cloud storage? Write one advantage and one disadvantage of it. Model answer: Cloud storage is a service that keeps your files on a company's servers on the Internet so that you can open and share them from any device. Advantage: the files are safe even if your phone or computer is lost (or: they can be opened anywhere and shared). Disadvantage: you need the Internet to reach them (or: your data

What is e-governance? Give two examples of e-governance in Nepal. Model answer: e-Governance is the use of ICT by the government to give services and information to citizens, businesses and its own offices. Examples (any two): the Nagarik App, the online passport form, SEE and NEB results online, online tax filing with the Inland Revenue Department, the Hello Sarkar complaint service.

Name any two digital payment systems of Nepal and write one safety rule for using them. Model answer: Any two of eSewa, Khalti, IME Pay, Fonepay QR, connectIPS, mobile banking. Safety rule: never tell anyone your OTP or MPIN (or: use only the official app, keep the phone locked, check the amount and the receiver before confirming).

What is the digital divide? Write any two ways to reduce it. Model answer: The digital divide is the gap between people who have devices, the Internet and the skill to use ICT and people who do not. Ways (any two): cheaper data and devices; more towers and fibre in rural areas; community ICT centres and free Wi-Fi in schools and libraries; computer classes for adults; content in Nepali and lo
A 600 MB video is uploaded on a 40 Mbps connection. Find the shortest time the upload can take. Model answer: 600 MB × 8 = 4,800 Mb. Time = 4,800 ÷ 40 = 120 seconds = 2 minutes.

What is ICT? Explain any three uses of ICT in Nepal with an example of each. Model answer: ICT is the use of computers, telecommunication equipment, networks and software to collect, store, process, send and receive information (1 mark). Uses (any three, 1 mark each): Education — online classes, digital textbooks and results; e.g. Sikai Chautari lessons and SEE results published online. Banking — mobile bank

Describe any four communication technologies, giving an example of each from Nepal. Model answer: (Any four, 1 mark each.) Telephone (landline): turns the voice into an electrical signal that travels by wire through an exchange to the other telephone; two-way; e.g. a Nepal Telecom landline. Mobile phone: uses radio waves to the tower of its cell, and the towers are joined through the mobile exchange; carries calls,

What is the digital divide? Explain its causes in Nepal and suggest two ways to bridge it. Model answer: The digital divide is the gap between people who have access to ICT — devices, the Internet and the skill to use them — and people who do not (1 mark). Causes in Nepal (2 marks): the cost of devices and data; difficult hills and mountains where towers and cables are costly to build; weak electricity in some villages; l

What is computer ethics? Write any two of the Ten Commandments of computer ethics. Model answer: Computer ethics is the set of moral rules for using computers and the Internet rightly. Any two commandments (Computer Ethics Institute, 1992): do not use a computer to harm other people; do not snoop around in other people's files; do not use a computer to steal; do not copy or use software you have not paid for; do n

What is phishing? Write two signs of a phishing message. Model answer: Phishing is tricking people into giving passwords, OTPs, PINs or card numbers through a fake message, e-mail or website that looks as if it came from a bank, wallet or office. Signs: it creates urgency ("your account will be blocked today"); it asks for an OTP, PIN or password; the sender address or link is slightly wr

Differentiate between copyright and plagiarism. Model answer: Copyright is the legal right of the creator of a work — a book, song, film, photo or program — to control its copying and use; in Nepal it lasts for the author's life plus 50 years. Plagiarism is presenting someone else's words or work as your own without giving credit, such as copying an essay from a website into your

What is cyber bullying? What should a student do if it happens to them? Model answer: Cyber bullying is using phones, social media or games to insult, threaten, shame or harass someone again and again. The student should not reply, should save screenshots as evidence, block and report the bully on the platform, and tell a parent or teacher; serious cases can be reported to the Cyber Bureau.

Explain hacking, identity theft, software piracy and cyber bullying. Model answer: Hacking: getting into someone's computer, account or network without permission (an offence under section 45 of the ETA). Identity theft: stealing someone's personal details — name, photo, citizenship number, password — to pretend to be them, open fake accounts or cheat others. Software piracy: copying, selling or usin

Who is a digital citizen? Write any three rules for using social media safely. Model answer: A digital citizen is a person who uses the Internet and digital technology responsibly, safely and with respect for others (1 mark). Any three rules: think before you post — posts stay for ever; keep your accounts private and share no personal details such as address, phone number or school timetable; use strong, diffe

What is computer ethics? Write any two commandments of computer ethics. Model answer: Computer ethics is the set of moral principles that guide how we use computers, networks and the Internet. Commandments (any two): do not use a computer to harm other people; do not snoop in other people's files; do not use a computer to steal; do not copy or use paid software you have not paid for; always use a comput

Differentiate between ethics and law with two points. Model answer: Ethics are moral rules followed by choice, from conscience; laws are made by the state and everyone must obey them. Breaking an ethical rule brings shame or loss of trust; breaking a law brings a fine, prison or both.

What is hacking? Under which section of the ETA 2063 is unauthorised access punished, and what is the maximum punishment? Model answer: Hacking is getting into a computer, network or account without the owner's permission. Unauthorised access is punished under section 45 of the ETA 2063, with a fine up to Rs 2 lakh, or prison up to 3 years, or both.

What is phishing? Write any two signs of a phishing message. Model answer: Phishing is tricking people into giving their passwords, PINs, OTPs or card numbers through a fake message that seems to come from a trusted company. Signs (any two): a strange or misspelt web address; a demand for a password, MPIN or OTP; panic and a short deadline; "Dear customer" instead of your name; spelling mista

What is cyber bullying? Write two things a student should do if bullied online. Model answer: Cyber bullying is using phones, chat or social media to repeatedly hurt, threaten or shame someone. The student should (any two): not reply; keep screenshots as evidence; block and report the bully on the app; tell a parent or teacher (and the police in serious cases).

Differentiate between copyright infringement and plagiarism. Model answer: Copyright infringement is copying or using a work without the owner's permission; it is a legal offence under the Copyright Act. Plagiarism is using someone's work without giving credit; it is an ethical and academic offence. (Giving credit does not make unlicensed copying legal; permission does not make uncredited cop

What is software piracy? Write two harms of it. Model answer: Software piracy is copying, selling or using software without the owner's licence. Harms (any two): the programmers lose the money they earned; pirated copies often carry viruses; they get no security updates; it is illegal under the Copyright Act.

Write the full name of Nepal's cyber law and the date it was authenticated. Name two things to which it gives legal recognition. Model answer: The Electronic Transactions Act, 2063, authenticated and published on 22 Mansir 2063 BS (8 December 2006). It gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures.

What is a digital footprint? Give one example each of an active and a passive footprint. Model answer: A digital footprint is the record of everything a person does online. Active: a post, comment or photo you share on purpose. Passive: your search history, location data or cookies recorded without your notice.

Write any four rules for the safe use of social media. Model answer: Any four: use a strong, unique password and MFA; keep the profile private and accept only people you know; never share your address, phone number, location or ID card; think before posting; check facts before sharing; never share an OTP or MPIN; never meet an online friend alone; block and report bullies and fake accou

What is computer ethics? Explain any six of the Ten Commandments of computer ethics with an example of each. Model answer: Computer ethics is the set of moral principles that guide the use of computers, networks and the Internet (1 mark). Any six, half a mark each: (1) do not use a computer to harm others — e.g. posting a photo to embarrass a classmate; (2) do not interfere with others' computer work — e.g. switching off a friend's compute

What is cyber crime? Explain any three cyber crimes, with an example and one way of protection for each. Model answer: Cyber crime is any illegal act done by means of a computer, phone, network or the Internet (1 mark). Any three (1 mark each): Hacking — entering a computer or account without permission, e.g. breaking into a result system to change marks; protect with strong passwords, MFA and updates. Phishing — fake messages that tri

Describe the Electronic Transactions Act, 2063: when it was made, its aims, and any three offences with their punishments. Model answer: The Electronic Transactions Act, 2063 is Nepal's cyber law. It was authenticated and published on 22 Mansir 2063 BS (8 December 2006) and has 12 chapters and 80 sections (1 mark). Aims (1 mark): to give legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures; to make electronic transactions secure and reliable;

What is intellectual property? Explain copyright and plagiarism. How can a student avoid plagiarism in a project? Model answer: Intellectual property is a creation of the mind, such as a book, song, photo, program, invention or brand name; the rights that protect it are intellectual property rights (1 mark). Copyright is the legal right of a creator to copy, publish and sell an original work and stop others; it is automatic, and in Nepal lasts

Who is a digital citizen? Explain netiquette and any four rules for the safe use of social media. Model answer: A digital citizen is a person who uses the Internet and digital technology responsibly, safely and respectfully (1 mark). Netiquette is good manners online: be polite, do not write in capitals, do not spam, respect others' privacy, give credit, think before posting (1 mark). Safe use of social media (2 marks, any four)

Write any two ways a computer virus spreads. Model answer: Any two: infected pen drives and memory cards; pirated or cracked software and games; e-mail attachments and links from unknown senders; fake websites and apps; files shared over a network.

Write any four symptoms of a computer infected by a virus. Model answer: Any four: the computer becomes very slow or hangs; programs crash or the computer restarts by itself; files go missing, change, or cannot be opened; folders on a pen drive turn into shortcuts; unwanted pop-up adverts appear; the antivirus is switched off without your knowing; messages are sent from your account without

What is ransomware? Name one ransomware attack. Model answer: Ransomware is malware that locks (encrypts) a user's files or computer and demands money (a ransom) to unlock them. Example: WannaCry, which on 12 May 2017 locked more than 200,000 computers in over 150 countries and demanded 300 US dollars in Bitcoin.

What is antivirus software? Name two antivirus programs. Model answer: Antivirus software is a utility program that detects, blocks and removes viruses and other malware. Examples: Microsoft Defender, Avast, Kaspersky, Norton, ClamAV (any two).

Explain how antivirus software works, and differentiate between an antivirus and a firewall. Model answer: How it works: it compares files with a database of signatures (patterns of known malware) and also watches the behaviour of programs for suspicious actions; its real-time scanner checks every file as it is opened or downloaded; a found threat is cleaned, deleted or put in quarantine; the signature list must be updated

Write any four ways to protect a computer from viruses and other malware. Model answer: Any four: install an antivirus and keep it updated; turn on automatic updates for the operating system and apps; scan pen drives before opening them; download software only from official sites, never cracked copies; do not open attachments or links from unknown senders; keep backups by the 3-2-1 rule (three copies, two

What is a computer virus? Write any two ways by which it spreads. Model answer: A computer virus is a harmful program that attaches itself to other files, copies itself when the infected file is run, and damages data without the user's knowledge. It spreads (any two) through infected pen drives, pirated software, e-mail attachments, fake links and downloads, and shared network folders.

Differentiate between a virus and a worm. Model answer: A virus needs a host file and spreads only when a person runs the infected file; a worm is a complete program that copies itself over a network by itself. A virus mainly damages files; a worm mainly uses up network speed and computer resources.

What is a Trojan horse? Why is it given this name? Model answer: A Trojan horse is a harmful program disguised as a useful or attractive one, such as a free game or a software crack; it does harm (steals data, opens a backdoor) once installed and does not copy itself. It is named after the Greek story of soldiers hidden in a wooden horse given to Troy as a gift.

What is ransomware? Write one way to protect your files from it. Model answer: Ransomware is malware that locks a computer or encrypts its files and demands money to unlock them. Protection (any one): keep a backup on a disk that is unplugged after use or in cloud storage; install security updates; do not open unknown attachments.

Differentiate between spyware and adware. Model answer: Spyware hides and secretly collects information such as passwords and browsing and sends it to someone; adware shows unwanted adverts and is very visible. Example: a keylogger is spyware; a toolbar that keeps opening shopping sites is adware.

What is antivirus software? Name any two antivirus programs. Model answer: Antivirus software is a utility program that detects, blocks and removes viruses and other malware. Examples (any two): Microsoft Defender, Avast, AVG, Avira, Kaspersky, Norton 360, McAfee, Bitdefender, ESET NOD32, Quick Heal, ClamAV.

What is a virus signature? Why must antivirus software be updated regularly? Model answer: A virus signature is the recognisable pattern of code that identifies a known virus; antivirus programs keep a database of them. It must be updated because new malware appears every day, and an antivirus can recognise by signature only the malware whose signature is already in its database.

Differentiate between antivirus software and a firewall. Model answer: Antivirus software checks files and programs for malware and removes or quarantines it; a firewall checks the data entering and leaving through the network and blocks unauthorised connections. Antivirus uses a signature database; a firewall uses rules about which programs and addresses may connect.

What is a backup? Explain the 3-2-1 backup rule. Model answer: A backup is an extra copy of files kept somewhere else so that they can be recovered after loss or damage. The 3-2-1 rule: keep 3 copies of important files, on 2 different kinds of storage, with 1 copy away from the computer (for example in cloud storage).

What is malware? Explain any four types of malware with an example of each. Model answer: Malware (malicious software) is any program made to harm a computer or its user (1 mark). Any four (3 marks): Virus — attaches itself to a file and spreads when the file is run; e.g. Brain (boot sector virus). Worm — a separate program that copies itself over networks by itself; e.g. the Morris worm. Trojan horse — dis

Write a short history of computer viruses, describing any four important events. Model answer: Any four, 1 mark each: 1971 Creeper — Bob Thomas's program moved between ARPANET computers showing "I'M THE CREEPER: CATCH ME IF YOU CAN"; Reaper was written to delete it. 1982 Elk Cloner — a 15-year-old's program spread on Apple II floppy disks and showed a poem. 1983–84 — Fred Cohen demonstrated a self-copying progra

What is antivirus software? Explain how it detects and deals with malware. Model answer: Antivirus software is a utility program that detects, blocks and removes malware (1 mark). How it works (3 marks): signature checking — it compares files with a database of known virus signatures, which must be updated regularly; behaviour (heuristic) checking — it watches for suspicious actions such as a program chang

Explain any four ways of protecting a computer from viruses and other malware. Model answer: Any four, 1 mark each, with the reason: antivirus and firewall — real-time scanning removes malware and the firewall blocks unauthorised connections; updates — patches close the security holes that worms use, as WannaCry showed; safe browsing and downloading — official sites and stores only, no cracked software, no pop

A cyber café's computers have become slow, show adverts on every page, and the folders on customers' pen drives turn into shortcuts. Name the likely malware and write a plan to clean the computers and keep them safe. Model answer: The slowness and adverts point to adware (and possibly spyware) on the computers, and the shortcut folders to a pen-drive virus or worm (1 mark). Plan (3 marks): disconnect each infected computer from the network; update the antivirus and run a full scan, quarantining or deleting what it finds; uninstall unknown progra

Differentiate between a hub and a switch. Model answer: A hub copies every signal it receives to all its ports, so all computers share the speed and data can collide. A switch reads the MAC address and sends each frame only to the port of the destination computer, so it is faster and more private.

Differentiate between LAN and WAN with one example each. Model answer: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area such as a room, building or school campus and is fast — for example a school computer lab. A WAN (Wide Area Network) covers a country or the whole world and joins many LANs — for example the Internet, or the network joining a bank's branches across Nepal.

Name two wired and two wireless transmission media. Model answer: Wired: twisted-pair (UTP) cable, coaxial cable, optical fibre (any two). Wireless: radio waves (Wi-Fi), Bluetooth, microwave, satellite, infrared (any two).
A school's Internet connection is 16 Mbps. What is the shortest time to download a 120 MB video? Model answer: 120 MB = 120 × 8 = 960 megabits. Time = 960 ÷ 16 = 60 seconds (1 minute).

What is a computer network? Explain any four network components. Model answer: A computer network is two or more computers and devices connected by wired or wireless media to share data, hardware, software and an Internet connection (1 mark). Any three components: server — a powerful computer that provides services such as files, printing or websites to others; client — a computer that uses those

Why is the Internet called a network of networks? Explain with ISPs, packets and TCP/IP. Model answer: (1) The Internet is not one network: it is millions of LANs and WANs of homes, schools, companies and countries joined together by routers. (2) ISPs (Internet Service Providers) such as Nepal Telecom and WorldLink connect users to the Internet, and ISPs exchange traffic with each other (in Nepal at npIX) and with other

Define a computer network. Write two advantages of a network in a school. Model answer: A computer network is a group of two or more computers and devices connected by wired or wireless media to exchange data and share hardware, software and other resources. In a school: one printer and one Internet line can be shared by all the lab computers, and a teacher can give an exercise to the whole class through

What is a NIC? What is a MAC address? Model answer: A NIC (Network Interface Card) is the circuit or card that connects a computer to the network medium, through an RJ-45 port or a Wi-Fi radio. A MAC address is the permanent 48-bit number given to each NIC, written as six pairs of hexadecimal digits such as 3C-52-82-9A-7F-10, which identifies it on the local network.

What are a server and a client? Give one example of each. Model answer: A server is a powerful computer that provides services such as files, web pages or email to other computers, e.g. the web server that holds a school's website. A client is a computer or phone that requests and uses those services, e.g. a student's phone opening that website.

Write two differences between wired and wireless media, with one example of each. Model answer: Wired media carry signals along a cable and keep devices in one place; wireless media carry signals through the air and let devices move. Wired media are usually faster, steadier and safer from eavesdropping; wireless media are quicker to set up but affected by walls and distance. Example of wired: UTP cable; of wirele

What is a modem? Why does a fibre connection need an ONT instead? Model answer: A modem (modulator–demodulator) converts the computer's digital signals into signals that a telephone or cable line can carry, and converts them back on arrival. A fibre line carries light, not electrical signals, so an ONT (Optical Network Terminal) is needed to convert light into electrical signals and back.

Give two reasons why the star topology is used in most computer labs. Model answer: A faulty cable or computer cuts off only that one computer, so the rest of the lab keeps working; and computers are easy to add, remove and check, because each has its own cable to the switch. (Also: a switch gives every computer full speed.)
A 600 MB video is downloaded on a 40 Mbps connection. Find the shortest download time. Model answer: 600 MB × 8 = 4,800 Mb. Time = 4,800 Mb ÷ 40 Mbps = 120 s = 2 minutes.

Why is the Internet called a "network of networks"? Model answer: The Internet is not one network but millions of separate networks — home and school LANs, the networks of ISPs and companies, national and international WANs — owned by different people and joined by routers. Because all of them follow the same TCP/IP rules, data can pass from any one of them to any other.

What is network topology? Explain bus, ring and star topologies with neat diagrams. Model answer: Network topology is the pattern in which the computers and devices of a network are connected (1 mark). Hub — joins the computers of a star LAN and copies all data to every port. Switch — joins the computers of a LAN and sends data only to the destination's port using its MAC address. Router — joins different networks, such as a LAN and the

What are transmission media? Explain twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre cables. Model answer: Transmission media are the paths along which data travels between devices: wired (guided) or wireless (unguided) (1 mark). Twisted pair: four pairs of insulated copper wires twisted to reduce noise, inside a plastic jacket; cheap, up to 1 Gbps over 100 m, RJ-45 connector; used for LAN cables. Coaxial: a copper core wit

Explain LAN, MAN and WAN with one example of each. Write one difference between LAN and MAN. Model answer: LAN: a network within a room, building or campus, up to about 1 km, owned by one organisation, very fast — e.g. a school computer lab. MAN: a network covering a city or valley that joins many LANs — e.g. a cable-TV network in Kathmandu Valley, or a bank's branches in one city. WAN: a network across a country or the wor

Convert $(1110101101)_2$ into octal and hexadecimal. Model answer: Octal: groups of three from the right: 001 110 101 101 → 1, 6, 5, 5, so $(1655)_8$. Hexadecimal: groups of four from the right: 0011 1010 1101 → 3, A, D, so $(3AD)_{16}$. (Both equal 941 in decimal.)
How many megabytes and kilobytes are there in 2 GB? Model answer: 1 GB = 1024 MB, so 2 GB = 2 × 1024 = 2048 MB; 1 MB = 1024 KB, so 2048 × 1024 = 2,097,152 KB.

What is a number system? Define base (radix) with one example. Model answer: A number system is a way of writing numbers with a fixed set of digits and rules. Its base (radix) is the number of different digits it uses: binary has base 2 (digits 0 and 1), and decimal has base 10 (digits 0 to 9).

Why do computers use the binary number system? Model answer: A computer is made of electronic switches that have only two states, off and on, which are easy to make and to tell apart; they are written as 0 and 1. Storage also uses two states (magnetised one way or the other, charge or no charge), so all data is stored and processed as binary digits.

Convert $(1011101)_2$ into octal and hexadecimal. Model answer: Octal: 1 | 011 | 101 → 001 | 011 | 101 → $(135)_8$. Hexadecimal: 101 | 1101 → 0101 | 1101 → 5, D → $(\mathrm{5D})_{16}$. Check: the binary number is 64 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 93, and 64 + 24 + 5 = 93, 80 + 13 = 93.
How many bits are there in 2 KB? Show the working. Model answer: 2 KB = 2 × 1024 = 2,048 bytes, and each byte is 8 bits, so 2,048 × 8 = 16,384 bits.

Write the units of memory from the bit to the yottabyte in order, with the relation between each pair. A 32 GB memory card stores songs of 4 MB each. How many songs can it hold? Model answer: (a) 1 nibble = 4 bits; 1 byte = 8 bits; 1 KB = 1024 bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB; 1 TB = 1024 GB; 1 PB = 1024 TB; 1 EB = 1024 PB; 1 ZB = 1024 EB; 1 YB = 1024 ZB. (b) 32 GB = 32 × 1024 = 32,768 MB; 32,768 ÷ 4 = 8,192 songs. (c) Disk makers count 1 TB as 1,000,000,000,000 bytes (powers of 1000), but the computer

How many bytes does an uncompressed 800 × 600 picture with 24-bit colour need? Give the answer in KB too. Model answer: Pixels = 800 × 600 = 480,000; 24 bits = 3 bytes per pixel, so size = 480,000 × 3 = 1,440,000 bytes; ÷ 1024 = 1,406.25 KB (about 1.37 MB).

Differentiate between JPEG and PNG. Model answer: JPEG uses lossy compression: it throws away fine detail to make photographs very small, and it has no transparency. PNG uses lossless compression, keeps every pixel exactly, supports transparent backgrounds, and suits logos, screenshots and diagrams.

Differentiate between GIMP and Inkscape. Model answer: GIMP (GNU Image Manipulation Program) is a free raster editor for photographs and paintings, working pixel by pixel with layers. Inkscape is a free vector editor for logos, posters and diagrams that stay sharp at any size; it saves SVG files.

Write the full forms of BMP, JPEG, PNG, GIF and SVG, with one feature of each. Model answer: BMP — Bitmap: uncompressed, so files are very large. JPEG — Joint Photographic Experts Group: lossy, small files for photographs. PNG — Portable Network Graphics: lossless, supports transparency. GIF — Graphics Interchange Format: only 256 colours, supports simple animation. SVG — Scalable Vector Graphics: vector forma

Write the steps to make a Dashain greeting card in Paint and save it as a PNG file. Model answer: (1) Open Paint and set the page size with Resize (or Image Properties). (2) Use the Fill tool to colour the background, and the shapes tool (rectangle, star) with Colour 1 and Colour 2 for a border and decorations. (3) Use the Text tool (A) to type "Happy Dashain" and a short wish, choosing font, size and colour; draw

Define computer graphics. Write any two of its uses. Model answer: Computer graphics are pictures, drawings, charts and animations created, stored, edited and displayed with a computer. Uses (any two): advertising banners; animated films and games; CAD drawings of buildings; digital maps; X-ray and CT images in hospitals; diagrams in e-learning lessons.

What is a pixel? What does a screen resolution of 1366 × 768 mean? Model answer: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest unit of a digital picture, holding one colour. A resolution of 1366 × 768 means the screen has 1366 pixels across and 768 pixels down, 1,049,088 pixels in all.

Write any two differences between raster and vector graphics. Model answer: Raster graphics are made of pixels, while vector graphics are made of shapes described by numbers. A raster picture blurs or pixelates when enlarged, while a vector picture stays sharp at any size. (Also: raster suits photographs, vector suits logos and diagrams.)
Write the full forms of BMP, JPEG, GIF and SVG. Model answer: BMP — Bitmap; JPEG — Joint Photographic Experts Group; GIF — Graphics Interchange Format; SVG — Scalable Vector Graphics.

Name two free graphics programs and say whether each one is a raster or a vector program. Model answer: GIMP — a raster (photo-editing) program; Inkscape — a vector (drawing) program. (Paint, which comes free with Windows, is also raster.)

What are the uses of the Fill with colour tool and the Colour picker tool in Paint? Model answer: Fill with colour pours the chosen colour into a closed area, such as the inside of a circle. The Colour picker copies a colour from the picture and makes it the current colour, so the same shade can be used again.

Differentiate between lossy and lossless compression, with one format of each. Model answer: Lossless compression makes a file smaller while keeping every pixel exactly, e.g. PNG (or GIF). Lossy compression throws away small details to make the file much smaller, and the original cannot be got back, e.g. JPEG.

Find the size in KB of an uncompressed 800 × 600 picture in 24-bit colour (1 KB = 1024 bytes). Model answer: Pixels = 800 × 600 = 480,000. 24 bits = 3 bytes, so size = 480,000 × 3 = 1,440,000 bytes = 1,440,000 ÷ 1024 = 1,406.25 KB (about 1.37 MB).

What is a layer in GIMP? Give one advantage of using layers. Model answer: A layer is like a transparent sheet laid over a picture; each part of the picture can be on its own layer. Advantage: one part, such as the text, can be moved, changed or hidden without disturbing the rest of the picture.

What is colour depth? How many colours can an 8-bit picture show? Model answer: Colour depth is the number of bits used to store the colour of one pixel. An 8-bit picture can show $2^8 = 256$ colours.

What are raster and vector graphics? Explain each with two examples and write any four differences between them. Model answer: Raster graphics are pictures made of a grid of pixels, each holding one colour; examples: a phone photograph, a scanned certificate. Vector graphics store pictures as shapes — points, lines, curves and filled areas — described by numbers; examples: a school logo, a map of Nepal's provinces. Differences (any four): (1)

Describe the image formats BMP, JPEG, PNG, GIF and SVG: give the type, the kind of compression and one use of each. Model answer: BMP (Bitmap): raster, uncompressed, very large files; used by simple Windows programs. JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group): raster, lossy compression, 16.7 million colours, no transparency; used for photographs. PNG (Portable Network Graphics): raster, lossless, supports transparency; used for logos, screenshots an

Write the steps to draw a greeting card in Paint using shapes, colours and text, and to save it as a PNG file. Name the tools you use. Model answer: (1) Open Paint from the Start menu and set the canvas size with Image properties (Ctrl+E). (2) Fill the background with the Fill with colour tool. (3) Draw hills, a kite or a house with the Shapes tools (curve, polygon, oval, rectangle), choosing Size and Colour 1; hold Shift for a perfect circle or square. (4) Fill ea

A camera takes photos of 4000 × 3000 pixels in 24-bit colour. Model answer: (a) 4000 × 3000 = 12,000,000 pixels (12 megapixels). (b) 12,000,000 × 3 bytes = 36,000,000 bytes; ÷ 1024 ÷ 1024 ≈ 34.3 MB. (c) 34.3 ÷ 3.5 ≈ 9.8 times smaller — the effect of lossy compression. (d) 16 GB = 16 × 1024 = 16,384 MB; 16,384 ÷ 3.5 = 4,681.1, so 4,681 photos.

Differentiate between linear and interactive multimedia. Model answer: Linear multimedia plays from beginning to end in a fixed order, and the user only watches, like a film or a TV advertisement. Interactive multimedia lets the user control it — click, choose, answer — like a game, a website or the E-Paath lessons.

Differentiate between animation and video. Model answer: Video is recorded from real life with a camera. Animation is made of drawn or computer-made pictures shown quickly, usually 12 to 30 a second, so that they seem to move.

Name two input devices and two output devices used for multimedia. Model answer: Input: microphone, webcam, digital camera, scanner, graphics tablet (any two). Output: monitor, speakers, headphones, projector (any two).

Write two uses of multimedia in health. Model answer: Any two: medical images such as X-ray, CT and MRI scans; telemedicine — video consultations with distant doctors; training doctors and nurses with videos and 3D models; health awareness campaigns with videos and animations.

Explain the uses of multimedia in education, entertainment and business. Model answer: Education: interactive lessons (E-Paath), videos and animations, projectors in classrooms and online classes make learning interesting and easier to understand. Entertainment: films, music, video games, YouTube and virtual reality. Business: advertisements, product videos on shopping sites such as Daraz, presentations

Write two advantages and two disadvantages of multimedia. How many bytes does one minute of uncompressed CD-quality stereo sound need (44,100 samples a second, 16 bits, 2 channels)? Model answer: Advantages: it holds attention and makes learning interesting; it explains hard ideas with pictures, sound and motion; it suits learners who learn by seeing, hearing or doing; it can reach a large audience. Disadvantages: making it takes time, skill and costly equipment; its large files need storage and fast Internet;

What is multimedia? Name its five elements. Model answer: Multimedia is the combined use of two or more forms of media to present information, usually with a computer. Its five elements are text, graphics, audio, video and animation.

Write two differences between video and animation. Model answer: A video is recorded from real life with a camera, while an animation is made of drawn or computer-generated pictures. Video shows real people and places (a cricket match); animation can show anything that can be drawn, including imaginary things (a cartoon, a moving diagram of the heart).

Differentiate between linear and interactive multimedia with one example each. Model answer: Linear multimedia plays from start to end in a fixed order and the viewer only watches, e.g. a TV advertisement. Interactive multimedia lets the user choose and responds to clicks and answers, e.g. an E-Paath lesson or a video game.

Name any two input devices and two output devices used in multimedia. Model answer: Input: microphone, webcam, digital camera, scanner, graphics tablet (any two). Output: monitor, speakers, headphones, projector (any two).

What is the use of Model answer: (a) A graphics card (GPU) draws pictures, 3D scenes and video frames on the screen quickly. (b) A sound card changes sound from the microphone into digital form and changes digital sound back into sound for the speakers.

Write any two uses of multimedia in education. Model answer: Interactive lessons such as E-Paath make learning interesting and give practice with feedback; teachers show videos, animations and simulations with a projector; students join online classes and watch tutorials (any two).

Write any two uses of multimedia in health. Model answer: Doctors study X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI images on screens; telemedicine lets a remote health post consult a specialist by video call; doctors and nurses are trained with videos and 3D animations; awareness videos teach people about vaccination and hygiene (any two).

Name one program for each job: playing a video, editing sound, editing video, making a 3D animation. Model answer: Playing a video: VLC media player. Editing sound: Audacity. Editing video: OpenShot (or Kdenlive or CapCut). 3D animation: Blender.

A 2-minute voice recording uses 22,050 samples per second, 16 bits per sample and 1 channel (mono). Find its uncompressed size in KB (1 KB = 1024 bytes). Model answer: Bytes = 22,050 × 16 × 1 × 120 ÷ 8 = 5,292,000 bytes; ÷ 1024 = 5,167.97 KB (about 5.05 MB).

Define multimedia. Explain its five elements with one example of each. Model answer: Multimedia is the combined use of two or more forms of media — text, graphics, audio, video and animation — to present information, usually with a computer (1 mark). Text: letters, numbers and symbols, e.g. the title and instructions of a lesson. Graphics: still pictures such as photos, diagrams and maps, e.g. a labell

What is a multimedia system? Describe the input, output and storage devices and the software it needs. Model answer: A multimedia system is a computer (or phone or tablet) with the hardware to capture, store and play sound, pictures and video, and the software to make, edit and play multimedia. Input devices: microphone (sound), webcam and digital camera (pictures and video), scanner (printed pictures), graphics tablet (drawing). Out

Entertainment: films, music videos, cartoons and video games, watched on TV, YouTube and phones. Business: adverts, product photos and videos on Daraz, presentations, training videos

Write any four advantages and any four disadvantages of multimedia. Disadvantages: (1) making it needs time, skill a

Write any two features of a good algorithm. Model answer: Any two: finiteness — it ends after a limited number of steps; definiteness — every step is clear and has only one meaning; input and output — it states what it receives and produces at least one result; effectiveness — every step can actually be carried out.

Write two differences between an algorithm and a flowchart. Model answer: An algorithm is written in words as numbered steps, while a flowchart is drawn with standard symbols joined by arrows. An algorithm is quicker to write and change; a flowchart makes branches and loops easier to see.
Write an algorithm to find the average of four numbers. Model answer: Step 1: Start. Step 2: Read A, B, C and D. Step 3: SUM = A + B + C + D. Step 4: AVG = SUM ÷ 4. Step 5: Display AVG. Step 6: Stop.

What is pseudocode? Write pseudocode to find the sum of two numbers. Model answer: Pseudocode is an algorithm written in short, structured English statements with keywords such as INPUT, PRINT, IF … ENDIF and WHILE … ENDWHILE; it looks like a program but cannot be run. Example: BEGIN / INPUT A, B / SET S = A + B / PRINT S / END.

Step 4: S = S + I. Step 5: I = I + 2, and go to step 3. Step 6: Display S. Step 7: Stop. Flowchart. Start → rectangle "S = 0, I = 2" → diamond "Is I ≤ 50?" → Yes: rectangle "S = S + I" → rectangle "I = I + 2" → arrow back to

Explain the steps of program development. Model answer: (1) Problem analysis: understand the problem and list its input, process and output. (2) Program design: plan the steps with an algorithm, flowchart or pseudocode. (3) Coding: write the program in a language such as QBASIC. (4) Testing and debugging: run it with test data and remove errors. (5) Documentation: write com

What is an algorithm? Write any two features of a good algorithm. Model answer: An algorithm is a finite set of clear, step-by-step instructions for solving a problem, from Start to Stop. Any two features: it has input and output; every step is definite (one meaning only); it is finite (it ends); every step is effective (can be carried out).

Draw the symbols for terminal, input/output, process and decision, and write the use of each. Model answer: Terminal — an oval, used for Start and Stop. Input/output — a parallelogram, used to read data or display results. Process — a rectangle, used for a calculation or assignment. Decision — a diamond, used for a yes/no question with two exits.

Write any two differences between an algorithm and a flowchart. Model answer: An algorithm is written in words as numbered steps, while a flowchart is drawn with standard symbols joined by arrows. An algorithm is quicker to write and change, while a flowchart is easier to follow, especially for branches and loops.
Write an algorithm to find the area of a rectangle. Model answer: Step 1: Start. Step 2: Read the length L and breadth B. Step 3: A = L × B. Step 4: Display A. Step 5: Stop.

What is selection? Give one example from daily life. Model answer: Selection is a control structure in which a condition is tested and one of two (or more) paths is followed depending on whether it is true or false. Example: if the traffic light is green, cross the road; otherwise wait.

What is a loop? What is an infinite loop? Model answer: A loop is a group of steps that is repeated while a condition is true (or a fixed number of times). An infinite loop is a loop whose condition never becomes false, usually because the update step is missing, so it repeats for ever.

Write an algorithm and draw a flowchart to find the area and circumference of a circle of radius R. Model answer: Algorithm. Step 1: Start. Step 2: Read R. Step 3: A = 3.14 × R × R. Step 4: C = 2 × 3.14 × R. Step 5: Display A and C. Step 6: Stop. Flowchart. Start (oval) → Read R (parallelogram) → A = 3.14 × R × R (rectangle) → C = 2 × 3.14 × R (rectangle) → Display A, C (parallelogram) → Stop (oval), joined top to bottom by arrows

If yes, display "Eligible to vote"; otherwise display "Not eligible". Step 4: Stop. Flowchart. If no, go to step 7. Step 5: F = F × I. Step 6: I = I + 1, and go to step 4. Step 7: Display F. Step 8: Stop. Flowchart. What is a flowchart? Write any four rules for drawing a flowchart and any two of its advantages. Model answer: A flowchart is a pictorial representation of an algorithm using standard symbols joined by flow lines (1 mark). Any four rules: one Start and one Stop; use standard symbols only; flow from top to bottom and left to right with an arrowhead on every line; a decision has two labelled exits (Yes/No); flow lines do not cros

Differentiate between machine language and assembly language. Model answer: Machine language is written in binary (0s and 1s), is understood directly by the processor and needs no translator. Assembly language uses short words called mnemonics, such as MOV and ADD, and needs an assembler to translate it into machine code. Both are low-level and machine-dependent.

Differentiate between a syntax error and a logical error, with an example of each. Model answer: A syntax error breaks the grammar rules of the language, so the program does not run, for example PRNT for PRINT. A logical error is a mistake in the method, so the program runs but the output is wrong, for example A = L + B for the area of a rectangle.

Write any three features of high-level languages, and name four high-level languages with the person who created each. Model answer: Features (any three): English-like words and mathematical signs; easy to write, read and correct; portable (machine-independent); must be translated by a compiler or interpreter; one statement does the work of many machine instructions (2 marks). Languages (2 marks): BASIC — John Kemeny and Thomas Kurtz (1964), whose Q

Write any two differences between a low-level and a high-level language. Model answer: A low-level language (machine or assembly) is close to the hardware and machine-dependent, while a high-level language uses English-like words and is portable. Low-level programs are hard to write and correct but run very fast; high-level programs are easy to write and correct but must be translated by a compiler or in

What is a language processor? Name its three types. Model answer: A language processor (translator) is a program that converts a program written in assembly or a high-level language into machine language. Its three types are the compiler, the interpreter and the assembler.

Write any two differences between a compiler and an interpreter. Model answer: A compiler translates the whole program at once, while an interpreter translates and runs one line at a time. A compiler makes an object program that runs without it, while an interpreter makes no object program and is needed every time. (Also: a compiler lists all errors after checking the whole program; an interprete

What is assembly language? Why does it need an assembler? Model answer: Assembly language is a low-level language that uses short words called mnemonics (such as MOV, ADD, SUB) in place of binary instructions. The processor understands only machine language, so an assembler must translate the mnemonics into binary before the program can run.

Define syntax error and logical error with one example each. Model answer: A syntax error breaks the grammar rules of the language, for example PRIMT "Hello" instead of PRINT "Hello". A logical error is a mistake in the method, so the program runs but gives a wrong result, for example AVG = A + B / 2 instead of AVG = (A + B) / 2.

What is a run-time error? Give two examples. Model answer: A run-time error is an error that occurs while the program is running, when it is asked to do something impossible, and it stops the program with a message. Examples: dividing a number by zero; the square root of a negative number; storing a number too large for its variable (overflow).

What is debugging? Write any two ways of debugging a program. Model answer: Debugging is the process of finding and correcting the errors (bugs) in a program. Any two ways: reading the error messages; dry running the program with a trace table; printing the values of variables at different points; stepping through it line by line (F8 in QBASIC) or using breakpoints (F9).

Define constant and variable with one example of each. Model answer: A constant is a value that does not change while the program runs, for example 25 or "Nepal". A variable is a named memory location whose value can change while the program runs, for example AGE in AGE = 14.

Write any four rules for naming a variable in QBASIC. Model answer: Any four: it must begin with a letter; it may contain letters, digits and a full stop; it may be up to 40 characters long; it must not contain spaces or other symbols except a type symbol at the end; it must not be a keyword such as PRINT or END.

What is a programming language? Explain machine language, assembly language and high-level language, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each. Model answer: A programming language is a set of words, symbols and rules used to write instructions for a computer (1 mark). Machine language: written in 0s and 1s; advantage — runs directly and fastest, needs no translation; disadvantage — very hard to write and correct, and machine-dependent. Assembly language: uses mnemonics suc

Explain compiler, interpreter and assembler. Which translator is used for QBASIC programs and which for C programs? Model answer: A compiler translates the whole high-level program at once into an object program (such as an.exe file), lists all errors after checking, and the object program then runs fast without the compiler. An interpreter translates and carries out one line at a time, stops at the first error, makes no object program and is nee

What are testing and debugging? Explain the three types of programming error with one example each. Model answer: Testing is running a program with test data whose correct results are known and comparing the outputs; debugging is finding and correcting the errors (1 mark). Syntax error: breaking the rules of the language, found by the translator, e.g. PRIMT for PRINT. Run-time error: an impossible operation while the program runs,

Explain compiler, interpreter and assembler. Which translator is used for Python programs and which for C programs? Model answer: A compiler translates the whole high-level program at once into an object program (such as an.exe file), lists all errors after checking, and the object program then runs fast without the compiler.
