concepts.t: The table shows SEE pass rates of a school: 2078 – 62%, 2079 – 70%, 2080 – 68%, 2081 – 85%. Write a description. Model answer: Model: The table shows the SEE pass rate of the school from 2078 to 2081. Overall, the rate improved by 23 percentage points. It rose from 62% in 2078 to 70% in 2079, fell slightly to 68% in 2080, and then jumped sharply to 85% in 2081, the highest in the period.

concepts.u: The Magic Mirror / Poem: If I was
concepts.t: Write a news story: a fire in Kalanki market; 15 shops burnt; no deaths; loss of about Rs 2 crore; short circuit suspected; fire brigade controlled it after three hours. Model answer: Headline (Fire Destroys 15 Shops in Kalanki), byline, dateline, a lead answering what/where/when/how (Fifteen shops were burnt in a fire at Kalanki market on … night), body with the loss, cause, fire brigade's work and no casualties; past tense; third person.

concepts.u: Conservation of Earth / An Official Notice
concepts.t: Write a notice on behalf of your school's Eco Club about a cleanliness campaign. Model answer: School name, date, NOTICE, title, what (cleanliness campaign), when, where, who should take part, what to bring (gloves, sacks), the issuer (Coordinator, Eco Club).

concepts.u: Conservation of Earth / An Official Notice
concepts.t: Write an opinion essay: "Should mobile phones be allowed in school?" Model answer: Clear opinion in the introduction; two or three reasons with examples; the opposing view and your reply; conclusion; connectives of reason and contrast.

concepts.u: An Anecdote: Why I Became a Vegan /
concepts.t: Write two paragraphs on "The Unification of Nepal" or any historical event you have studied. Model answer: Time order, correct dates and names, causes, main events and results; past tenses; a concluding sentence on the event's importance.

concepts.u: Road Accidents in Nepal: Are Poor Roads Solely
concepts.t: Write an opinion essay: "Should students be allowed to ride motorbikes to school?" Model answer: Clear opinion; reasons (safety, age and licence rules, maturity, cost, alternatives such as bicycles and school buses); the other side (saves time, lack of transport); conclusion restating the opinion; connectives.

concepts.u: A Tale of Two Birds / News Report:
concepts.t: Write a news report: a landslide in Myagdi; three houses buried; two people injured; rescue by Nepal Army and locals; road blocked for two days. Model answer: Headline (Landslide Buries Three Houses in Myagdi), byline, dateline, lead (what, where, when, casualties), body (rescue work, injured taken to hospital, road blocked, a reported statement from an official), third person, past tense.

concepts.u: The Old Woman and the Lime Tree /
concepts.t: Explain: "Nothing is easy and nothing is impossible." Model answer: Every goal needs effort, so nothing comes easily; but with determination and courage every goal can be reached.

Find the curved surface area and the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Model answer: Curved surface $=2\times\frac{22}{7}\times7\times10=440$ cm²; volume $=\frac{22}{7}\times49\times10=1540$ cm³.

A rectangular garden 28 m long and 20 m wide has a circular pond of radius 7 m. Find Model answer: (a) Pond $=\pi r^2=\frac{22}{7}\times7\times7=154$ m².(b) Garden $=28\times20=560$ m², so grass area $=560-154=406$ m².(c) Cost $=406\times25=\text{Rs }10{,}150$.

A trapezium-shaped field has parallel sides 30 m and 18 m, and the distance between them is 12 m. Find its area. The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. Find its area, its side and its perimeter. Model answer: (a) Area of a trapezium $=\frac12(a+b)h=\frac12(30+18)\times12=288$ m².(b) Area of a rhombus $=\frac12d_1d_2=\frac12\times16\times12=96$ cm². The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 8 cm and 6 cm: side $=\sqrt{64+36}=\sqrt{100}=10$ cm. Perimeter $=4\

The marks of 20 students are: 35, 42, 48, 55, 60, 62, 65, 68, 70, 72, 74, 75, 78, 80, 82, 85, 88, 90, 92, 95. Find the mean and the median, and say why they are close together here. Model answer: Mean. The sum is $35+42+48+55+60+62+65+68+70+72+74+75+78+80+82+85+88+90+92+95=1416$, so $\bar x=\frac{1416}{20}=70.8$. Median. With $n=20$ (even) it is the mean of the 10th and 11th values: $\frac{72+74}{2}=73$. Why they are close. The values rise steadily with no extreme value and no gap, so there is no outlier to pul

A survey of 180 families found 45 with no bicycle, 90 with one, 36 with two and 9 with three. Draw a pie chart, and find the mean number of bicycles per family. Model answer: Pie chart. Total families $=45+90+36+9=180$, so one family is $\frac{360}{180}=2°$.

The marks of 10 students are 12, 15, 11, 15, 18, 20, 15, 14, 16, 12. Arrange them in order and find the mean, median and mode. Model answer: Ascending order: 11, 12, 12, 14, 15, 15, 15, 16, 18, 20. Sum $=148$, so the mean $=148\div10=14.8$. With $n=10$ the median is the average of the 5th and 6th values: $\frac{15+15}{2}=15$. The mode is the most frequent value, 15 (it occurs three times). Check: the three averages are close together because there are no ex

Find the mean of the data: $x=2,3,4,5,6$ with frequencies $f=3,5,8,3,1$. The monthly incomes of five families are Rs 12,000, 14,000, 15,000, 16,000 and 1,43,000. Find the mean and the median, and say which is the better Model answer: (a) $\sum f=3+5+8+3+1=20$. $\sum fx=6+15+32+15+6=74$. Mean $=\dfrac{74}{20}=3.7$.(b) Mean $=\dfrac{12000+14000+15000+16000+143000}{5}=\dfrac{200000}{5}=\text{Rs }40{,}000$. The median is the middle value of the ordered data: Rs 15,000. The median is the better average here: the one very high income pulls the mean up to
Write $A=\{2,4,6,8,10\}$ in set-builder form and find $n(A)$. Model answer: $A=\{x:x$ is an even number and $2\le x\le10\}$, and $n(A)=5$.
Convert $(100)_{10}$ into binary and into base 5. Model answer: In binary: $64+32+4=100$, so $(1100100)_2$. In base 5: $100=4\times25$, so $(400)_5$.

Write $0.\overline{6}$ and $0.\overline{18}$ as fractions. Model answer: $x=0.\overline{6}$ gives $9x=6$, so $x=\frac69=\frac23$. $x=0.\overline{18}$ gives $99x=18$, so $x=\frac{18}{99}=\frac{2}{11}$.
Simplify $\sqrt{48}$ and $\sqrt{12}+\sqrt{27}$. Model answer: $\sqrt{48}=\sqrt{16\times3}=4\sqrt{3}$. And $\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}$, $\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt{3}$, so the sum is $5\sqrt{3}$.
Show that $\sqrt{2}$ lies between 1.4 and 1.5. Model answer: $1.4^2=1.96$ and $1.5^2=2.25$. Since $1.96<2<2.25$, taking square roots gives $1.4<\sqrt{2}<1.5$.

Write three rational numbers between $\frac13$ and $\frac12$. Classify each of these as rational or irrational, with a reason: $\sqrt{16}$, $\sqrt{20}$, $\frac{22}{7}$, $0.25$, $\pi$, $\sqrt{0.09}$. Model answer: (a) Write both with denominator 24: $\frac13=\frac{8}{24}$ and $\frac12=\frac{12}{24}$. Any numerators 9, 10, 11 fit between, giving $\frac{9}{24}=\frac38$, $\frac{10}{24}=\frac{5}{12}$ and $\frac{11}{24}$.(b) $\sqrt{16}=4$: rational (a whole number). $\sqrt{20}$: irrational, since 20 is not a perfect square and its de

The Sun is $1.496\times10^{8}$ km from the Earth and light travels at $3\times10^{5}$ km per second. Model answer: (a) $t=\dfrac{1.496\times10^{8}}{3\times10^{5}}=0.4987\times10^{3}=4.987\times10^{2}\approx499$ seconds. In minutes: $498.7\div60=8.31\approx8.3$ minutes.(b) $0.000045=4.5\times10^{-5}$ (move the point 5 places to the right). $6.02\times10^{4}=60{,}200$ (move the point 4 places to the right).
If 8 men can do a job in 15 days, how long will 12 men take? Model answer: Total work $=8\times15=120$ man-days; with 12 men the time is $120\div12=10$ days.
Find the profit percent when an article bought for Rs 2,500 is sold for Rs 2,800. Model answer: Profit $=300$; profit percent $=\frac{300}{2500}\times100=12\%$.

A shopkeeper marks his goods 40 % above the cost price and then allows a discount of 20 % on the marked price. Find his profit percent, and explain why the profit is not 20 %. Model answer: Take CP $=$ Rs 100. Then $\text{MP}=100\times1.40=\text{Rs }140$, and the discount is 20 % of the marked price: $0.20\times140=\text{Rs }28$, so $\text{SP}=140-28=\text{Rs }112$. Profit $=112-100=\text{Rs }12$, that is 12 % on the cost. Why not 20 %. The 40 % is added to the cost price while the 20 % discount comes off

A refrigerator has a marked price of Rs 40,000. The shopkeeper allows a 15% discount and then charges 13% VAT on the discounted price. Model answer: (a) Discount $=15\%\times40000=\text{Rs }6000$, so SP before VAT $=40000-6000=\text{Rs }34{,}000$.(b) VAT $=13\%\times34000=\text{Rs }4{,}420$ (VAT goes on the discounted price).(c) Bill $=34000+4420=\text{Rs }38{,}420$.(d) Profit $=34000-30000=\text{Rs }4000$, and profit $\%=\dfrac{4000}{30000}\times100=13\tfrac13\%$

An agent earns 5% commission on the first Rs 1,00,000 of sales in a month and 8% on the rest. In one month his sales are Rs 2,50,000. Find Model answer: (a) First part: $5\%\times100000=\text{Rs }5000$. Remaining sales $=250000-100000=\text{Rs }150{,}000$, and $8\%\times150000=\text{Rs }12{,}000$. Commission $=5000+12000=\text{Rs }17{,}000$.(b) Total income $=17000+8000=\text{Rs }25{,}000$.(c) Average rate $=\dfrac{17000}{250000}\times100=6.8\%$, which lies between 5%
If 9 kg of potatoes cost Rs 315, find the cost of 14 kg. Model answer: 1 kg costs $315\div9=\text{Rs }35$; 14 kg cost $14\times35=\text{Rs }490$.

A bus travels 240 km from Pokhara to Bharatpur at 60 km/h and returns by the same road at 40 km/h. Find the time for each journey, the total time, and the average speed for the whole trip. Why is the average not 50 km/h? Model answer: Going: $240\div60=4$ hours. Returning: $240\div40=6$ hours. Total time $=4+6=10$ hours for $240+240=480$ km, so average speed $=480\div10=48$ km/h. It is not $\frac{60+40}{2}=50$ km/h because the bus spends more time at the slower speed (6 hours at 40 km/h against 4 hours at 60 km/h), so the slower speed counts more.

A hostel has food for 60 students for 24 days. After 8 days, 20 students leave. For how many more days will the remaining food last the remaining students? Model answer: Total food $=60\times24=1440$ student-days. In 8 days the 60 students eat $60\times8=480$ student-days, leaving $1440-480=960$. The remaining students number $60-20=40$, so the food lasts $960\div40=24$ more days (inverse variation: fewer students, more days). The whole stay is $8+24=32$ days.

Find the simple interest and the amount on Rs 24,000 at 8% p.a. for $2\tfrac12$ years. At what rate per cent p.a. will Rs 24,000 amount to Rs 31,200 in 3 years? Model answer: (a) $I=\dfrac{PTR}{100}=\dfrac{24000\times2.5\times8}{100}=\text{Rs }4{,}800$, so the amount $=24000+4800=\text{Rs }28{,}800$.(b) Interest $=31200-24000=\text{Rs }7200$, and $R=\dfrac{I\times100}{PT}=\dfrac{7200\times100}{24000\times3}=10\%$ p.a.

A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. Model answer: (a) Doubling means interest $=P$ in 8 years, so $R=\dfrac{100\times P}{P\times8}=12.5\%$ p.a.(b) To become three times, the interest must be $2P$: $T=\dfrac{2P\times100}{P\times12.5}=16$ years.(c) $T=\frac{9}{12}=\frac34$ year, so $I=\dfrac{15000\times\frac34\times12}{100}=\text{Rs }1{,}350$. Always convert months to y
Factorise $x^2+7x+12$ by finding two numbers whose product is 12 and whose sum is 7, and check by expanding. Model answer: The two numbers are 3 and 4, because $3\times4=12$ and $3+4=7$. So
Solve $2x+5\ge11$ and show the solution on a number line. Model answer: $2x\ge6$, so $x\ge3$: a filled circle at 3 with the shading to the right.

Solve $3x+2y=16$ and $2x-y=6$ by the elimination method, and check both equations. Model answer: Step 1 — make the $y$ coefficients match. The second equation times 2 gives $4x-2y=12$. Step 2 — add (the $y$ terms have opposite signs):
Two angles are complementary and one is four times the other. Find both. Model answer: $x+4x=90$, so $5x=90$ and $x=18°$; the angles are 18° and 72°.
Two straight lines intersect and one angle is 42°. Find the other three. Model answer: 42° (vertically opposite), 138° and 138° (each supplementary to 42°).
Two angles of a triangle are 55° and 65°. Find the third and say what kind of triangle it is. Model answer: $180-(55+65)=60°$; all angles are less than 90°, so it is acute-angled.
In a parallelogram one angle is 72°. Find the other three angles. Model answer: The opposite angle is 72° and the other two are each $180-72=108°$.
A chord of length 24 cm is 5 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius. Model answer: Half the chord is 12 cm, so $r=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}=13$ cm.

The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2:3:4$. Find them and name the triangle by its angles. The vertical angle of an isosceles triangle is $40^\circ$. Find the base angles. Model answer: (a) Parts $2+3+4=9$, and one part $=180\div9=20^\circ$. The angles are $40^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $80^\circ$: all acute, all different, so it is an acute-angled scalene triangle.(b) The base angles are equal: $\dfrac{180-40}{2}=70^\circ$ each.

State the five tests of congruence, naming the parts each uses. Model answer: SSS — all three sides. SAS — two sides and the included angle. ASA — two angles and the side between them. AAS — two angles and a side not between them. RHS — the right angle, the hypotenuse and one other side.

Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 8 cm and 12 cm. Find the scale factor and the ratio of their areas. Model answer: Scale factor $=\frac{12}{8}=1.5$; ratio of areas $=\left(\frac{8}{12}\right)^2=\frac{64}{144}=\frac49$, that is $4:9$.

In two triangles $\angle A=\angle D=65°$ and $\angle B=\angle E=45°$. Prove the triangles similar and state the third pair of equal angles. Model answer: Two angles of one equal two angles of the other, so the triangles are similar by AA. The third pair is $\angle C=\angle F=180-(65+45)=70°$.

In a quadrilateral $ABCD$, the diagonal $AC$ bisects both $\angle A$ and $\angle C$. Prove that $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle ADC$ and hence that $AB=AD$ and $CB=CD$. Model answer: Given. $\angle BAC=\angle DAC$ and $\angle BCA=\angle DCA$ (the diagonal bisects both angles). To prove. $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle ADC$, so $AB=AD$ and $CB=CD$.

In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB=CD$ and $AB\parallel CD$. Draw the diagonal $AC$ and prove that triangles $ABC$ and $CDA$ are congruent. Hence show that $BC=AD$. Model answer: Given: $AB=CD$, $AB\parallel CD$. To prove: $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle CDA$. Proof: (i) $AB=CD$ (given). (ii) $\angle BAC=\angle DCA$ (alternate angles, since $AB\parallel CD$ and $AC$ is the transversal). (iii) $AC=CA$ (common side). So $\triangle ABC\cong\triangle CDA$ by SAS. Corresponding parts of congruent trian

A pole 3 m high casts a shadow 2 m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow 14 m long. Find the height of the tree. Are all squares similar? Are all rhombuses similar? Give reasons. Model answer: (a) The sun's rays make the same angle, so the pole with its shadow and the tree with its shadow form similar right triangles: $\dfrac{\text{height of tree}}{3}=\dfrac{14}{2}$, so the height $=3\times7=21$ m.(b) All squares are similar: every angle is $90^\circ$ and the ratio of corresponding sides is the same for any

A square pyramid has a base of side 10 cm and a vertical height of 12 cm. Find its slant height, volume, lateral surface area and total surface area. Model answer: Half the base is 5 cm, and the slant height is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed with the height: $l=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}=13$ cm. Volume $=\frac13\times\text{base}\times h=\frac13\times100\times12=400$ cm³. Lateral area $=4\times\frac12\times10\times13=260$ cm². Total surface area $=260+100=360$ cm².
In which quadrant does each of $(5,-2)$, $(-4,-6)$ and $(-1,7)$ lie? Model answer: $(5,-2)$ — quadrant IV; $(-4,-6)$ — quadrant III; $(-1,7)$ — quadrant II.

The point $P(-3,4)$ lies in which quadrant? Write its image when reflected in the $y$-axis, the $x$-axis and the origin. Find the distance between $(-3,-2)$ and $(9,3)$. Model answer: (a) $x<0$ and $y>0$: the second quadrant. Reflection in the $y$-axis: $(3,4)$. Reflection in the $x$-axis: $(-3,-4)$. Reflection in the origin: $(3,-4)$.(b) $d=\sqrt{(9-(-3))^2+(3-(-2))^2}=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{144+25}=\sqrt{169}=13$ units.

What is a semi-regular tessellation? Give one example of a vertex arrangement. Model answer: A tessellation using two or more kinds of regular polygon, in the same arrangement at every vertex. Example: 4.8.8, where one square and two octagons meet, $90+135+135=360°$.

Name the transformation that turns one brick in a wall into the next, and the one that makes a mirror pattern. Model answer: One brick to the next is a translation (a glide reflection also occurs in a normal brick wall, because alternate courses are offset). A mirror pattern is a reflection.

A room 4 m long and 3 m wide is to be paved with square tiles of side 25 cm. Find the number of tiles, the number to buy if 5% extra is added for breakage, and the cost at Rs 45 per tile. State the number of lines of sym Model answer: Floor $=400\times300$ cm; along the length $400\div25=16$ tiles and along the width $300\div25=12$ tiles, so $16\times12=192$ tiles. Extra $5\%$ of 192 $=9.6$, so buy $192+9.6=201.6\approx202$ tiles. Cost $=202\times45=\text{Rs }9{,}090$. A square tile has 4 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 4. A regul

A triangle has vertices $A(1,1)$, $B(4,1)$ and $C(1,3)$. (i) Reflect it in the $y$-axis and give the image. (ii) Find the area of both triangles and compare them. Model answer: (i) Reflection in the $y$-axis changes the sign of $x$: $A'(-1,1)$, $B'(-4,1)$, $C'(-1,3)$. (ii) The object has a horizontal side $AB=3$ and a vertical side $AC=2$, so $\text{area}=\frac12\times3\times2=3$ square units. The image has $A'B'=3$ and $A'C'=2$, so its area is also 3 square units. Conclusion. The areas are e

A walker goes 6 km north and then 8 km east. Find his distance and bearing from the start. Model answer: The two legs are at right angles, so distance $=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$ km. From a scale drawing (say 1 cm to 1 km), the protractor gives a bearing of about 053°.

Write the three-figure bearings of north-east, south-west and north-west. The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $070^\circ$: find the bearing of $A$ from $B$. Model answer: (a) North-east $=045^\circ$, south-west $=225^\circ$, north-west $=315^\circ$ (bearings are measured clockwise from north, in three figures).(b) The back bearing is found by adding $180^\circ$ to a bearing below $180^\circ$: $070+180=250^\circ$.(c) The back bearing of $130^\circ$ is $130+180=310^\circ$. (For a bearing

A tree 12 m tall is drawn to the scale 1 cm: 2 m. Find the height in the drawing and write the scale as a ratio. A path measures 7.5 cm on this drawing: find its real length. Model answer: (a) $12\div2=6$ cm. As a ratio: $2\text{ m}=200$ cm, so 1 cm: 200 cm is $1:200$.(b) $7.5\times2=15$ m.(c) $30\text{ m}=3000$ cm, and $3000\div500=6$ cm; $18\text{ m}=1800$ cm, and $1800\div500=3.6$ cm. The drawing is a rectangle 6 cm by 3.6 cm.

A hiker walks 3 km due east and then 4 km due north. Model answer: (a) The two legs form a right angle, so the distance is $\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=\sqrt{25}=5$ km.(b) The finishing point is 3 km east and 4 km north of the start. The angle east of north is found from $\tan\theta=\frac34$, so $\theta\approx36.9^\circ\approx37^\circ$ and the bearing is $037^\circ$.(c) The back bearing is $037+18
Find $x$ and $y$ if $\left(\frac{x}{2}+1,\ y-2\right)=(3,\ x)$. Model answer: First components: $\frac{x}{2}+1=3$, so $x=4$. Second components: $y-2=x=4$, so $y=6$.
If $P=\{a,b,c\}$ and $Q=\{0,1\}$, find $Q\times P$ and $n(P\times Q)$. Model answer: $Q\times P=\{(0,a),(0,b),(0,c),(1,a),(1,b),(1,c)\}$ and $n(P\times Q)=3\times2=6$.
If $f(x)=x^2-4x+3$, find the pre-images of 0 and of 3. Model answer: Pre-images of 0: $x^2-4x+3=0$, $(x-1)(x-3)=0$, so $x=1$ or 3. Pre-images of 3: $x^2-4x=0$, $x(x-4)=0$, so $x=0$ or 4.

State, with reasons, which of these are functions: $R_1=\{(1,1),(2,4),(3,9)\}$; $R_2=\{(4,2),(4,-2),(9,3)\}$; $R_3=\{(x,y): y=3\}$ on $\{1,2,3\}$; the circle $x^2+y^2=4$. Use the vertical line test where it helps. Model answer: $R_1$: a function, each first component appears once. $R_2$: not a function, 4 has two images, 2 and $-2$. $R_3=\{(1,3),(2,3),(3,3)\}$: a function (constant), each input has the one image 3. The circle: not a function, the vertical line $x=0$ meets it at $(0,2)$ and $(0,-2)$.
If $A=\{a,b\}$ and $B=\{1,2,3\}$, find $A\times B$ and $n(A\times B)$. Model answer: $A\times B=\{(a,1),(a,2),(a,3),(b,1),(b,2),(b,3)\}$; $n(A\times B)=2\times3=6$.

If $A=\{2,4\}$ and $B=\{1,3\}$, find $B\times A$ and show that $A\times B\neq B\times A$. Model answer: $B\times A=\{(1,2),(1,4),(3,2),(3,4)\}$ and $A\times B=\{(2,1),(2,3),(4,1),(4,3)\}$. The pair $(1,2)$ is in $B\times A$ but not in $A\times B$, so the sets are not equal.

If $n(A\times B)=6$ and $n(B)=3$, find $n(A)$ and the number of relations from $A$ to $B$. Model answer: $n(A)\times3=6$, so $n(A)=2$. A relation is a subset of $A\times B$, which has 6 members, so there are $2^6=64$ relations.
If $A=\{1,2,3\}$, $B=\{2,3,4,5,6\}$ and $R=\{(x,y): y=2x\}$ from $A$ to $B$, list $R$ and find its domain and range. Model answer: $R=\{(1,2),(2,4),(3,6)\}$; domain $=\{1,2,3\}$; range $=\{2,4,6\}$.
Find the inverse of $R=\{(1,2),(2,4),(3,6)\}$ and state its domain and range. Model answer: $R^{-1}=\{(2,1),(4,2),(6,3)\}$; domain of $R^{-1}=\{2,4,6\}$; range of $R^{-1}=\{1,2,3\}$.
State, with a reason, whether $\{(1,5),(2,6),(2,7),(3,8)\}$ is a function. Model answer: It is not a function, because the first component 2 has two images, 6 and 7.
A function $f: A\rightarrow B$ is defined by $f(x)=x+3$, where $A=\{-1,0,1,2\}$. Find its range. Model answer: $f(-1)=2$, $f(0)=3$, $f(1)=4$, $f(2)=5$, so the range is $\{2,3,4,5\}$.

If $(x+y,\ 3)=(7,\ x-y)$, find $x$ and $y$. Taking $A=\{x,y\}$ and $B=\{1,2\}$, find $A\times B$ and $B\times A$, and verify that $n(A\times B)=n(B\times A)$. Model answer: Equating components: $x+y=7$ and $x-y=3$. Adding, $2x=10$, so $x=5$ and $y=2$. Then $A=\{2,5\}$ and $B=\{1,2\}$. $A\times B=\{(2,1),(2,2),(5,1),(5,2)\}$ and $B\times A=\{(1,2),(1,5),(2,2),(2,5)\}$. Each has 4 members, so $n(A\times B)=n(B\times A)=4=2\times2$, although the two sets are different.

For $f(x)=2x-1$ with domain $\{-1,0,1,2,3\}$: (i) make a table of values, (ii) write $f$ as a set of ordered pairs, (iii) find the range, (iv) plot the points and explain why they pass the vertical line test. Model answer: (i) $x$: $-1, 0, 1, 2, 3$ give $f(x)$: $-3, -1, 1, 3, 5$. (ii) $f=\{(-1,-3),(0,-1),(1,1),(2,3),(3,5)\}$. (iii) Range $=\{-3,-1,1,3,5\}$. (iv) The five points lie on a straight line rising 2 units for every 1 unit to the right. Their $x$-coordinates are all different, so any vertical line passes through at most one of t

Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$ and $B=\{2,4,6,8\}$ and let $R=\{(x,y): y=2x,\ x\in A,\ y\in B\}$. (i) List $R$. (ii) Write its domain, co-domain and range. (iii) Find $R^{-1}$. (iv) Is $R$ a function from $A$ to $B$? Which type? Model answer: (i) $y=2x$ gives $1\to2$, $2\to4$, $3\to6$, so $R=\{(1,2),(2,4),(3,6)\}$. (ii) Domain $=\{1,2,3\}$; co-domain $=B=\{2,4,6,8\}$; range $=\{2,4,6\}$ (8 is in the co-domain but is not an image). (iii) Interchange each pair: $R^{-1}=\{(2,1),(4,2),(6,3)\}$. (iv) Every member of $A$ has exactly one image, so $R$ is a functio

A function is defined by $f(x)=x^2-2x+3$ with domain $\{-1,0,1,2,3\}$. (i) Make a table of values and write the range. (ii) Find the pre-images of 3. (iii) Find $f(a+1)$. (iv) Is $f$ one-to-one? Give a reason. Model answer: (i) $f(-1)=1+2+3=6$; $f(0)=3$; $f(1)=1-2+3=2$; $f(2)=4-4+3=3$; $f(3)=9-6+3=6$. Range $=\{2,3,6\}$. (ii) $f(x)=3$ for $x=0$ and $x=2$, so the pre-images of 3 are 0 and 2. (iii) $f(a+1)=(a+1)^2-2(a+1)+3=a^2+2a+1-2a-2+3=a^2+2$. (iv) $f$ is not one-to-one: $f(0)=f(2)=3$ and $f(-1)=f(3)=6$ (it is many-to-one).
Write the degree, the leading coefficient and the constant term of $3x^2-5+2x^4-x$. Model answer: In standard form $2x^4+3x^2-x-5$: degree 4, leading coefficient 2, constant term $-5$.

State, with a reason, whether each is a polynomial: (i) $3x^2-\sqrt{2}\,x+1$ (ii) $2x+\frac{3}{x}$. Model answer: (i) Yes: the powers of $x$ are 2, 1 and 0; the coefficient $\sqrt{2}$ is allowed. (ii) No: $\frac{3}{x}=3x^{-1}$ has a negative power of $x$.

Let $P(x)=3x^2+2x-5$ and $Q(x)=x^2-4x+7$. Find $P+Q$, $P-Q$ and $2P-3Q$, and state the degree and the number of terms of each result. Model answer: $P+Q=(3+1)x^2+(2-4)x+(-5+7)=4x^2-2x+2$: degree 2, three terms. $P-Q=(3-1)x^2+(2+4)x+(-5-7)=2x^2+6x-12$: degree 2, three terms. $2P-3Q=(6x^2+4x-10)-(3x^2-12x+21)=3x^2+16x-31$: degree 2, three terms.
Write the first four terms of the sequence with $t_n=\frac{2n-1}{n+1}$. Model answer: $t_1=\frac{1}{2}$, $t_2=\frac{3}{3}=1$, $t_3=\frac{5}{4}$, $t_4=\frac{7}{5}$.
Find the general term and the 15th term of $2, 6, 10, 14, \ldots$. Model answer: The difference is 4 and each term is 2 less than $4n$: $t_n=4n-2$, so $t_{15}=58$.
Is 101 a term of $5, 9, 13, \ldots$? If so, which term? Model answer: $t_n=4n+1$. Setting $4n+1=101$ gives $n=25$, a natural number, so 101 is the 25th term.

Find the general term of $0, 3, 8, 15, 24, \ldots$ by the method of differences, find the 10th term, and evaluate the sum of the first four terms written in sigma notation. Model answer: First differences $3, 5, 7, 9$; second differences 2, so compare with $n^2$: the terms are each 1 less, so $t_n=n^2-1$. Then $t_{10}=99$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{4}(k^2-1)=0+3+8+15=26$.

Using $\sum_{k=1}^{n}k=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, find (i) $\sum_{k=1}^{30}k$ (ii) $\sum_{k=1}^{12}(2k+3)$ (iii) the sum of all the multiples of 4 from 4 to 100. Model answer: (i) $\frac{30\times31}{2}=465$. (ii) $2\sum_{k=1}^{12}k+\sum_{k=1}^{12}3=2\times78+36=192$. (iii) $4+8+\cdots+100=4(1+2+\cdots+25)=4\times\frac{25\times26}{2}=4\times325=1300$.
Find the general term of $7, 11, 15, 19, \ldots$. Model answer: The difference is 4. Comparing with $4n$ ($4, 8, 12, 16$), each term is 3 more, so $t_n=4n+3$.

Find the next two terms of $1, 3, 6, 10, 15, \ldots$ and state the rule. Model answer: The differences are $2, 3, 4, 5$, so the next differences are 6 and 7: the next terms are 21 and 28. These are the triangular numbers, $t_n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$.

Is 75 a term of $4, 9, 14, 19, \ldots$? Give a reason. Model answer: $t_n=5n-1$. Setting $5n-1=75$ gives $n=\frac{76}{5}=15.2$, which is not a natural number. So 75 is not a term (the 15th term is 74 and the 16th is 79).

Write $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{16}$ in sigma notation and find its value. Model answer: The $k$th term is $\frac{1}{2^k}$, so the series is $\sum_{k=1}^{4}\frac{1}{2^k}$. Its value is $\frac{8+4+2+1}{16}=\frac{15}{16}$.

Find the general term of $2, 6, 12, 20, 30, \ldots$ by the method of differences, find its 15th term, and find $\sum_{k=1}^{5}t_k$. Then $t_{15}=225+15=240$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{5}t_k=2+6+12+20+30=70$.

The general term of a sequence is $t_n=2^n-1$. (i) Write its first five terms. (ii) Write the series of these five terms in sigma notation and find $S_5$. (iii) Is 255 a term? If so, which one? The general term of a sequence is $t_n=n^2+2n$. Write the first four terms and $t_{10}$. Which term is 143? Is 100 a term of the sequence? For 100: $(n+1)^2=101$, which is not a perfect square, so $n$ is not a whole number and 100 is not a term.

Find the general term of each sequence and use it to write the 8th term: (i) $3,7,11,15,\dots$ (ii) $2,6,18,54,\dots$ (iii) $1,4,9,16,\dots$ (iv) $1,\frac12,\frac13,\frac14,\dots$ Model answer: (i) The common difference is 4 and the first term 3, so $t_n=3+4(n-1)=4n-1$; $t_8=31$. Evaluate (i) $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{5}(2r+1)$ and (ii) $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{4}r^2$. (iii) Write $2+4+6+\dots+20$ in sigma notation and find its sum. Write the next three terms of $\frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{4}, \frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{6}, \ldots$ and state the limit of the sequence. Find the point that divides the join of $(-4,6)$ and $(8,-3)$ internally in the ratio $1:2$. Model answer: $\left(\frac{1(8)+2(-4)}{3},\ \frac{1(-3)+2(6)}{3}\right)=(0,3)$.

Two angles of a triangle are $60^\circ$ and $50^g$. Find the third angle in radians. Model answer: $50^g=45^\circ$, so the third angle is $180^\circ-60^\circ-45^\circ=75^\circ=75\times\frac{\pi}{180}=\frac{5\pi}{12}$ radians.
If $\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}$ and $\theta$ is acute, find $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$. Model answer: $p=5$, $h=13$, $b=\sqrt{169-25}=12$. So $\cos\theta=\frac{12}{13}$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{5}{12}$.

Prove that $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\sec\theta\,\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta$. Model answer: LHS $=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\sec\theta\,\mathrm{cosec}\,\theta=$ RHS.

Find the values of $\sin120^\circ$ and $\cos135^\circ$. Model answer: $\sin120^\circ=\sin(180^\circ-60^\circ)=\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$; $\cos135^\circ=\cos(180^\circ-45^\circ)=-\cos45^\circ=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Find the acute angle $\theta$ if $2\cos\theta=1$. Model answer: $\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}=\cos60^\circ$, so $\theta=60^\circ$.

A ladder 10 m long makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach? Model answer: $\sin60^\circ=\frac{h}{10}$, so $h=10\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=5\sqrt{3}\approx8.66$ m.

Prove that (i) $\frac{1}{1+\sin\theta}+\frac{1}{1-\sin\theta}=2\sec^2\theta$ (ii) $(\sec\theta-\tan\theta)(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)=1$. Model answer: (i) LHS $=\frac{(1-\sin\theta)+(1+\sin\theta)}{(1+\sin\theta)(1-\sin\theta)}=\frac{2}{1-\sin^2\theta}=\frac{2}{\cos^2\theta}=2\sec^2\theta=$ RHS. (ii) LHS $=\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta$ (difference of two squares) $=1=$ RHS, using $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta$.

Find the magnitude and direction of $\binom{-3}{3}$. Model answer: Magnitude $\sqrt{9+9}=3\sqrt{2}$. $x<0$, $y>0$: quadrant II, with acute angle $45^\circ$, so the direction is $180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$.

Find $m$ if $\binom{m}{-6}$ and $\binom{2}{-3}$ are parallel. Are they like or unlike? Model answer: $\binom{m}{-6}=k\binom{2}{-3}$ needs $k=2$, so $m=4$. The scalar is positive, so they are like vectors.
Find the unit vector in the direction of $\binom{5}{12}$. Model answer: $|\vec{a}|=13$, so $\hat{a}=\binom{\frac{5}{13}}{\frac{12}{13}}$.

If $\vec{a}=\binom{3}{4}$ and $\vec{b}=\binom{-2}{1}$, find $|\vec{a}|$, $|\vec{b}|$, $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$ and $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|$, and show that $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|<|\vec{a}|+|\vec{b}|$. Write two differences between scalar and vector quantities, with one example of each. Model answer: A scalar has magnitude only, a vector has magnitude and direction; two scalars are added as ordinary numbers, but vectors are added by the triangle law (by components). Examples: mass 5 kg (scalar); a force of 10 N upwards (vector).
Find the magnitude and direction of $\vec{a}=\binom{2}{2}$. Model answer: $|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{4+4}=2\sqrt{2}$. Both components are positive and $\tan\theta=\frac{2}{2}=1$, so $\theta=45^\circ$.
Find the unit vector in the direction of $\binom{3}{-4}$. Model answer: $|\vec{a}|=5$, so $\hat{a}=\binom{\frac{3}{5}}{-\frac{4}{5}}$.
If $\vec{a}=\binom{2}{-1}$, find $3\vec{a}$, $-2\vec{a}$ and $|3\vec{a}|$. Model answer: $3\vec{a}=\binom{6}{-3}$, $-2\vec{a}=\binom{-4}{2}$, and $|3\vec{a}|=3\sqrt{5}$ (since $|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{5}$).

Show that $\binom{2}{-3}$ and $\binom{-4}{6}$ are parallel, and say whether they are like or unlike. Model answer: $\binom{-4}{6}=-2\binom{2}{-3}$: parallel, and unlike because the scalar $-2$ is negative.
If $\vec{a}=\binom{3}{1}$ and $\vec{b}=\binom{1}{2}$, find $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$ and $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|$. Model answer: $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\binom{4}{3}$ and $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|=\sqrt{16+9}=5$.

A translation sends $(3,-2)$ to $(-1,4)$. Find the translation vector and the image of the origin. Model answer: $\binom{-1-3}{4+2}=\binom{-4}{6}$; the origin goes to $(-4,6)$.

For the point $(4,7)$, show that rotation through $180^\circ$ about $O$ gives the same image as reflection in the $x$-axis followed by reflection in the $y$-axis. Model answer: $180^\circ$: $(-4,-7)$. Reflections: $(4,7)\rightarrow(4,-7)\rightarrow(-4,-7)$. The same image.

The triangle $A(2,1)$, $B(4,1)$, $C(4,3)$ is rotated through $-90^\circ$ about the origin and the image is then translated by $\binom{-1}{2}$. Find the final image. Model answer: $-90^\circ$, $(x,y)\rightarrow(y,-x)$: $A'(1,-2)$, $B'(1,-4)$, $C'(3,-4)$. Translating by $\binom{-1}{2}$: $A''(0,0)$, $B''(0,-2)$, $C''(2,-2)$.

Define isometric and non-isometric transformations, with one example of each. Model answer: An isometric transformation keeps the distance between every two points, so the image is congruent to the object; example: rotation. A non-isometric transformation changes distances, so the image differs in size; example: enlargement with scale factor 2.
Find the image of the triangle $A(1,2)$, $B(3,5)$, $C(4,1)$ after reflection in the $x$-axis. Model answer: $(x,y)\rightarrow(x,-y)$: $A'(1,-2)$, $B'(3,-5)$, $C'(4,-1)$.

A rotation about the origin maps $P(5,-1)$ to $P'(1,5)$. Find the angle and direction of the rotation. Model answer: For $P(5,-1)$, $(-y,x)=(1,5)$, which is the image. So it is a rotation through $+90^\circ$, anticlockwise.

Find the image of $(-2,-5)$ under rotation through $180^\circ$ about the origin, and show that the same image comes from reflection in the $x$-axis followed by reflection in the $y$-axis. Model answer: $180^\circ$: $(2,5)$. In the $x$-axis: $(-2,5)$; then in the $y$-axis: $(2,5)$. The same image.

Show that reflection in the $y$-axis keeps the length of $AB$, where $A(1,3)$ and $B(4,7)$. Model answer: $AB=\sqrt{9+16}=5$. The images are $A'(-1,3)$ and $B'(-4,7)$, and $A'B'=\sqrt{(-4+1)^2+(7-3)^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5$. The length is unchanged.

Find $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$ and the distance $PP_3$. Model answer: $P_1=(-3,2)$; $P_2=(-2,-3)$ (applying $(-y,x)$); $P_3=(-1,-7)$. $PP_3=\sqrt{4^2+9^2}=\sqrt{97}\approx9.85$ units.

The mean of 8 numbers is 20. If the number 34 is removed, find the mean of the remaining numbers. Model answer: The total was $8\times20=160$; without 34 it is 126, shared by 7 numbers: $\frac{126}{7}=18$.
Find the range and the coefficient of range for the classes 20–30, 30–40, 40–50, 50–60. Model answer: $L=60$, $S=20$: range $=40$, coefficient $=\frac{40}{80}=0.5$.

(ii) Kathmandu: $\frac{176}{7}\approx25.14$°C; Jumla: $\frac{122}{7}\approx17.43$°C. (iii) Jumla, because both its range and its coefficient of range are larger.

Distinguish between Model answer: (a) Observation is studying an object or event carefully with the sense organs (or instruments) without changing it; it gives information and leads to a guess. A test is a fixed scientific procedure to check whether that guess (hypothesis) is true, e.g. dipping litmus in lemon juice. (b) Research is an in-depth study o

What is observation? Why is it important in scientific work? Model answer: Observation is the process of experiencing an object, event or process very carefully using the sense organs. It is important because it gives the first information about a thing, helps us make hypotheses and records the results of tests and experiments.

What is done in scientific work when observation does not give enough information? Model answer: A hypothesis is made from the observation, and a test or experiment is carried out to check it. Instruments such as a hand lens or microscope may also be used to observe more closely.

What precautions should be taken while carrying out a scientific experiment? Model answer: Follow the given method; wear an apron, gloves and goggles; never taste or directly smell chemicals; use a test-tube holder and point the tube away from people; take care with burners and hot objects; do reactions that give fumes in a fume hood; keep hot apparatus off the bare table; wash hands afterwards.

List the things that should be done and should not be done in the laboratory. Model answer: Do: wear a lab coat, follow instructions, know the emergency exit, use holders and tongs, keep the bench clean, wash hands after work. Do not: eat or drink, taste or smell chemicals, play or tease, handle materials carelessly, put hot apparatus directly on the table.

What should we pay attention to while doing research? Model answer: Have a clear question and objective; follow the steps in order; collect data honestly; keep a control for comparison; repeat if it fails and improve the method; be patient; write a report and name the sources used.

In what conditions is a survey conducted? What are survey tools? Give examples. Model answer: A survey is done when the information is spread among many people, households or places (e.g. waste management in a community, use of fertiliser by farmers) and must be collected directly. Survey tools are the means of collecting data: questionnaire, interview, group discussion and observation.

Objective: to observe and draw an onion-peel cell and a human cheek cell. Materials: onion, clean toothpick, slides, cover slips, iodine or methylene blue, water, forceps, needle, microscope. Steps: (i) Peel a thin layer from the inside of an onion scale, place it in a drop of wa

(a) A scanner is an input device that changes a hard copy into a soft copy; a printer is an output device that changes a soft copy into a hard copy. (b) A search engine is a program that finds pages on many websites by keyword (Google); a website is a collection of web pages with its ow

Differentiate between Model answer: (a) VR creates an artificial 3-D world that a person experiences through a headset; AI makes a machine think, learn and decide like a human. (b) The code of conduct is a set of moral guidelines for using computers, without legal punishment; cyber law is the law of the state, and breaking it is punished by jail or fine.

What kind of technology is an ATM? Write its important functions. Model answer: An ATM is an electromechanical (computer-based) banking technology. Functions: withdraw and deposit cash, check balance, give a mini statement, pay bills, transfer funds, change PIN.

List the main parts of a photocopy machine. Model answer: Glass plate (platen) and cover, light source and lens, light-sensitive drum with electrostatic charge, toner, fuser (heat and pressure), paper tray, control panel with Start button, output tray.

What is a printer? Mention its function. Model answer: A printer is an output device that produces a hard copy of a digital file. It prints text and pictures in black and white or colour; types are dot-matrix, ink-jet and laser.

What is a search engine? Explain the need for search engines with an example. Model answer: A search engine is a software system that finds information on the internet by keywords. It is needed because we often do not know the website address; e.g. typing "Curriculum Development Centre" in Google gives the link www.moecdc.gov.np, saving time.
Write the main features of an ISP. Model answer: High-speed internet; e-mail addresses; protection from phishing and malware; web hosting; charges according to the data package.

Mention the opportunities and benefits of social media. Model answer: A strong medium of expression and discussion; quick news and notices; brand development and advertising for businesses; customer feedback; learning (e.g. NCED Virtual on YouTube); keeping in touch with family abroad.

Write the full forms: ATM, WWW, URL, Wi-Fi, ISP, AI, VR. Model answer: Automated Teller Machine; World Wide Web; Uniform Resource Locator; Wireless Fidelity; Internet Service Provider; Artificial Intelligence; Virtual Reality.

Mention the dangers to internet security and the ways to avoid them. Model answer: Dangers: malware (viruses, worms, Trojan horses, spyware); phishing by false messages; identity theft; hacking; botnets. Ways to avoid: strong and different passwords; two-factor authentication; update software; use antivirus and a firewall; back up data; do not open unknown links or attachments; never share PIN or OTP

What is artificial intelligence? What is its main objective? Write any four fields where AI is used. Model answer: AI is the making of programs or machines that can do tasks needing human intelligence — understanding language, recognising objects, deciding and solving problems. Its main objective is to make machines that think and learn like humans so that work becomes faster and more accurate. Fields: health care (diagnosis), agri

What is robotics? Mention some important tasks done by robots. Model answer: Robotics is the branch of computer science and engineering dealing with the design, construction, operation and use of robots. Tasks: welding, painting and assembling in factories; helping in surgery; planting and harvesting; packing and sorting goods; exploring space and the deep sea; defusing bombs and rescue work.

What is virtual reality? Write the sectors in which it is used. Model answer: VR is a computer-made 3-D imitation of an environment that a user experiences through a headset and sensors as if it were real. Sectors: military training and PTSD therapy, education (virtual field trips), sports training and broadcasting, mental health (anxiety, phobia), medical surgery training, fashion, architecture

What is cloud computing? Write two services and two advantages of cloud computing. Model answer: Cloud computing is using remote servers on the internet to store, manage and process data and programs instead of a local computer. Services: online file storage (e.g. Google Drive), e-mail, web hosting, running software online. Advantages: low cost (pay only for use); access from anywhere; reliable backup; strong secu

Where are mitochondria found in a cell? Write their functions. Model answer: In the cytoplasm of both plant and animal cells. Functions: oxidise glucose with oxygen to release energy stored as ATP (power house); contain DNA that passes on some hereditary characters.

Which organelle digests itself, and why? Model answer: The lysosome. It is full of digestive enzymes; when the enzyme level becomes very high, or the cell is old or damaged, the membrane breaks and the enzymes digest the cell itself — so it is called the suicidal bag.

Write the role of the Golgi body and the vacuole. Model answer: Golgi body: secretes mucus, saliva, sweat and tears; sorts and packs proteins; helps form the new membrane or cell plate in division. Vacuole: stores cell sap, balances water and salts, and collects wastes before they are removed.

Why is the nucleus called the brain of the cell? What happens if a cell has no nucleus? Model answer: It controls and coordinates all activities of the cell and carries the hereditary material. Without a nucleus the cell cannot divide or control its work, and soon dies (e.g. mature red blood cells live only about 120 days).

What is food poisoning? Write its causes and prevention. Model answer: Illness from eating food spoiled by microbes or their toxins. Causes: stale, uncovered or undercooked food; dirty hands or utensils; germs like Salmonella, Clostridium, norovirus. Prevention: eat fresh, well-cooked, covered food; wash hands; keep food cold; avoid smelly food.
How is amoeba useful to people? Model answer: Amoeba proteus eats bacteria, so it is used to control bacteria (e.g. in cleaning waste water).

Write the functions of the three kinds of plastids in a plant cell. What would happen to a plant with no chloroplasts? Model answer: Chloroplast: makes food by photosynthesis, gives green colour, helps make fatty acids and amino acids. Chromoplast: gives colour to flowers and fruits to attract insects and birds for pollination and seed dispersal. Leucoplast: stores starch, protein and fat. Without chloroplasts the plant could not make food, so it wo

Write the merits and drawbacks of the two-kingdom system, and explain how the five-kingdom system corrected them. Model answer: Merits: first scientific system; simple; easy to tell plants from animals. Drawbacks: fungi put with plants; prokaryotic bacteria and eukaryotic algae put together; unicellular and multicellular not separated; lichens and Euglena had no place. Correction: Whittaker's five-kingdom system put prokaryotes in Monera, unice

What are the methods of food preservation? Describe one, and write the importance of food preservation. Why does fungus grow in a pickle jar, and how can it be stopped? Model answer: Dry, wet and cold preservation (table in 3.5). Wet preservation: the food is washed or boiled, dried, then kept in strong salt solution, lemon juice, vinegar or mustard oil in an airtight jar; e.g. lemon pickle. Importance: food lasts longer, nutrients are kept, seasonal food is available all year, loss to farmers is r

What is a microorganism? Give one example from each group, write four advantages of microorganisms, and name two diseases caused by each group. Model answer: Microorganisms are living beings too small to see without a microscope. Examples: virus — coronavirus; bacteria — Rhizobium; protozoa — Amoeba; fungi — yeast; algae — Chlamydomonas. Advantages: decomposition and soil fertility; nitrogen fixation; curd and cheese; antibiotics and vaccines; fermentation (bread, jaand). D

What is biodiversity? Give examples. What is the role of species richness? Model answer: Biodiversity is the variety of living beings in different habitats, including variety within species, between species and between ecosystems; e.g. rhinos and tigers in Chitwan, rhododendrons in the hills, yaks in the Himalaya. Species richness (many species) keeps food webs complex and the ecosystem stable and producti

Explain the present status of biodiversity in Nepal. Model answer: Nepal has 0.1 % of the world's land but about 3.2 % of plant and 1.1 % of animal species, more than 118 ecosystems and 15 forest types; it ranks about 27th in the world. Endemic spiny babbler, rare rhino, tiger and wild yak, 32 rhododendron species and Marshi rice of Jumla show its richness.

What is sustainable development? Give an example. Model answer: Development that meets present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs; e.g. building a road with drains, retaining walls and slope planting so that it lasts for many years.

Write a food chain of four links and say what happens to it if the frog is removed. Model answer: Grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. If frogs are removed, grasshoppers increase and damage the grass and crops, while snakes lose food and decline or move away.

What are the methods of conserving biodiversity? Explain one, and write other measures of conservation. Model answer: In-situ and ex-situ conservation. In-situ: organisms are protected in their natural habitat, e.g. national parks (Chitwan), wildlife reserve (Koshi Tappu), hunting reserve (Dhorpatan) and conservation areas (Annapurna); it is natural and cheap and protects all species, but poaching and fire are hard to control. Explain the causes of degradation of biodiversity in points. Model answer: Any eight from the list in 4.2, each with a short reason (e.g. overgrazing destroys seedlings; invasive banmara displaces native plants).

What are the principles of sustainable development? Describe any one. Model answer: Ecosystem and biodiversity conservation; population control and human resource management; cultural conservation and public participation. Public participation: when people take part in a project and their culture is respected, they own and protect it — e.g. a village-built irrigation canal is maintained by the village

What are the SDGs? Illustrate Nepal's efforts to achieve them. Model answer: SDGs are 17 global goals with 169 targets and 232 indicators, adopted by 193 UN members in 2015 for 2016–2030. Nepal's efforts: Climate Change Council and cabinet meeting at Kalapatthar (2009); lowering Tsho Rolpa; community forests; periodic plans for poverty reduction, education and employment; National Environment P

Name the method of asexual reproduction: yeast, paramecium, pineapple, banana, planaria, begonia, ginger, onion, sugarcane, Mucor, sweet potato, Spirogyra. Model answer: Yeast — budding; paramecium — binary fission; pineapple — bulbils (and suckers); banana — sucker; planaria — regeneration; begonia — leaf; ginger — rhizome; onion — bulb; sugarcane — stem cutting (aerial stem); Mucor — sporulation (and fragmentation); sweet potato — root; Spirogyra — fragmentation.

What are stock and scion? Write two advantages of grafting. Model answer: The stock is the lower rooted part (a young seedling); the scion is the twig of a good-quality plant joined on it. Advantages: early fruiting; fruit of the desired quality; combines a hardy root with a productive shoot.

What is gametogenesis? Where does it occur in plants and animals? Model answer: Gametogenesis is the formation of gametes. In plants it occurs in the anther (pollen, male gametes) and ovule (egg); in animals in the testes (sperms) and ovaries (ova).

Compare self-pollination and cross-pollination with their advantages and disadvantages. Model answer: Self: pollen to the same flower or same plant; small dull flowers; no agent needed; seed setting is sure and parent characters are kept, but no new variety and vigour falls. What is double fertilisation? Describe the process. Model answer: Two fusions in the ovule of a flowering plant. The pollen grain forms a pollen tube that grows through the style to the ovule; its nucleus forms two male gametes; one fuses with the egg to form the zygote (→ embryo) and the other fuses with the secondary nucleus to form the endosperm nucleus (→ endosperm). Write the methods of seed dispersal and explain any one with examples. Name the method for mango, chestnut, maple, gram, cobbler's pegs, sesame, pumpkin, coconut and pear. Model answer: Wind, water, animals, gravity and bursting of pods (table in 5.4.2). Mango — gravity (and animals); chestnut — bursting/gravity; maple — wind; gram — bursting of pods; cobbler's pegs — animals (sticking); sesame — bursting of pods; pumpkin — animals/people; coconut — water; pear — animals.

Define reference point, relative velocity and retardation. Model answer: A reference point is a fixed point, line or place with which the position of a body is compared. Relative velocity is the velocity of a body with respect to another body. Retardation is the rate of decrease of velocity (negative acceleration).

Which class of lever is a pair of scissors? What can a lever with MA more than 1 do? Write other advantages of a lever besides making work easy. Model answer: First class (the pivot is between blade and handle). A lever with MA > 1 lifts a load larger than the effort (multiplies force). Other advantages: changes the direction of the force, increases speed or distance of movement (third class), and allows work at a convenient place (tongs keep hands away from fire).

How can we show that a liquid exerts pressure? Write two applications of liquid pressure. Model answer: Make holes at different heights in a bottle full of water; water comes out from all holes (pressure acts sideways) and spurts farthest from the lowest hole (pressure increases with depth). Applications: dams thick at the bottom; tanks kept high; divers' suits.

What is atmospheric pressure? Write two uses of it. Model answer: The pressure exerted by the weight of air on unit area of the earth's surface (760 mmHg at sea level). Uses: drinking with a straw, filling a syringe or fountain pen, pumping tyres.
A bus covers 4.2 km in 7 minutes. Find its average velocity. Model answer: $s=4.2$ km $=4200$ m, $t=7$ min $=420$ s. $\bar{v}=\frac{4200}{420}=10$ m/s.

A car starts from rest with an acceleration of 5 m/s² for 6 s. Find its final velocity and average velocity. Model answer: $v=u+at=0+5\times6=30$ m/s. Average velocity $=\frac{u+v}{2}=\frac{0+30}{2}=15$ m/s. (The answer printed in the textbook, 15 m/s and 7.5 m/s, would be correct only for an acceleration of 2.5 m/s²; with 5 m/s² the correct values are 30 m/s and 15 m/s.)
Two motorcycles move at 50 km/h and 60 km/h. Find their relative velocity in the same and opposite directions. Model answer: Same direction: $60-50=10$ km/h. Opposite directions: $60+50=110$ km/h.

An effort of 300 N lifts a load of 900 N with a 2 m first-class lever; the load is 50 cm from the fulcrum and the effort is at the other end. Find MA, VR and efficiency. Model answer: $L.D.=0.5$ m, $E.D.=2-0.5=1.5$ m. $MA=\frac{900}{300}=3$; $VR=\frac{1.5}{0.5}=3$; $\eta=\frac{3}{3}\times100\%=100\%$ (an ideal lever, friction neglected).

What is convection? How does wind blow? Write two applications of convection. Model answer: Transfer of heat in liquids and gases by the movement of heated particles. Wind: the sun heats the ground; the air above becomes warm and light and rises; cooler air from nearby flows in to take its place — this moving air is wind. Why does the speed of sound stay the same when frequency changes? Why does sound become fainter as we move away from the source? Model answer: The speed depends only on the medium; since $v=f\lambda$ is fixed, a higher frequency gives a proportionally shorter wavelength. The energy spreads over a larger area and part is absorbed by the air, so intensity falls with distance.

Wind insulated wire round an iron nail and connect it to a cell through a switch: the nail attracts pins only while current flows — current produces magnetism.
